question: How many years did Jeroboam reign before he slept with his fathers?
answer: Jeroboam reigned for 22 years, and he slept with his fathers.

question: Who was reigning in Judah?
answer: Rehoboam the son of Solomon was reigning in Judah.

question: How did Judah provoke Yahweh to jealousy?
answer: Judah provoked Yahweh to jealousy with the sins they committed.

question: What did Judah build on every high hill and under every green tree?
answer: Judah built shrines and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

question: What despicable things did the nations do?
answer: The Israelite people did the same disgraceful things with male prostitutes that the people had done whom Yahweh had forced to leave so that the Israelites could possess the land.

question: In what year did Shishak come up against Jerusalem?
answer: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak came up against Jerusalem.

question: What shields did Shishak take away from Jerusalem?
answer: Shishak took all the shields of gold that Solomon had made.

question: What did King Rehoboam do with the shields of bronze that he made?
answer: King Rehoboam put them into the hands of the palace guards.

question: When would the guards carry the shields of bronze?
answer: Whenever the king entered the house of Yahweh, the guards would carry the shields.

question: Where were the other matters of King Rehoboam written?
answer: The other matters of King Rehoboam were written in book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah.

question: Who became king in Rehoboam’s place?
answer: Abijah, Rehoboam’s son, became king in his place.

question: When did Abijah begin to reign over Judah?
answer: Abijah began to reign over Judah in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam.

question: How long did Abijah rule in Jerusalem?
answer: Abijah ruled in Jerusalem for three years.

question: Was Abijah’s heart devoted to Yahweh his God?
answer: Abijah’s heart was not devoted to Yahweh his God.

question: Why did Yahweh raise up a son for Abijah in Jerusalem?
answer: Yahweh raised up a son for Abijah for the sake of David.

question: In what matter did David turn away from Yahweh?
answer: David only turned away from Yahweh in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

question: What happened all the days of Abijah’s life?
answer: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of Abijah’s life.

question: When Abijah slept with his fathers, who became king in his place?
answer: When Abijah slept with his fathers, Asa became king in his place.

question: When did Asa begin to reign over Judah?
answer: Asa began to reign over Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel.

question: How many years did Asa reign in Jerusalem?
answer: Asa reigned 41 years in Jerusalem.

question: What did Asa do in the eyes of Yahweh?
answer: Asa did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh, as David had done.

question: What did Asa do in the land?
answer: Asa removed the male prostitutes and the idols his ancestors had made in the land.

question: Whom did Asa remove from being queen?
answer: Asa removed his own grandmother Maacah from being queen.

question: What was the condition of Asa’s heart toward Yahweh?
answer: Asa’s heart was completely dedicated to Yahweh all his days.

question: What did Asa bring into the house of Yahweh?
answer: Asa brought all the items that his father had dedicated to God and all the gold and silver things that he had dedicated to God into the house of Yahweh.

question: With whom was Asa at war?
answer: Asa was at war with Baasha king of Israel all their days.

question: Why did Baasha build up Ramah?
answer: Baasha built up Ramah so that no one would enter into or leave the area that King Asa ruled.

question: What did Asa do with all the silver and gold from the storerooms of the house of Yahweh?
answer: Asa sent the silver and gold to Ben Hadad, the grandson of the king of Aram, who lived in Damascus.

question: What did Asa say to Benhadad?
answer: Asa said to Benhadad, “Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father.”

question: What did Benhadad do after he listened to Asa?
answer: After he listened to Asa, Benhadad sent his armies to attack the cities of Israel.

question: What did Baasha do when he heard about this?
answer: When Baasha heard about the attacks, he stopped building up Ramah.

question: What did Asa do with the materials that had been used to build up Ramah?
answer: Asa took the materials that had been used to build up Ramah and used them to build up Geba and Mizpah.

question: Where were all of Asa’s matters written?
answer: All of Asa’s matters were written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah.

question: After Asa slept with his fathers, who became king in his place?
answer: After Asa slept with his fathers, his son Jehoshaphat became king in his place.

question: Who began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa?
answer: Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa.

question: How did Nadab walk in the sight of Yahweh?
answer: Nadab did evil in the sight of Yahweh and walked in the ways of his father and in his sin.

question: What did Baasha son of Ahijah do at Gibbethon?
answer: Baasha the son of Ahijah killed Nadab at Gibbethon.

question: What did Baasha do as soon as he became king?
answer: As soon as Baasha became king, he killed all of the family of Jeroboam. He did not leave one of Jeroboam’s descendants breathing.

question: How long was there war between Asa and Baasha?
answer: There was war between Asa and Baasha all their days.

question: How long did Baasha reign in Tirza?
answer: Baasha reigned in Tirza for 24 years.

question: How did Baasha live?
answer: Baasha did evil in the sight of Yahweh and lived in the way of Jeroboam. encouraging his people to sin in the same way that he sinned.

question: Out of what did Yahweh raise Baasha?
answer: Yahweh raised him out of the dust.

question: What would eat anyone belonging to Baasha who died in the city?
answer: The dogs would eat anyone belonging to Baasha who died in the city.

question: Why did the word of Yahweh come against Baasha and his family?
answer: The word of Yahweh came against Baasha and his family both because of all the evil he did in the sight of Yahweh and also because he had killed all of Jeroboam’s family.

question: What was Elah doing when Zimri killed him?
answer: Elah was drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza when Zimri killed him.

question: When did Zimri kill all the family of Baasha?
answer: When Zimri began to reign, as soon as he had sat on his throne, he killed all the family of Baasha.

question: To whom did Gibbethon belong?
answer: Gibbethon belonged to the Philistines.

question: Where did Zimri kill himself?
answer: Zimri killed himself in the citadel attached to the king’s palace, burning it down over himself and dying in the fire.

question: About what two leaders were the people of Israel divided into two parts?
answer: The people of Israel divided into two parts about who should be their king, Tibni or Omri.

question: Why did Omri call the name of the city Samaria?
answer: Omri called the name of the city Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill.

question: Who became king in Omri’s place?
answer: Ahab his son became king in his place.

question: Who had built the house of Baal in Samaria?
answer: Ahab had built the house of Baal in Samaria.

question: What caused the loss of Hiel’s son Abiram?
answer: Hiel began rebuilding Jericho, causing the loss of his oldest son, Abiram.

question: What ominous message did Elijah give to Ahab?
answer: Elijah told Ahab that as Yahweh lives, there would be no dew or rain unless he said so.

question: Who did Yahweh command to feed Elijah while Elijah was at the brook Cherith?
answer: Yahweh commanded the ravens to feed Elijah at the brook Cherith.

question: What happened when there was no rain in the land?
answer: The brook dried up when there was no rain in the land.

question: Where did Elijah go after the brook dried up?
answer: Yahweh sent Elijah to a widow in Zarephath.

question: Why was the widow gathering two sticks?
answer: The widow was gathering two sticks so she could go in and cook for herself and her son, that they could eat, and die from hunger.

question: For how long would the widow’s jar of meal and jug of oil be full?
answer: They would be full until the day that Yahweh sent rain on the earth.

question: How sick was the woman’s son?
answer: The son’s sickness was so severe that there was no more breath left in him.

question: What did Elijah do to save the child?
answer: Elijah stretched himself on the child three times; he cried out to Yahweh and said, “Yahweh my God, please let this child become alive again.”

question: How did the woman know that Elijah was a man of God?
answer: The woman knew that Elijah was a man of God when her son revived, and Elijah took the child and gave him to his mother.

question: What message did Yahweh ask Elijah to give to Ahab during the severe famine?
answer: Yahweh asked Elijah to tell Ahab he would send rain on the land.

question: How did Obadiah honor Yahweh when Jezebel was killing the prophets of Yahweh?
answer: Obadiah honored Yahweh by hiding 100 prophets by fifties in a cave and feeding them with bread and water.

question: Why did Ahab and Obadiah go through the land to all the water springs and brooks?
answer: Ahab and Obadiah were searching for water and grass so they could keep a horse or a mule alive.

question: What dangerous message did Elijah ask Obadiah to tell Ahab?
answer: Elijah asked Obadiah to tell Ahab that Elijah is here.

question: Why was Obadiah reluctant to tell Ahab that “Elijah is here.”?
answer: Obadiah was reluctant to tell Ahab, “Elijah is here,” because all the nearby nations had taken an oath swearing that Elijah was not there.

question: What did Obadiah think would happen as soon as he left Elijah?
answer: Obadiah thought the Spirit of Yahweh would carry Elijah some place Obadiah would not know.

question: What did Elijah tell Obadiah to calm his fears?
answer: Elijah told Obadiah that as Yahweh lives, he would surely show himself to Ahab that day.

question: What did Ahab call Elijah when he met him?
answer: Ahab called Elijah “one troubling Israel” when he met him.

question: How did Elijah respond to Ahab calling him a “troublemaker”?
answer: Elijah told the king that Ahab and his father’s family were the troublemakers because they abandoned the commandments of Yahweh to follow the Baals.

question: Who did Elijah say to gather on Mount Carmel?
answer: Elijah said to gather all the people of Israel, along with the 450 prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel’s table.

question: Who did Elijah tell the people they should follow?
answer: Elijah told the people to follow Yahweh if he was God or follow Baal if he was truly God.

question: What proposal did Elijah bring before the people?
answer: Elijah proposed that he and the prophets of Baal each call upon their god to consume the sacrifice of a bull by fire to prove which one was God.

question: How long did the prophets of Baal call on Baal?
answer: The prophets of Baal called on Baal from morning until noon.

question: After Elijah mocked the prophets of Baal at noon, what did the prophets of Baal do?
answer: The prophets of Baal cried more loudly and cut themselves with swords and spears.

question: How long did the prophets of Baal continue their raving?
answer: The prophets of Baal were raving until the time of the evening sacrifice.

question: What did Elijah do to the ruined altar of Yahweh?
answer: Elijah repaired the altar of Yahweh with twelve stones.

question: What did Elijah make around the altar of Yahweh?
answer: Elijah dug a trench around the altar of Yahweh.

question: What did Elijah have the people do to the wood and the bull for the burnt offering?
answer: Three times Elijah had the people fill four jars with water and pour them on the burnt offering and the wood.

question: How did the people of Israel respond when the fire of Yahweh fell and consumed the sacrifice and everything around it?
answer: The people lay face down on the ground and said, “Yahweh, he is God! Yahweh, he is God!”

question: What did Elijah do with the prophets of Baal?
answer: Elijah brought the prophets of Baal down to the brook of Kishon and killed them.

question: What did the servant of Elijah see after he looked toward the sea seven times?
answer: On the seventh time, the servant saw a cloud as small as a man’s hand.

question: What did Elijah tell his servant to say to Ahab?
answer: Elijah told his servant to tell Ahab to make ready his chariot and go down so the rain would not stop him.

question: What did Elijah do as Ahab rode and went to Jezreel?
answer: Elijah tucked his robe in his belt and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

question: What threat did Jezebel make to Elijah?
answer: Jezebel told Elijah that by the next day she would have killed him, just like he killed all those prophets of Baal.

question: How did Elijah respond to the threat from Jezebel?
answer: Elijah fled for his life to Beersheba.

question: Why did Elijah request that he might die?
answer: Elijah requested that he might die because he felt he was no better than his dead ancestors.

question: What happened as Elijah was sleeping under a juniper tree?
answer: An angel touched Elijah and said to him, “Get up and eat.”

question: What did Elijah see and do after the angel touched him?
answer: Elijah saw bread that had been baked on coals and a jug of water. Elijah ate and drank, and then he lay down again.

question: How long did it take Elijah to get to Horeb, the mountain of God?
answer: Elijah traveled 40 days and 40 nights to Horeb.

question: How did Elijah respond when Yahweh asked him what he was doing in a cave?
answer: Elijah told Yahweh that he had been very zealous for him, but the people of Israel had forsaken his covenant, destroyed his altars, and killed his prophets, and he was the only one left, and they sought to kill him too.

question: What did Yahweh tell Elijah to do?
answer: Yahweh told Elijah to return to the wilderness near Damascus to anoint Hazael to be king over Aram, Jehu to be king over Israel, and Elisha to be a prophet in his place.

question: How did Yahweh respond to Elijah’s claim that he was the only prophet left in the land?
answer: Yahweh told Elijah there were 7,000 people in Israel who never worshiped Baal.

question: What excuse did Elisha give to Elijah after he draped his cloak on him?
answer: Elisha asked Elijah to let him kiss his mother and father before he followed him.

question: What was the message which Ahab received from Ben Hadad when the city of Samaria was under siege?
answer: Ben Hadad told Ahab that his silver and gold as well as his wives and children were now Ben Hadad’s possessions.

question: How did Ben Hadad respond to Ahab’s willingness to give him his silver, gold, wives, and children?
answer: Ben Hadad informed Ahab that he was sending his servants the next day, and they would seize with their hands anything valuable of Ahab’s and bring it to him.

question: What was the advice which the king of Israel received from all the elders of the land and the people?
answer: The elders of the land and the people told the king not to listen or consent to the demands of Ben Hadad.

question: What was the message Ahab sent back to Ben Hadad?
answer: Ahab told Ben Hadad that he was agreeable to his first demand, but he could not accept his second demand.

question: What was the response of Ben Hadad to the message of Ahab?
answer: Ben Hadad took an oath that he would reduce Samaria less than a handful of ashes.

question: What did Ben Hadad say when the king of Israel told him that he should not boast as if the battle were over?
answer: Ben Hadad told his soldiers to prepare to attack the city.

question: Who did Yahweh say would win the battle for Israel against the great army of the Arameans?
answer: Yahweh told Ahab that the 232 young soldiers commanded by the district governors would win the battle for Israel.

question: When the young soldiers advanced first, what were Ben Hadad and the 32 lesser kings who were supporting him doing?
answer: Ben Hadad and his 32 lesser kings were drinking themselves drunk.

question: What happened to Ben Hadad and the Arameans?
answer: Ben Hadad escaped on a horse with some horsemen, and many of the Arameans were killed in a great slaughter.

question: What message did the prophet bring to the king of Israel?
answer: The prophet told the king of Israel that the king of Aram would return against them again, so Israel should strengthen itself and think carefully and prepare for what they would do.

question: What did the servants of the king of Aram give as the reason for Israel being stronger in battle than the Arameans?
answer: The servants of the king of Aram told him Israel was stronger than the Arameans, since their god is a god of the hills.

question: What did Ben Hadad do after the beginning of the new year?
answer: Ben Hadad mustered the Arameans and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.

question: What did a man of God say to the king of Israel concerning the Arameans?
answer: The man of God said that because the Arameans said God was a god of the hills and not a god of the valleys, God was going to place the Aramean army into the hands of the king of Israel in the valley.

question: What was the outcome of the battle between the armies?
answer: Israel killed 100,000 Aramean footmen in one day. The rest fled to Aphek, into the city where a wall fell on 27,000 men who were left, and Ben Hadad fled into the city, into an inner room.

question: What did Ben Hadad’s servants do for Ben Hadad?
answer: Ben Hadad’s servants put sackcloth on their waists and ropes around their heads and went to the king of Israel and begged the king of Israel to let Ben Hadad live.

question: What proposal did Ben Hadad make to Ahab when he was summoned to meet with him in his chariot?
answer: Ben Hadad told Ahab that he would restore to him the cities which had been taken from Israel if Ahab would let him go.

question: Why was one of the prophets killed by a lion?
answer: One of the prophets was killed by a lion because he did not obey the voice of Yahweh by hitting his fellow prophet.

question: How did the prophet disguise himself from the king after he had been hit and wounded?
answer: The prophet disguised himself from the king with a bandage over his eyes.

question: Why did the prophet tell a story to the king of Israel?
answer: The prophet told the story to the king of Israel to deceive him, so the king would make a ruling which would result in the forfeit of the king’s own life.

question: What bold statement did the prophet make to the king of Israel?
answer: The prophet told the king that he would lose his own life since he had allowed the man to live whom Yahweh had sentenced to death.

question: What did Ahab the king of Samaria want from Naboth the Jezreelite?
answer: Ahab, king of Samaria, wanted the vineyard from Naboth, which was near his palace.

question: What did Ahab offer Naboth for his vineyard?
answer: Ahab offered to give Naboth a better vineyard or to pay him in silver.

question: Why did Naboth refuse to give his vineyard to Ahab?
answer: Naboth refused to give his vineyard to Ahab because it was the inheritance of his ancestors.

question: What did Ahab do when Naboth refused to give up his vineyard?
answer: Ahab became resentful and angry, went to bed, and refused to eat any food.

question: Who told Ahab to get up from bed, eat, and be happy?
answer: Ahab’s wife, Jezebel, told him to get out of bed, eat, and be happy. She said she would get the vineyard for him.

question: What did Jezebel do to make sure Ahab would get Naboth’s vineyard?
answer: Jezebel had two dishonest men falsely accuse Naboth of blasphemy against God and the king at a public fast.

question: What would be the penalty for Naboth’s blasphemy?
answer: Naboth would be taken out and stoned to death.

question: Who did Yahweh send to the vineyard to meet Ahab?
answer: Yahweh sent Elijah the Tishbite to the vineyard.

question: What did Ahab do when Jezebel told him that Naboth was dead?
answer: When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he went to the vineyard to take possession of it.

question: What did Elijah tell Ahab would happen to him because of his sin?
answer: Elijah told Ahab that dogs would lick his blood where they had licked the blood of Naboth.

question: What message did Elijah deliver to Ahab from Yahweh?
answer: Elijah told Ahab that Yahweh said his family will all be killed, because he had provoked Yahweh and caused Israel to sin.

question: What would happen to Jezebel?
answer: The dogs would eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel.

question: What did Ahab do when he heard these words?
answer: Ahab tore his clothes, put sackcloth on his body, fasted and showed that he was sorry for the sins he had committed.

question: What did Yahweh do when Ahab humbled himself before him?
answer: Yahweh said that he would not bring this disaster in Ahab’s day, but would do it in his son’s day.

question: How long was there no war between Aram and Israel?
answer: For three years there had been no war between Aram and Israel.

question: Who was the king of Judah?
answer: The king of Judah was Jehoshaphat.

question: What did the king of Israel ask Jehoshaphat to do with him?
answer: The king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat to go to Ramoth Gilead and make war on the king of Aram.

question: Who did the king of Israel call together to seek the will of Yahweh in this matter?
answer: The king of Israel gathered the prophets, 400 men, and asked them about making war on Aram.

question: From what other prophet did the king of Israel seek advice?
answer: The king of Israel called upon Micaiah, the son of Imiah.

question: As the kings Ahab and Jehoshaphat sat on their thrones before the prophets, what was the prophesy they heard?
answer: As the kings Ahab and Jehoshaphat sat on their thrones, all the prophets said to them that they should attack Ramoth Gilead and win.

question: Was Micaiah in agreement with all the other prophets?
answer: Yes, Micaiah was in agreement with all the other prophets.

question: What bad news did Micaiah tell the king of Israel?
answer: Micaiah told the king of Israel that they would have no shepherd and would be scattered.

question: How did Micaiah tell the king of Israel that he would be enticed to go to Ramoth Gilead?
answer: Micaiah told the king of Israel that he would be enticed to go to Ramoth Gilead by the lies his prophets would tell him.

question: What did the king of Israel order to be done to Micaiah?
answer: The king of Israel ordered that Micaiah be seized and put in prison and be fed only a little bread and water until the king of Israel returned safely.

question: What did the king of Israel do to avoid capture in the battle at Ramoth Gilead?
answer: The king of Israel disguised himself to avoid capture at Ramoth Gilead.

question: How did Ahab receive a serious wound at the battle of Ramoth Gilead?
answer: A soldier of Aram shot his bow at random and the arrow struck Ahab between the joints of his armor, wounding him.

question: Where was Ahab buried?
answer: Ahab was buried in Samaria.

question: Who became king at the death of Ahab?
answer: His son Ahaziah became king of Israel.

question: How long did Jehoshaphat reign in Jerusalem?
answer: Jehoshaphat reigned in Jerusalem for 25 years.

question: What was said about the reign of Jehoshaphat?
answer: It was said that Jehoshaphat did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh.

question: What was said about the reign of Ahaziah?
answer: It was said that Ahaziah did the evil things that his father and mother had done and the evil things that Jeroboam had done, leading the Israelite people to worship idols.

question: Of whom was Peter an apostle?
answer: Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.

question: To whom did Peter write?
answer: Peter wrote to the foreigners of the dispersion, the chosen ones, throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.

question: Whom did Peter want to be blessed?
answer: Peter wanted the God and Father of their Lord Jesus Christ to be blessed.

question: How did God give them a new birth?
answer: In his great mercy, God gave them a new birth through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.

question: Why would the inheritance not perish, become stained, or fade away?
answer: The inheritance would not perish, become stained, or fade away because the inheritance was reserved in heaven for them.

question: By what means were they protected in God’s power?
answer: They were protected through faith for the salvation that is ready to be revealed in the last times.

question: Why was it necessary for them to feel sorrow in many different trials?
answer: It was necessary so that their faith would be tested, and so that their faith would be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

question: What is more precious than gold which perishes?
answer: Faith is more precious than gold.

question: Although the believers had not seen Jesus, what did they do?
answer: They loved him and believed in him and were very glad with unspeakable joy that was full of glory.

question: What did the ones who believed in him receive as the result of their faith?
answer: They received the salvation of their souls.

question: About what did the prophets search and inquire carefully?
answer: The prophets searched about the salvation the believers were receiving, about the grace that was to be theirs.

question: About what was the Spirit of Christ telling the prophets in advance?
answer: He was telling them about the sufferings of Christ and the glories that would follow him.

question: Whom were the prophets serving by their searches and inquiries?
answer: They were serving the believers.

question: Who desired the results of the prophets’ searches and inquiries to be revealed?
answer: Even the angels desired the results to be revealed.

question: What did Peter command the believers to do as obedient children?
answer: He commanded them to prepare their minds to obey God, be sober in their thinking, and have complete confidence in the grace that would be brought them, and not to conform themselves to their former desires.

question: Why did Peter say the believers should be holy?
answer: Because the one who called them is holy.

question: Why should the believers spend the time of their journey in fear?
answer: Because they called as “Father” the one who judges impartially according to each person’s work.

question: With what were the believers redeemed?
answer: They were not redeemed with silver or gold, but with the honored blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot.

question: From whom had the foreigners, the chosen ones, learned futile behavior?
answer: They had learned futile behavior from their fathers.

question: When was Christ foreknown, and when was he revealed?
answer: He was foreknown before the foundation of the world; he was revealed to the foreigners, the chosen ones, in what was then the last times.

question: How did the believers make their souls pure?
answer: They made their souls pure by obedience to the truth for brotherly love.

question: How were the believers born again?
answer: They were born again from imperishable seed, through the living and remaining word of God, not from perishable seed.

question: What is all flesh like, and what is its glory like?
answer: Flesh is like grass; its glory is like the flower of grass.

question: What happens to the word of the Lord?
answer: The word of the Lord remains forever.

question: What were the believers told to put aside?
answer: They were told to put aside all evil deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander.

question: Why were the believers to long for pure spiritual milk?
answer: They were to long for pure spiritual milk that they might grow in salvation.

question: Who was the living stone who was rejected by people and chosen by God?
answer: Jesus Christ was the living stone.

question: Why were the believers also like living stones?
answer: They were like living stones because they were being built up to be a spiritual house.

question: Why did the builders stumble, disobeying the word?
answer: The builders stumbled because they were appointed to do that.

question: Why were the believers a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, and a people for God’s possession?
answer: They were chosen so that they might announce the wonderful actions of God.

question: Why did Peter call the beloved to abstain from sinful desires?
answer: He called them to abstain so that those who might speak of them as having done evil would see their good behavior and praise God.

question: Why were the believers to obey every human authority?
answer: They were to obey every human authority because God wanted to use their obedience to silence the ignorant talk of foolish people.

question: Instead of using their freedom as a covering for wickedness, what were the foreigners, the chosen ones, to do?
answer: They were to use their freedom to be servants of God.

question: Why were servants supposed to be subject to their masters, even the malicious ones?
answer: Servants were supposed to be subject even to malicious masters because doing good and then suffering by being punished for it is praiseworthy with God.

question: Why were the servants called to suffer for doing good?
answer: Because Christ suffered for them, leaving an example for them, and gave himself to the one who judges justly.

question: Why did Christ carry Peter, believers, and the servants’ sins in his body to the tree?
answer: He carried their sins so that they might have no more part in sin, but instead live for righteousness, and because they were healed by his bruises.

question: After they all had been wandering away like lost sheep, to whom did they return?
answer: They all returned to the shepherd and guardian of their souls.

question: Why should wives submit to their husbands?
answer: Wives should submit so that those husbands who are disobedient might be won without a word.

question: How should wives adorn themselves?
answer: Wives should adorn themselves in the inner person of the heart, in the lasting beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit.

question: Which holy woman did Peter mention as an example of a wife who had confidence in God and submitted to her husband?
answer: Peter mentioned Sarah as an example.

question: Why should husbands live with their wives according to knowledge?
answer: Husbands should live with their wives according to knowledge so that their prayers are not hindered.

question: Why did Peter instruct all of the foreigners, the chosen ones, to be likeminded and to continue to bless?
answer: Because they were all called to do so, that they might inherit a blessing.

question: Why should the one who wants to love life stop his tongue from evil and turn away from what is bad and do what is good?
answer: Because the eyes of the Lord see the righteous.

question: Who were the ones who were blessed?
answer: Those who suffered because of righteousness were blessed.

question: How were the believers always to answer everyone who asked about their confidence in God?
answer: They were to be ready to answer always with meekness and respect.

question: What were the believers told to do to maintain their confidence in God?
answer: They were told to set apart the Lord Christ as precious in their hearts.

question: Why did Christ suffer once for sins?
answer: Christ suffered once so that he would bring Peter and the believers to God.

question: Why were the spirits to whom Christ preached in the spirit now in prison?
answer: The spirits who are now in prison were disobedient when the patience of God was waiting in the days of Noah.

question: What kind of baptism saves the believer?
answer: The baptism that saves the believer is not the washing with water, but the appeal of a good conscience to God through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

question: As Jesus is at the right hand of God in heaven, what must angels, authorities, and powers do?
answer: They must all submit to him.

question: With what did Peter command the believers to arm themselves?
answer: He commanded them to arm themselves with the same intention that Christ had when he suffered in the flesh.

question: Why did the Gentiles speak evil about the believers?
answer: They spoke evil about the foreigners, the chosen ones, because they did not participate in sensuality, passion, drunkenness, carousing, wild parties, and in wicked idolatries like the Gentiles.

question: Who is God ready to judge?
answer: God is ready to judge both the living and the dead.

question: Why were the believers to be of sound mind and have fervent love for one another?
answer: They were to do those things because the end of all things was coming, and for the sake of their prayers.

question: Why were each of the believers to use the gifts they had received to serve one another?
answer: They were to use their gifts so that God may be glorified through Jesus Christ.

question: Why were the believers told to rejoice if they experienced the sufferings of Christ or were insulted for the name of Christ?
answer: Because they were blessed if they were insulted.

question: For what actions were Christians not to be found guilty and suffer?
answer: Christians were not to suffer as murderers, thieves, evildoers, or meddlers.

question: Why should the ungodly person and the sinner obey God’s gospel?
answer: The ungodly person and the sinner obey God’s gospel because their judgment will be even more severe that the judgment of righteous people.

question: How were those who suffered according to the will of God to act?
answer: They were to entrust their souls to the faithful Creator while they did good.

question: What did Peter exhort his fellow elders to do?
answer: He exhorted them to tend the flock of God and look after them.

question: Who was Peter?
answer: Peter was a fellow elder, a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and a participant in the glory that will be revealed.

question: Why did all of them need to have humility and serve one another?
answer: Because God gives grace to the humble, and so that God might exalt them in due time.

question: To whom were the younger men to submit?
answer: They were to submit to the older men.

question: What were the people instructed to do?
answer: They were instructed to be sober, to be watchful, to stand firm against the devil, and to be strong in their faith.

question: What is the devil like?
answer: He is like a roaring lion stalking around, looking for someone to devour.

question: What would happen to the people after they had suffered for a little while?
answer: God would perfect, establish, and strengthen them.

question: As whom did Peter regard Silvanus?
answer: Peter regarded Silvanus as a faithful brother.

question: What did Peter say about what he had written?
answer: He said that what he had written was the true grace of God.

question: Who greeted the believers and how were they to greet one another?
answer: She who was in Babylon, and Mark, Peter’s son in the faith, greeted them; they were to greet one another with a kiss of love.

question: Who were the two wives of Elkanah?
answer: The wives of Elkanah were Hannah and Peninnah.

question: How many children did Hannah have at that time?
answer: At that time Hannah had no children.

question: Why did Elkanah give twice as much meat to Hannah?
answer: He gave a double portion to Hannah because he loved her.

question: Why did Hannah’s adversary provoke her?
answer: She provoked Hannah in order to make her upset, because Yahweh had closed her womb.

question: What did Hannah do because she was so sorrowful about not having children?
answer: She went to the house of Yahweh, and she cried very sorrowfully as she prayed to Yahweh.

question: What did Hannah vow to Yahweh?
answer: Hannah vowed that if Yahweh would give her a son, she would give him to Yahweh and they would never cut his hair.

question: Because Hannah was speaking to Yahweh from her heart, what did Eli the priest think about her actions?
answer: Eli saw Hannah’s lips moving but did not hear her voice, so he thought she was drunk.

question: What did Hannah assure Eli she was doing?
answer: Hannah assured Eli that she was not drunk but was talking to Yahweh because someone made her feel very badly.

question: What did Eli say to Hannah that caused her to go on her way, eat, and no longer feel sad?
answer: Eli told her to go in peace and said that he hoped the God of Israel would grant her request.

question: When Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son, what did she name him?
answer: Hannah named her son Samuel because she had requested him from Yahweh.

question: Why did Hannah not go with her husband to the house of Yahweh for the yearly sacrifice?
answer: She did not go because she was waiting until her son was weaned.

question: What offerings did Hannah bring with her when she brought her son to the house of Yahweh?
answer: Hannah brought three bulls, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine.

question: What did Hannah present to Yahweh?
answer: Hannah presented her son to Yahweh for as long as he would live.

question: Why did Hannah laugh at her enemies?
answer: Hannah laughed because she rejoiced in Yahweh’s salvation.

question: Why does Hannah say that people should not boast or speak arrogantly?
answer: People should not boast or speak arrogantly because Yahweh is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.

question: In Hannah’s song, who is the one who is unable to have more children?
answer: The woman who had many children before is not able to have any more.

question: Who decides death and life, or who goes down to Sheol or is raised up?
answer: Yahweh is the one who decides death and life, and who causes people to go down to Sheol or to come up from there.

question: Who makes people poor or rich?
answer: Yahweh makes people poor, and he makes them rich.

question: Who raises up the poor and lifts the needy to sit in a seat of honor?
answer: Yahweh raises them up to sit in a seat of honor.

question: Who does Hannah say will protect the feet of his faithful people and silence the wicked in darkness?
answer: Hannah says that Yahweh will guard the feet of his faithful people and will silence the wicked.

question: Who will judge the ends of the earth and give strength to his king?
answer: Yahweh will judge the ends of the earth and give strength to his king.

question: What child served Yahweh in the presence of Eli the priest?
answer: Samuel served Yahweh in the presence of Eli the priest.

question: Whose sons were wicked men who did not know Yahweh?
answer: Eli the priest’s sons did very bad things.

question: What was the custom of the priests with the people at the time of sacrifice?
answer: The custom was for the priest’s servant to come with a three-pronged fork while the meat was boiling and take whatever the fork brought up for the priest.

question: What evil thing did Eli’s sons have their servant do?
answer: They had their servant demand raw meat for the priest before the fat was burned as an offering to Yahweh, and had him take it by force if the person refused.

question: Why was the sin of Eli’s sons so great?
answer: Their sin was great before Yahweh because the men were treating very disrespectfully the offerings that people were bringing to Yahweh.

question: What would Samuel’s mother make for him from year to year to clothe him?
answer: She would make him a small robe each year.

question: How would Eli bless Elkanah and his wife?
answer: Eli blessed them by asking Yahweh to give them more children from Hannah.

question: What was Yahweh’s response to Eli’s prayer for Samuel’s parents to have more children?
answer: Yahweh helped Hannah, and she bore three more sons and two daughters.

question: What did Eli say to his sons when he heard evil reports about them?
answer: Eli told his sons that the report he was hearing from Yahweh’s people about their evil deeds was not good. He told them to stop doing what they were doing.

question: Why did Eli’s sons not listen to his voice?
answer: Eli’s sons did not listen to his voice because Yahweh desired to make them die.

question: Who grew up and was good in the sight of Yahweh and also with men?
answer: Samuel grew up and was good in the sight of Yahweh and with men.

question: Who told Eli that Yahweh chose Eli’s ancestors out of all the tribes of Israel to be Yahweh’s priest?
answer: A man of God told Eli that Yahweh had chosen his ancestors.

question: How had Eli and his sons scorned Yahweh’s sacrifices and offerings?
answer: They scorned the sacrifices and offerings by honoring his sons above Yahweh and fattening themselves on the best parts of offerings.

question: What did Yahweh tell Eli would happen to the men in his family?
answer: Yahweh told Eli that all the men born in his family would die young.

question: What did Yahweh say would be a sign to Eli that his prophecy would come true?
answer: The sign would be that both of his sons would die on the same day.

question: Who will walk before Yahweh’s faithful priest always?
answer: Yahweh has chosen another man who will serve him faithfully and continually be a helper to the king whom Yahweh will appoint.

question: Why will everyone left in Eli’s family come and bow down to the faithful priest?
answer: They will ask him to allow them to work with the other priests so that they can have food to eat.

question: What was Samuel’s reply when he heard Yahweh call to him as he was lying down?
answer: Samuel replied that he was ready to do whatever you ask.

question: What did Eli tell Samuel to do when Samuel ran to him?
answer: Eli said that he did not call Samuel and told him to go lie down again.

question: What had not yet been revealed to Samuel?
answer: The word of Yahweh had not yet been revealed to Samuel.

question: What did Eli realize after the third time that Samuel came to him?
answer: Eli realized that it was Yahweh who had been calling Samuel.

question: What did Eli tell Samuel to say if he was called again?
answer: Eli told Samuel to say that Yahweh should speak, because his servant was listening.

question: What did Yahweh say would happen to the ears of everyone when they heard what he was going to do?
answer: Yahweh said that the ears of everyone who heard it would tingle.

question: What had Eli’s sons brought upon themselves?
answer: Eli’s sons had brought a curse upon themselves.

question: What would never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering?
answer: The iniquity of Eli’s house would never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.

question: What was Samuel afraid to do in the morning after he opened the doors of the house of Yahweh?
answer: He was afraid to tell Eli about the vision.

question: What did Samuel do after Eli told him that he must not hide from him the words that Yahweh had spoken?
answer: Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him.

question: What did all Israel from Dan to Beersheba know about Samuel?
answer: All Israel knew that Samuel was established as a prophet of Yahweh.

question: What was the result of the battle between Israel and the Philistines?
answer: Israel was defeated by the Philistines.

question: What did the elders of Israel decide to do so that they could be saved from the power of their enemies?
answer: The elders decided to bring the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh from Shiloh to be with them.

question: Who was with the Box of the Covenant of God?
answer: The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the Box of the Covenant.

question: What did the Philistines wonder when they heard the great shout from the people of Israel?
answer: The Philistines wondered about the meaning of the great shout in the camp of the Hebrews.

question: Who did the Philistines say had come into the camp of the Hebrews?
answer: The Philistines said that a god had come into the camp.

question: With what did the Philistines say that the gods of Israel had struck the Egyptians in the wilderness?
answer: They said that the gods had struck the Egyptians with every kind of plague.

question: What happened to the two sons of Eli when the Box of God was taken Israel was struck and fled?
answer: The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

question: What did the whole city do when the man from the battle line entered the city and told the news?
answer: When the man told the news, the whole city cried out.

question: What question did Eli ask when he heard the noise of the outcry?
answer: Eli asked what the sound of the tumult meant.

question: What did the man tell Eli had happened to his sons and to the Box of God when Israel was defeated?
answer: The man told Eli that his two sons were dead and the Box of God had been taken.

question: What was the injury that killed Eli when he fell over backward from his seat by the side of the gate?
answer: Eli broke his neck and he died.

question: What happened when Phinehas’s pregnant wife heard that the Box of God was captured and her father-in-law and husband were dead?
answer: Phinehas’s wife knelt down and gave birth because her labor pains suddenly began.

question: What name did Phinehas’s wife give to the baby and why did she give him that name?
answer: She named the baby Ichabod, saying that the glory had departed from Israel because the Box of God had been taken.

question: In what position did the people find the idol Dagon the next day after the Philistines brought the Box of God into Dagon’s house?
answer: Dagon was found fallen face down on the ground before the Box of Yahweh.

question: What remained of the idol Dagon the next morning after they had set him back in his place?
answer: Only the body of Dagon remained; his head and hands were lying cut off in the doorway.

question: Why did the men of Ashdod say that the Box of the God of Israel should not stay with them?
answer: They said it should not stay because the hand of their God was severe against them and against their god Dagon.

question: To what place did the Philistines move the Box of the God of Israel?
answer: The Philistines moved the Box to Gath.

question: With what did Yahweh strike the men of the city of Gath?
answer: Yahweh struck them with tumors.

question: What did the people of Ekron say the Box of the God of Israel would do to them?
answer: They said that it would kill them and their people.

question: To what place did the people of Ekron ask the rulers to send the Box?
answer: They asked that the Box be sent back to its own place.

question: To what place did the cry of the city go?
answer: The cry of the city went up to the heavens.

question: For how long was the Box of Yahweh in the Philistines’ country?
answer: The Box was in the country of the Philistines for seven months.

question: Who did the Philistines call to ask for advice on how the Box of Yahweh should be sent back to its own country?
answer: They called for the priests and the diviners to tell them how to send the Box back.

question: What did the priests and diviners tell the Philistine people to send as a guilt offering to the God of Israel?
answer: They told the Philistines to send five gold tumors and five gold mice.

question: Why did the priests and diviners say the people should not be stubborn like the Egyptians and Pharaoh were?
answer: Because when God dealt severely with the Egyptians and Pharaoh, they had to let Israel go.

question: What animals did the priests and diviners tell the Philistines to tie to the cart for the Box of Yahweh?
answer: They told the Philistines to hitch two nursing cows to the cart.

question: How would the Philistines know that it was Yahweh who had done this great harm to them?
answer: The Philistines would know it was Yahweh if the cows pulling the cart went on their own to Beth Shemesh.

question: Where did the nursing cows go with the cart carrying the Box and the gold mice and tumors?
answer: The cows went straight in the direction of Beth Shemesh.

question: What were the people of Beth Shemesh doing when they lifted up their eyes and saw the Box?
answer: They were harvesting their wheat in the valley.

question: What did the people of Beth Shemesh do with the cows that had pulled the cart?
answer: They offered the cows as a burnt offering to Yahweh.

question: Who took down the Box of Yahweh and the box that was with it?
answer: The Levites took down the Box of Yahweh and the box that was with it.

question: What did the five rulers of the Philistines do when they saw what had happened?
answer: They returned that day to Ekron.

question: What did the numbers of gold tumors and gold mice represent?
answer: The five gold tumors represented the people of their five cities, and the gold mice represented all the Philistine cities belonging to those rulers.

question: Why did Yahweh strike some of the men of Beth Shemesh?
answer: Yahweh struck them because they looked into his Box.

question: What did the messengers from Beth Shemesh ask the people of Kiriath Jearim to do?
answer: The messengers asked the people of Kiriath Jearim to come and take the Box of Yahweh to their city.

question: What did the men of Kiriath Jearim do to Abinadab’s son, Eleazar, so that he could take care of the Box of Yahweh?
answer: They consecrated him to keep the Box of Yahweh.

question: What did all the house of Israel do during the twenty years that the Box remained in Kiriath Jearim?
answer: During that time, the Israelite people were very sorry that Yahweh was not helping them anymore.

question: What did Samuel tell the people of Israel that they needed to remove from among them for Yahweh to rescue them from the Philistines?
answer: Samuel told them that they needed to remove the foreign gods and the Ashtoreths from among them and serve Yahweh only.

question: What did the people of Israel admit that they had done when they gathered at Mizpah?
answer: They admitted that they had sinned against Yahweh.

question: Why did the people of Israel ask Samuel to call out to Yahweh for them?
answer: They were afraid because they heard that the rulers of the Philistines were coming to attack them.

question: What did Yahweh do when Samuel offered a lamb as a burnt offering and cried out to him?
answer: Yahweh answered Samuel.

question: What did Yahweh do that threw the Philistines into confusion as they drew near to attack Israel?
answer: Yahweh thundered with a great sound on that day against the Philistines.

question: What did Samuel set up between Mizpah and Shen as a remembrance that Yahweh had helped them?
answer: Samuel took a stone and set it up.

question: What happened to the towns that the Philistines had taken from Israel?
answer: They were recaptured by Israel.

question: What did Samuel do as he went on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, Mizpah, and back to Ramah?
answer: Samuel judged Israel in all these places.

question: In what ways did Samuel’s two sons, who were judges, not walk in the ways of their father?
answer: They were not honest like their father. They accepted bribes, and they did not make honest decisions about people’s disputes.

question: What request did the elders of Israel make of Samuel?
answer: They asked Samuel to appoint a king to judge them, like all the other nations.

question: What did Samuel do when he was displeased by the elders’ request to give them a king?
answer: Samuel prayed to Yahweh.

question: Why did Yahweh tell Samuel to listen to the voice of the people?
answer: Yahweh told Samuel to listen because the people were not rejecting Samuel, but they were rejecting Yahweh from reigning over them.

question: What warning did Yahweh tell Samuel to give to the people of Israel?
answer: Yahweh told Samuel to warn the people about the way the king would rule over them.

question: For what did Samuel warn the people that a king would take their sons?
answer: Samuel warned that the king would take their sons to be officers and soldiers, to plow his fields and harvest his crops, and to make weapons of war.

question: How did Samuel warn the people about what a king would do with their daughters and property?
answer: Samuel warned that the king would take their daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers, and he would take the best of their fields and vineyards and olive groves to give to his attendants.

question: How did Samuel warn the people about what a king would do with their servants and animals?
answer: Samuel warned that the king would take their servants, the best of their young men and donkeys, and a tenth of their flocks, and the people would become his servants.

question: What did Samuel warn would happen when the people cried out because of the king they had chosen?
answer: Samuel said that Yahweh would not answer them on that day.

question: How did the people of Israel respond to the warnings from Samuel?
answer: The people refused to listen and said they wanted a king over them so they could be like the other nations.

question: What was Yahweh’s response when Samuel repeated the people’s words to him?
answer: Yahweh told Samuel to listen to their voice and appoint a king for them.

question: What were the outstanding physical features of Saul, the son of Kish?
answer: Saul was a handsome young man who was taller than any of the other people from his shoulders upward.

question: What was the outcome when Kish asked his son Saul to go and look for their lost donkeys?
answer: Saul took one of the servants and passed through many places without finding them.

question: What did Saul tell his servant they should do when they came to the land of Zuph?
answer: Saul told his servant that they should go back so his father would not stop being concerned about the donkeys and become concerned about them.

question: What different idea did the servant present to Saul?
answer: The servant suggested they should go to a man of God in the city who might tell them the way they should go.

question: What did the servant have to give to the man of God so he would tell them which way to go?
answer: The servant had a fourth of a shekel of silver to give to the man of God.

question: What did Saul and his servant ask the young women who were coming out to draw water?
answer: Saul and his servant asked if the seer was in the city.

question: Why was the seer coming to the city on that day?
answer: The seer was coming to the city because the people were having a sacrifice at the high place, and he would bless the sacrifice.

question: What did Yahweh reveal to Samuel about Saul’s role in Israel?
answer: Yahweh told Samuel that he was to anoint Saul as ruler over Israel, and Saul would save Yahweh’s people from the hand of the Philistines.

question: What invitation did Samuel give to Saul after he revealed that he was the seer Saul was seeking?
answer: Samuel invited Saul to go up and eat with him at the high place.

question: How did Samuel surprise Saul with what he told him?
answer: Samuel told him that all the desire of Israel was for him and his father’s house, even though Saul was from the least clan of the smallest tribe.

question: What did Samuel tell the cook to serve to Saul?
answer: Samuel told the cook to serve Saul the thigh portion that had been set aside for him for the appointed time.

question: What did Samuel say to Saul from the roof in the morning?
answer: Samuel told Saul to get up so he could send him on his way.

question: Why did Samuel tell Saul to stand still for a while on the outskirts of the city?
answer: Samuel told Saul to stand still so Samuel could tell him the word of God.

question: Why did Samuel pour a flask of oil on Saul’s head and kiss him?
answer: He did this because Yahweh had anointed Saul to be a ruler over his inheritance.

question: What future event did Samuel share with Saul?
answer: Samuel told Saul that he would find two men near Rachel’s tomb who would tell him that the donkeys had been found.

question: What did Samuel tell Saul would happen when he came to the oak of Tabor?
answer: Three men going up to God at Bethel would meet him and give him two loaves of bread, which he should take.

question: What did Samuel tell Saul would happen when he came to Gibeah of God?
answer: The Spirit of Yahweh would rush upon him, he would prophesy with a group of prophets, and he would be changed into a different man.

question: What instructions did Samuel give to Saul for later?
answer: Samuel told Saul to go down to Gilgal and wait seven days for Samuel to come and offer sacrifices.

question: What happened when Saul turned his back to leave Samuel?
answer: When Saul turned to leave, God changed Saul’s inner being.

question: Why did people wonder if Saul was one of the prophets?
answer: They saw him prophesying with the prophets and wondered how this had happened to the son of Kish.

question: What did Saul tell his uncle when he was asked where he had gone?
answer: Saul told his uncle that when he and his servant could not find the donkeys, they went to Samuel.

question: What did Saul not tell his uncle about what Samuel had said to him?
answer: Saul did not tell his uncle about the matter of the kingship.

question: Why did Yahweh say that Israel had rejected him?
answer: Israel had rejected Yahweh because they had asked for a king to be set over them.

question: What happened when Saul, the son of Kish, was chosen as the next king?
answer: They looked for Saul, but he could not be found.

question: Where was Saul when he was chosen as the next king?
answer: Saul had hidden himself among the bags.

question: What did Samuel say about the man whom Yahweh had chosen?
answer: Samuel said that there was no one like Saul among all the people.

question: How were the customs of the kingship established and preserved?
answer: Samuel told the people the customs of the kingship, wrote them in a book, and placed the book before Yahweh.

question: How did some wicked men show their dislike for Saul?
answer: Some wicked men despised Saul and did not bring him a gift.

question: What was the response of Nahash the Ammonite to the request for a covenant from the men of Jabesh?
answer: He said he would make a covenant with them if he could gouge out all their right eyes and bring disgrace on Israel.

question: How did the elders of Jabesh respond to Nahash’s proposal?
answer: They asked for seven days to send messengers throughout Israel to see if anyone would save them.

question: Why were the people in Saul’s town of Gibeah weeping?
answer: They were weeping because they had heard the words of the men from Jabesh.

question: How did Saul respond to the threat against Jabesh?
answer: The Spirit of God rushed upon him, he became very angry, and he persuaded the men of Israel and Judah to fight.

question: What message did the messengers bring back to the men of Jabesh?
answer: They told the men of Jabesh that they would have deliverance the next day by the time the sun was hot.

question: What did the men of Jabesh say to Nahash the Ammonite?
answer: They told Nahash that they would come out to him the next day, and he could do to them whatever seemed good to him.

question: What was the outcome of the battle between Israel and the Ammonites?
answer: The people of Israel attacked and defeated the Ammonites, and the survivors were totally scattered.

question: Why did Saul say that none of the men who opposed him would be put to death?
answer: Saul said no one would be put to death, because that day Yahweh had brought deliverance to Israel.

question: Why did Samuel, Saul, and all the people of Israel go to Gilgal?
answer: They went to Gilgal to renew the kingship, make Saul king before Yahweh, and sacrifice peace offerings.

question: What did the people of Israel say when Samuel asked if he had ever wronged them?
answer: The people of Israel told Samuel he had not defrauded or oppressed them or taken anything from anyone.

question: Why did Samuel tell the people of Israel to present themselves before Yahweh?
answer: He told them to present themselves so he could make the case against them that they should not have asked for a king instead of trusting Yahweh to rescue them.

question: What did God do to the ancestors of Israel after they forgot Yahweh their God?
answer: Yahweh sold them into the hand of Sisera, the Philistines, and the king of Moab, who all fought against them.

question: What did Yahweh do after Israel’s ancestors cried out to him and asked to be rescued from their enemies?
answer: Yahweh sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue them.

question: What did Samuel remind the people of Israel that they had requested?
answer: Samuel reminded the people that they had wanted a king to reign over them, even though Yahweh their God was their king.

question: What choice did Samuel present to the people of Israel?
answer: They could fear Yahweh and serve him, or they could rebel against his command and his hand would be against them.

question: What did Samuel challenge the people of Israel to do?
answer: Samuel challenged the people to stand and see the great thing Yahweh is doing before their eyes.

question: What did Samuel ask Yahweh to send so that the people would know the extent of their wickedness?
answer: He asked Yahweh to send thunder and rain during the wheat harvest.

question: How did Samuel respond when the people of Israel realized their sin?
answer: Samuel told the people not to be afraid, but to serve Yahweh with all their heart and not turn aside.

question: What message of comfort did Samuel give to the people of Israel?
answer: Samuel comforted the people by telling them that Yahweh would not forsake them, because of his great name.

question: What did Samuel promise to do for Israel?
answer: He promised to continue to pray for them and to instruct them in the good and right way.

question: What did Samuel challenge the people of Israel to do?
answer: Samuel told them to fear Yahweh and serve him faithfully with all their heart, considering the great things he had done for them.

question: What did Saul do with the soldiers he did not choose to be with him?
answer: Saul sent the rest of the soldiers home to their own tents.

question: How did Israel make itself stink among the Philistines?

question: How did the Philistines respond to the attack by Jonathan?

question: How did the men of Israel react to the forces of the Philistines?

question: What did Saul do when Samuel did not come to Gilgal after seven days?

question: What excuse did Saul give Samuel for not waiting for him to offer the sacrifices?

question: How did Samuel rebuke Saul?

question: What strategy did the Philistines use against the people of Israel?

question: What problem did the Israelites face in their fight against the Philistines?

question: How were the soldiers of Israel hindered on the day of battle?

question: What secret plan did Jonathan, the son of Saul, have?

question: What did the six hundred men with Saul not know?

question: What proposal did Jonathan present to his young armor-bearer?

question: What was the armor-bearer’s response to the proposal?

question: What would be the sign to Jonathan and his armor-bearer that Yahweh had given the Philistines into their hand?

question: What was the result of the attack that Jonathan and his armor-bearer made on the Philistine garrison?

question: What did Saul do when his watchmen saw the Philistine army dispersing?

question: Why did Saul tell Ahijah the priest to bring the Box of God to him?

question: Who rejoined the Israelites who had remained with Saul and Jonathan?

question: Who saved Israel that day?

question: What caused the men of Israel to be distressed and faint?

question: How did Jonathan unknowingly break the oath?
answer: Jonathan, who had not heard the oath, ate some honey from a honeycomb.

question: How was Jonathan critical of the oath his father had made?

question: How did the people of Israel sin against Yahweh after their battle against the Philistines?

question: What did Saul believe was the reason why he did not receive an answer when he inquired of God?

question: How did Saul say he would deal with the sin that had been committed?
answer: He said that the person who committed the sin would surely die, even if it was his son Jonathan.

question: How was it determined that Jonathan was the person who had sinned?
answer: The priest threw a lot, and it indicated that either Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not one of the other Israelite soldiers. He threw the lot again, and the lot indicated that Jonathan had sinned.

question: How was Jonathan saved from death?
answer: The people redeemed Jonathan and would not allow him to die because he had brought about a great salvation for Israel.

question: How did Saul lead Israel as their king?

question: Why did Yahweh want Saul to attack and completely destroy Amalek?

question: Why did Saul tell the Kenites to depart from the Amalekites?

question: How did Saul disobey the directions that Yahweh had given to him?

question: Why did Yahweh regret that he had made Saul king?
answer: Yahweh regretted making Saul king because Saul had turned from following him and was no longer obedient to him.

question: What lie did Saul tell Samuel?

question: How did Samuel respond to the lie that Saul had told him?

question: What excuse did Saul give to Samuel to explain his disobedience?

question: How did Samuel rebuke Saul?

question: What excuse did Saul repeat to Samuel?

question: What was Samuel’s response to Saul?

question: What reason did Saul give Samuel for his sin?
answer: Saul said he had disobeyed Yahweh’s command because he was afraid of the people, and so he listened to their voice.

question: What declaration did Samuel give to Saul from Yahweh?
answer: Samuel said that Yahweh had rejected Saul from being king over Israel because Saul had rejected the word of Yahweh.

question: To whom was Yahweh going to give the kingdom of Israel?
answer: Samuel told Saul that Yahweh was going to give the kingdom to one of Saul’s neighbors, an Israelite who was a better man than Saul.

question: What did Samuel do to finish the task that Saul had not done?
answer: Samuel hacked King Agag to pieces before Yahweh.

question: Why did Yahweh tell Samuel to stop mourning for Saul?
answer: Yahweh told him to stop because he had rejected Saul from being king over Israel.

question: What did Samuel fear would happen if Saul heard he was going to Bethlehem?
answer: He feared that Saul would kill him.

question: How did Yahweh say that Samuel would know whom to anoint?
answer: Yahweh told Samuel that he would show him what to do and that Samuel should anoint the one Yahweh told him to anoint.

question: How did the elders of Bethlehem act when Samuel arrived?
answer: They came trembling to meet him and asked if his coming was in peace.

question: What did Samuel think when he looked at Eliab?
answer: He thought that surely Yahweh’s anointed one was standing before him.

question: How did Yahweh explain that he does not see as a human sees?
answer: Yahweh said that a human looks on the outward appearance, but Yahweh looks on the heart.

question: What did Samuel say to Jesse after seven of his sons passed before him?
answer: Samuel said that Yahweh had not chosen any of them.

question: Where was Jesse’s youngest son before Samuel called for him?
answer: The youngest son was out in the pasture tending the flock of sheep.

question: What happened to David after Samuel anointed him?
answer: The Spirit of Yahweh rushed upon David from that day forward.

question: What spirit troubled Saul after the Spirit of Yahweh had turned away from him?
answer: A bad spirit from Yahweh terrified him.

question: What did Saul’s servants suggest a skillful player on the lyre could do for him?
answer: When the bad spirit was on Saul, the person would play the lyre, and would calm down.

question: Which of Jesse’s sons did Saul ask to have sent to him?

question: What assignment did Saul give David because he loved him greatly?

question: What would happen to Saul when David played the lyre?
answer: The bad spirit would turn away from Saul, and he would calm down and feel better.

question: Why had Saul and the men of Israel encamped in the valley of Elah?
answer: They had drawn up in battle array to fight the Philistines.

question: What did Goliath have on his head?
answer: He had a helmet of bronze on his head.

question: What did Goliath carry between his shoulders?
answer: He had a curved sword of bronze between his shoulders.

question: What did Goliath call the ranks of Israel?
answer: Goliath called them servants of Saul.

question: What did Goliath say would happen to the Philistines if Israel’s chosen man killed him?
answer: He said the Philistines would become servants to Israel.

question: When Saul and all Israel heard what the Philistine said, how did they feel?
answer: They lost their courage and became terrified.

question: Which of Jesse’s sons had followed Saul to the battle?
answer: The three oldest sons of Jesse had followed Saul to the battle.

question: For how long and how often did the Philistine champion present himself for battle?
answer: He presented himself for forty days, morning and evening.

question: What was the army doing as David arrived at the camp?
answer: The army was going out to the battle array, shouting the war cry.

question: As David spoke with his brothers, who came out from the ranks of the Philistines?
answer: As David spoke, the champion, Goliath, the Philistine from Gath, came out from the ranks of the Philistines.

question: What would the king do for the man who killed Goliath?
answer: The king would enrich the man with great wealth, give him his daughter in marriage, and no longer require that man’s family to pay taxes or do unpaid work for the Israelite kingdom.

question: What did David say the man who killed the Philistine would take away from Israel?
answer: The man who killed the Philistine would turn away the disgrace from Israel.

question: What did Eliab accuse David of having in his heart?
answer: Eliab accused David of presumption and evil in his heart, saying David’s motive for coming was to watch the battle.

question: What did David tell Saul he would do?
answer: David told Saul that he would go and fight with the Philistine.

question: What did David do to a lion or a bear that took a sheep from the flock?
answer: He went out after it, struck it, and delivered the sheep from its mouth; if it rose against him, he would seize its jaw and strike it and kill it.

question: Why did David say this uncircumcised Philistine would be like the lion or the bear he had killed?
answer: The Philistine would be like them because he had taunted the arrayed armies of the living God.

question: Why was David not able to walk in the armor the king provided?
answer: He was not able to walk in the armor because he was not used it.

question: Why did the Philistine despise David when he saw him?
answer: He despised David because he was only a youth, ruddy, and with a boyish appearance, and Goliath believed he could easily defeat David.

question: When the Philistine came with a sword, spear, and curved sword, in whose name did David say he came?
answer: David said that he came in the name of Yahweh of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom the Philistine had taunted.

question: What did David say all the earth would know after he defeated the Philistine?
answer: All the earth would know that the Israelite people worship an all-powerful God.

question: What did David do when the Philistine drew near to meet him?
answer: David hurried and ran toward the battle line to meet him.

question: What did the Philistines do when they saw that their warrior was dead?
answer: The Philistines fled.

question: What did the people of Israel do when they returned from chasing the Philistines?
answer: The people of Israel plundered the Philistine camp.

question: What did David have in his hand when Abner brought him before Saul?
answer: David had the head of the Philistine in his hand.

question: How strongly was the soul of Jonathan bound to the soul of David?
answer: The soul of Jonathan was bound with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

question: What did Jonathan give to David along with his garments, sword, bow, and belt?
answer: Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David.

question: Over whom did Saul set David?
answer: Saul set him over the men of war.

question: What had the singers’ song ascribed to David that displeased Saul?
answer: They ascribed to David myriads, but they had ascribed only thousands to Saul.

question: What did Saul think as he threw the spear at David?
answer: Saul thought that he would strike David and pin him to the wall.

question: Why did David succeed in all his ways?
answer: David succeeded because Yahweh was with him.

question: What did Saul hope would happen to David if he fought the Philistines?
answer: Saul hoped the Philistines would kill David.

question: What did Saul think his daughter Michal would be for David if Saul gave her to him?
answer: Saul thought she could be a snare for David.

question: How did Saul command his servants to speak with David about becoming the king’s son-in-law?
answer: He commanded his servants to speak with David privately.

question: Why did David think he was not worthy to be the king’s son-in-law?
answer: He said he was a poor and insignificant man.

question: What was the only bride-price the king desired from David?
answer: The king desired one hundred foreskins of the Philistines.

question: What did David and his men do that exceeded the king’s requested bride-price?
answer: David and his men struck two hundred Philistines and brought their foreskins to the king.

question: How great was David’s success, so that he earned an excellent reputation?
answer: David was more successful than any of Saul’s other army commanders.

question: Why did Jonathan tell David to be on his guard and hide himself?
answer: Jonathan told him to be very careful because his father was seeking to kill David.

question: What did Jonathan tell Saul that David’s deeds had been for him?
answer: Jonathan told Saul that David’s deeds had been very good for him.

question: What did Saul swear after listening to Jonathan?
answer: Saul swore that as Yahweh lives, David would not be killed.

question: What happened when David again went out and fought with the Philistines?
answer: David’s soldiers killed many of the Philistine soldiers, and as a result, the rest of the Philistine army ran away.

question: Why did Saul send messengers to David’s house to watch him?
answer: Saul wanted them to kill David in the morning.

question: How did Michal help David to flee and escape?
answer: Michal lowered David out a window since soldiers were watching the door.

question: What did Saul plan to do when he ordered his messengers to bring David to him in the bed?
answer: Saul planned to kill him.

question: What did Michal use at the head of the idol in the bed to make it look like David?
answer: She put a weaving of goats’ hair at its head.

question: When David fled and escaped, to whom did he go in Ramah?
answer: David went to Samuel in Ramah.

question: What happened to Saul’s messengers when they saw the group of prophets?
answer: The Spirit of God came on them, and they also prophesied.

question: After sending messengers two more times, what did Saul do?
answer: Saul himself went to Ramah.

question: How long did Saul lie naked before Samuel?
answer: He lay naked all that day and all that night.

question: What did Jonathan say his father did not do without telling him?
answer: He said that his father did nothing either great or small without revealing it to him.

question: How close did David say he was to death?
answer: He said that there was only a step between him and death.

question: What did David ask Jonathan to let him do until the third evening?
answer: David asked to hide in the field until the third evening.

question: What reason did David tell Jonathan to give Saul if Saul missed him?
answer: He was to tell Saul that David had asked make a brief visit to his city, Bethlehem, for the yearly sacrifice for his whole clan.

question: Why did David ask Jonathan to deal faithfully with him?
answer: David asked this because Jonathan had brought him into a covenant of Yahweh.

question: Where did Jonathan ask David to go so they could talk?
answer: He asked David to go with him out into the field so they could speak privately.

question: Why did Jonathan want to make his father’s intentions known to David?
answer: Jonathan promised to reveal his father’s intentions so that David flee.

question: How did Jonathan know that David would keep his promise that he would not harm Jonathan’s descendants?
answer: Jonathan knew that David would keep that promise because David loved Jonathan as much as he loved himself.

question: Whom did Jonathan say he would send to find the arrows he shot?
answer: He said he would send a boy to find the arrows.

question: When the festival of the new moon came, what did the king do?
answer: The king came to the table for the feast.

question: What did Saul think might have happened to David to make him absent from the feast?
answer: Saul thought it was an accident and that David was not ritually clean.

question: Why did Jonathan say David had to attend his family’s sacrifice?
answer: He said David’s brother had commanded him to be there.

question: What did Saul call his son Jonathan in his burning anger?
answer: He called him the son a mother who must have been unfaithful to Saul, because no real son of his would have done that.

question: Why was Jonathan grieved for David?
answer: He was grieved for David because his father had dishonored him, saying unfairly that David was not loyal to him.

question: Where did Jonathan shoot an arrow as the boy ran?
answer: Jonathan shot an arrow over the boy so that it would land on the ground far ahead of him.

question: What did Jonathan do after David left?
answer: Jonathan went back into the city of Gibeah.

question: What did David say the king had told him to let no one know?
answer: He said the king had commanded him to let no one know anything about what the king sent him to do.

question: What did the priest tell David about the bread he had?
answer: The priest said that there was no common bread, but there was holy bread, if the young men not recently become ceremonially unclean by having sexual relations with women.

question: From where had the bread of the Presence been taken?
answer: The bread of the Presence had been taken from the table in Yahweh’s presence in the sacred tent.

question: What was the work of Doeg the Edomite, who was there that day and saw what Ahimelech did to help David?
answer: Doeg the Edomite was the chief of the herders who worked for Saul.

question: Why did David say he had no weapons with him?
answer: He said that he had not brought any weapons because the king’s matter was so urgent that he did not have time to get any weapons.

question: From whom was David fleeing when he went to Achish, the king of Gath?
