question: Why did Paul write this letter to the Corinthian church?
answer: He wrote to them so that they would know the depth of the love that he had for them.

question: What did Paul say the Corinthian saints should now do for the one they punished?
answer: Paul said they should forgive and comfort that person.

question: Why did Paul say the Corinthian saints should forgive and comfort the one they had punished?
answer: This was so that the one they had punished would not be overwhelmed by too much sorrow.

question: What is another reason Paul wrote to the Corinthian church?
answer: Paul wrote to them to test them and to find out whether they were obedient in everything.

question: Why was it important for the Corinthian church to know that whoever they had forgiven was also forgiven by Paul and in the presence of Christ?
answer: This was so that Satan would not trick them.

question: Why did Paul have no peace of mind when he went to the city of Troas?
answer: He had no peace of mind because he could not find his brother Titus in Troas.

question: What did God do through Paul and his companions?
answer: Through Paul and his companions God spread the sweet aroma of the knowledge of Christ everywhere.

question: How did Paul say that he and his companions were different from many people who sold the word of God for profit?
answer: Paul and his companions were different in that they spoke with purity of motives, as sent from God, speaking in Christ in the presence of God.

question: What letter of recommendation did Paul and his companions have?
answer: The saints at Corinth were their letter of recommendation, known and read by all people.

question: What was the confidence that Paul and his companions had in God through Christ?
answer: Their confidence was not in their own competence, but in the adequacy that God provided them.

question: What was the basis of the new covenant of which God had qualified Paul and his companions to be servants?
answer: The new covenant was based on the Spirit, who gives life, not the letter, which kills.

question: Why could the people of Israel not look directly at Moses’ face?
answer: They could not look directly at his face because of the glory of his face, a glory that was fading.

question: Which will have more glory, the ministry of condemnation or the service of righteousness?
answer: The ministry of righteousness abounds much more in glory.

question: How can Israel’s mind be opened and the veil removed from their hearts?
answer: Only when Israel turns to the Lord Christ are their minds opened and the veil lifted away.

question: What is the problem which remains today for the people of Israel whenever the old covenant of Moses is read?
answer: Their problem is that their minds are closed and a veil lies over their hearts.

question: How can Israel’s mind be opened and the veil removed from their hearts?
answer: Only when Israel turns to the Lord Christ are their minds opened and the veil lifted away.

question: What is present with the Spirit of the Lord?
answer: Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

question: Into what are all those who are seeing the glory of the Lord being transformed?
answer: They are being transformed into the same glorious likeness from one degree of glory into another.

question: Why did Paul and his companions not become discouraged?
answer: They did not become discouraged because of the ministry they had and because they had received mercy.

question: What were the ways that Paul and his companions had renounced?
answer: They had renounced the ways that are shameful and hidden. They did not live by craftiness and did not mishandle the word of God.

question: How did Paul and those like him recommend themselves to everyone’s conscience in the sight of God?
answer: They did this by presenting the truth.

question: To whom is the gospel veiled?
answer: It is veiled to those who are perishing.

question: Why is the gospel veiled to those who are perishing?
answer: It is veiled because the god of this world has blinded their unbelieving minds so they are not able to see the light of the gospel.

question: What did Paul and his companions proclaim about Jesus and about themselves?
answer: They proclaimed Christ Jesus as Lord and themselves as the servants of the Corinthian church for Jesus’ sake.

question: Why did Paul and his companions have this treasure in jars of clay?
answer: They had this treasure in jars of clay so that it would be clear that the exceedingly great power belongs to God and not to them.

question: Why did Paul and his companions carry in their bodies the death of Jesus?
answer: They carried the death of Jesus in their bodies so that the life of Jesus might also be shown in their bodies.

question: Who will be raised and brought into the presence of him who raised the Lord Jesus?
answer: Paul and his companions as well as the Corinthian saints will be brought into the presence of him who raised the Lord Jesus.

question: What will happen as a result of grace spreading to many people?
answer: As grace is spread to many people, thanksgiving will increase to the glory of God.

question: Why did Paul and his companions not become discouraged?
answer: They did not become discouraged because inwardly they were being renewed day by day. Also, their momentary, light affliction was preparing them for an eternal weight of glory that exceeds all measurement. Lastly, they were watching for unseen eternal things.

question: Why did Paul and his companions have reason to become discouraged?
answer: They had reason to become discouraged because, outwardly, they were decaying.

question: What did Paul say we still have if our earthly dwelling is destroyed?
answer: Paul said we have a building from God, a house not made by human hands, but an eternal house, in the heavens.

question: Why did Paul say that we groan while we are in this tent?
answer: Paul said this because while in this tent, we are burdened and want to be clothed so that what is mortal may be absorbed by life.

question: What did God give to us as a pledge of what is to come?
answer: God gave us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.

question: Would Paul rather be in the body or at home with the Lord?
answer: Paul said, “We would rather be away from the body and at home with the Lord.”

question: What was Paul’s goal?
answer: Paul made it his goal to please the Lord.

question: Why did Paul make it his goal to please the Lord?
answer: Paul made this his goal because we all must appear before the judgment seat of Christ to receive what is due for the things done in the body, whether for good or for bad.

question: Why did Paul and his companions persuade people?
answer: They persuaded people because they knew the fear of the Lord.

question: Paul said they were not again recommending themselves to the Corinthian saints. What were they doing?
answer: They were giving the Corinthian saints a reason to be proud of them, so that the Corinthian saints might have an answer for those who boasted about appearances but not about what was in the heart.

question: Since Christ died for all, what should those who live do?
answer: They should live no longer for themselves, but for him who died and was raised.

question: By what standards do the saints no longer judge anyone?
answer: The saints no longer judge anyone by human standards.

question: What happens to anyone who is in Christ?
answer: He is a new creation. The old things have passed away; new things have come.

question: When God through Christ reconciles people to himself, what does God do for them?
answer: God does not count their sinful acts against them, and he entrusts to them the message of reconciliation.

question: As appointed representatives of Christ, what is the plea of Paul and his companions to the Corinthians?
answer: Their plea to the Corinthians is to be reconciled to God for the sake of Christ!

question: Why did God make Christ become the sacrifice for our sin?
answer: God did this so that in Christ we might become the righteousness of God.

question: What did Paul and his companions beg the Corinthians not to do?
answer: They begged the Corinthians not to receive the grace of God to no effect.

question: When is the favorable time? When is the day of salvation?
answer: Now is the favorable time. Now is the day of salvation.

question: Why did Paul and his companions not place a stumbling block in front of anyone?
answer: They did not put a stumbling block in front of anyone, for they did not want their ministry to be blamed.

question: What are some of the things that Paul and his companions endured?
answer: They endured affliction, distress, hardship, beatings, imprisonments, riots, hard work, sleepless nights and hunger.

question: What did the actions of Paul and his companions prove?
answer: Their actions proved they were God’s servants.

question: Even though Paul and his companions were truthful, of what were they accused?
answer: They were accused of being deceitful.

question: What exchange does Paul wish to make with the Corinthians?
answer: Paul said his heart was wide open to the Corinthians and, in fair exchange, Paul wanted the Corinthians saints to open their hearts wide to Paul and his companions.

question: What reasons does Paul give as to why the Corinthian saints should not be tied together with unbelievers?
answer: Paul gives the following reasons: What association does righteousness have with lawlessness? Does light have fellowship with darkness? Can Christ agree with Beliar? What share does a believer have together with an unbeliever? Can there be agreement between the temple of God and idols?

question: What does the Lord say he will do for those who will, “Come out from among them and be set apart, and touch no unclean thing…”?
answer: The Lord says he will welcome them. He will be a Father to them and they will be his sons and daughters.

question: Of what does Paul say we are supposed to cleanse ourselves?
answer: We are supposed to cleanse ourselves of everything that makes us unclean in body and spirit.

question: What did Paul want the Corinthian saints to do for himself and his companions?
answer: Paul wanted them to, “Make room for us!”

question: What words of encouragement did Paul have for the Corinthian saints?
answer: Paul told the Corinthian saints they were in his and his companion’s hearts, to die together and to live together. Paul also told them he had great confidence in them and was proud of them.

question: What comfort did God give to Paul and his companions when they came to Macedonia and were troubled in every way–conflicts on the outside and fears on the inside?
answer: God comforted them by the arrival of Titus, by the report of the comfort Titus had received from the Corinthian saints, and by the Corinthian’s great affection and their sorrow and deep concern for Paul.

question: What did Paul’s previous letter produce in the Corinthian saints?
answer: The Corinthian saints experienced grief unto repentance in response to Paul’s previous letter.

question: What did Godly sadness produce in the Corinthian saints?
answer: Sadness brought about repentance in them.

question: Why did Paul say he wrote his previous letter to the Corinthian saints?
answer: Paul said he wrote so that the earnestness of the Corinthians saints for Paul and his companions should be made known to the Corinthian saints in the sight of God.

question: Why was Titus joyful?
answer: He was joyful because his spirit was refreshed by all the Corinthian saints.

question: Why did Titus’ affection for the Corinthian saints grow even greater?
answer: Titus’ affection for the Corinthian saints grew even greater as he remembered the obedience of all the Corinthian saints as they welcomed him with fear and trembling.

question: What did Paul want the Corinthian brothers and sisters to know?
answer: Paul wanted them to know about the grace of God that was given to the churches of Macedonia.

question: What did the churches of Macedonia do during a great test of affliction, and even though were extremely poor?
answer: They produced great riches of generosity.

question: What did Paul urge Titus to do?
answer: Paul urged Titus to bring to completion this act of grace on the part of the Corinthian saints.

question: In what else did the Corinthian believers abound?
answer: They abounded in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in all diligence, and in their love for Paul.

question: What does Paul say is a good and acceptable thing?
answer: Paul says it is a good and acceptable thing for the Corinthian saints to have a readiness to do that work.

question: Does Paul want this task to be done so others may be relieved and the Corinthian saints may be burdened?
answer: No. Paul said the Corinthians’ abundance at that current time would supply what they (the other saints) needed, and so that their abundance might also supply the Corinthian saints’ need, and so that there might be fairness.

question: What did Titus do after God put into his heart the same earnest care that Paul had for the Corinthian saints?
answer: Titus accepted Paul’s appeal, and being very earnest about it, he came to the Corinthian saints of his own free will.

question: What was Paul careful to avoid in his actions concerning this act of generosity?
answer: Paul was careful to avoid giving anyone reason to complain about his actions.

question: What did Paul tell the Corinthian saints to do concerning the brothers that were sent to them by the other churches?
answer: Paul told the Corinthian church to show them their love and to show them why Paul had boasted about the Corinthian church among the other churches.

question: About what does Paul say it is not necessary to write to the Corinthian saints?
answer: Paul says it is no necessary to write to them concerning the ministry for the saints.

question: Why did Paul send the brothers to Corinth?
answer: He sent the brothers so that his boasting about the Corinthian saints might not be futile, and so that the Corinthian saints would be ready, as Paul said they would be.

question: Why did Paul think it necessary to urge the brothers to go to the Corinthian saints and make arrangements in advance for the gift the Corinthians had promised?
answer: Paul thought is necessary so that Paul and his companions would not be put to shame in case any Macedonians came with Paul and found the Corinthians unprepared. Paul wanted the Corinthians to be ready with the gift as one freely offered and not because the Corinthians were forced to give it.

question: What example does Paul use to explain why believers should give generously?
answer: Paul says that people who sow only a little will reap only a little, but those who sow generously will also reap generously.

question: How is each one to give?
answer: Each one is to give as he has planned in his heart—not out of compelling obligation or so as to have sorrow when he gives.

question: What was the one who provides seed for the sower and bread for food going to do for the Corinthian saints?
answer: That one was going to supply and multiply their seed for sowing and increase the harvest of their righteousness. They were going to be enriched in every way so they could be generous.

question: For what reason were the saints in Jerusalem glorifying God?
answer: They were glorifying God because of the Corinthians’ obedience to their confession of the gospel of Christ and because of the generosity of the Corinthians’ gift.

question: Why did the other saints long for the Corinthian saints as they prayed for them?
answer: They longed for them because of the exceedingly great grace of God that was upon the Corinthians.

question: What did Paul beg of the Corinthian saints?
answer: Paul begged of them that when he was present with them, he would not have to be bold with self-confidence.

question: For what occasion did Paul think he would have to be bold with self-confidence?
answer: Paul thought he would have to be bold with self-confidence when he opposed those who supposed that Paul and his companions were living according to the flesh.

question: When Paul and his companions waged war, what kind of weapons did they not use?
answer: Paul and his companions did not use fleshly weapons when they waged war.

question: What did the weapons that Paul used have the power to do?
answer: The weapons Paul used had divine power to destroy strongholds.

question: For what reason did the Lord give Paul and his companions authority?
answer: The Lord gave Paul and his companions authority so they could build up the Corinthian saints and not destroy them.

question: What were some people saying about Paul and his letters?
answer: Some were saying Paul’s letters were serious and powerful, but physically he was weak and his speech was not worth listening to.

question: What did Paul say to those who thought he was much different in person than his letters indicated?
answer: Paul said that what he said by letter when he was away would be the same as he would do when he was there with the Corinthians saints.

question: What did those who praised themselves do to show they had no insight?
answer: They showed they had no insight because they measured themselves by one another and compared themselves with each other.

question: What were the limits of Paul’s boasting?
answer: Paul said his boasting would stay in the area that God had assigned to them, even reaching as far as the Corinthians. Paul said they would not boast about the labor of others, about the work being done in another’s area.

question: What were the specific limits of Paul’s boasting?
answer: Paul said their boasting would stay in the area that God had assigned to them, even reaching as far as the Corinthians. Paul said they would not boast about the labor of others, about the work being done in another’s area.

question: Who is the one who is approved?
answer: The one who is approved is the one the Lord commends.

question: Why did Paul have a godly jealousy for the Corinthian saints?
answer: He was jealous for them because he had promised them in marriage to one husband, to present them as pure virgins for Christ.

question: What was Paul afraid of concerning the Corinthian saints?
answer: Paul was afraid their thoughts might be led astray from a sincere and pure devotion to Christ.

question: What did the Corinthian saints tolerate?
answer: They tolerated someone coming and proclaiming another Jesus, a different gospel than the one Paul and his companions preached.

question: How did Paul preach the gospel to the Corinthians?
answer: Paul preached the gospel freely to the Corinthians.

question: How did Paul “rob” other churches?
answer: He “robbed” them by accepting support from them so he could serve the Corinthians.

question: How does Paul describe those who wish to be found equal to Paul and his companions in the things about which they boast?
answer: Paul describes such people as false apostles, deceitful workers, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ.

question: How does Satan disguise himself?
answer: He disguises himself as an angel of light.

question: Why did Paul ask the Corinthian saints to receive him like a fool?
answer: Paul asked them to receive him like a fool so he could boast a little.

question: With whom did Paul say the Corinthian saints gladly put up?
answer: Paul said they gladly put up with the foolish, with someone who enslaved them, with someone who caused divisions among them, with someone who took advantage of them, with one who put on airs, or one who slapped them in the face.

question: What are Paul’s boasts comparing himself to those who wish to be found equal with Paul in what they boasted about?
answer: Paul boasted that he was a Hebrew, an Israelite and a descendant of Abraham just like those who claimed to be equal to Paul. Paul said he was more a servant of Christ than they were–in even more hard work, in far more prisons, in beatings beyond measure, in facing many dangers of death.

question: What were some of the specific dangers Paul endured?
answer: Paul received five times the “40 lashes minus one” from the Jews. Three times he was beaten with rods. Once he was stoned. Three times he was shipwrecked. He spent a night and a day in the open sea. He was in danger from rivers, from robbers, from his own people, from the Gentiles. He was in danger in the city, in the wilderness, in the sea and in danger from false brothers.

question: According to Paul, what caused him to burn within?
answer: One causing another to fall into sin made Paul burn within.

question: What did Paul say he would boast about, if he had to boast?
answer: Paul said he would boast about what showed his weaknesses.

question: What danger afflicted Paul at Damascus?
answer: The governor of Damascus guarded the city to arrest Paul.

question: About what did Paul say he would now boast?
answer: Paul said he would go on to boast about visions and revelations from the Lord.

question: What happened to the man in Christ 14 years ago?
answer: He was caught up into the third heaven.

question: Why does Paul say it would not be foolish if he boasted?
answer: Paul said it would not be foolish for him to boast because he would be speaking the truth.

question: What happened to Paul to keep him from becoming puffed up?
answer: Paul was given a thorn in the flesh, a messenger from Satan to harass him.

question: What did the Lord tell Paul after Paul asked the Lord to remove his thorn in the flesh?
answer: The Lord told Paul, “My grace is enough for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.”

question: Why did Paul say it was preferable to boast about his weakness?
answer: Paul said it was preferable so that the power of Christ might reside in him.

question: What was performed among the Corinthians with all patience?
answer: Signs wonders and mighty deeds, the true signs of an apostle, were performed among them with all patience.

question: Why did Paul tell the Corinthians he would not be a burden to them?
answer: Paul told them this to show them that he did not want what was theirs. He wanted them.

question: What did Paul say he would most gladly do for the Corinthian saints?
answer: Paul said he would most gladly spend and be spent for their souls.

question: For what purpose did Paul say all these things to the Corinthian saints?
answer: Paul said all these things to build up the Corinthian saints.

question: What was Paul afraid he might find when he went back to the Corinthian saints?
answer: Paul was afraid that among them he would find arguments, jealousy, outbursts of anger, selfish ambition, gossip, pride, and disorder.

question: What was Paul afraid that God might do to him?
answer: Paul was afraid God might humble Paul before the Corinthian saints.

question: For what reason does Paul think he might mourn for many of the Corinthian saints who previously sinned?
answer: Paul was afraid they might not have repented of the impurity and sexual immorality and lustful indulgence which they previously practiced.

question: How many times had Paul already come to the Corinthian saints at the time 2 Corinthians was written?
answer: Paul had already come to them twice at the time 2 Corinthians was written.

question: Why did Paul tell the Corinthians saints who had sinned and all the rest that if he came again, he would not spare them?
answer: Paul told them this because the Corinthian saints were seeking evidence that Christ was speaking through Paul.

question: For what did Paul tell the Corinthian saints to examine and test themselves?
answer: Paul told them to examine and test themselves to see if they were in the faith.

question: What was Paul confident the Corinthian saints would find concerning Paul and his companions?
answer: Paul was confident the Corinthian saints would find that they were not unapproved, but approved by God.

question: What did Paul say that he and his companions were not able to do?
answer: Paul said they were not able to do anything against the truth.

question: Why did Paul write these things to the Corinthian saints while he was away from them?
answer: Paul did this so that when he was with them, he would not have to act harshly toward them.

question: How did Paul want to use the authority the Lord gave him with regard to the Corinthian saints?
answer: Paul wanted to use his authority to build up the Corinthian saints and not tear them down.

question: In concluding, what did Paul want the Corinthians to do?
answer: Paul wanted them to rejoice, to work for restoration, to agree with one another, to live in peace, and to greet each other with a holy kiss.

question: What did Paul want all the Corinthian saints to have with them?
answer: Paul wanted them all to have the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit.

question: By what title does the writer John introduce himself in this letter?
answer: John introduces himself as the elder.

question: To whom is this letter written?
answer: The letter is written to the elect lady and her children.

question: From whom does John say grace, mercy, and peace come?
answer: John says grace, mercy, and peace come from God, the Father, and from Jesus Christ, his Son.

question: Why is John rejoicing?
answer: John is rejoicing because he has found some of the lady’s children walking in the truth.

question: What commandment does John say they have had from the beginning?
answer: The commandment they have from the beginning is that they love one another.

question: What does John say that love is?
answer: Love is to walk according to God’s commandments.

question: What does John call those who do not confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh?
answer: John calls them the deceiver and the antichrist.

question: What does John tell the believers to be careful not to do?
answer: John tells the believers to be careful not to lose what they have worked for.

question: What does John tell the believers to do with anyone who does not bring the true teaching about Christ?
answer: They should not receive anyone who does not bring the true teaching about Christ.

question: Of what is a believer guilty if he receives someone who does not bring the true teaching about Christ?
answer: The believer who receives and greets a false teacher shares in his evil deeds.

question: What does John hope to do in the future?
answer: John hopes to come and speak directly with the elect lady.

question: How was Ahaziah injured?
answer: Ahaziah fell down through the lattice in his upper chamber in Samaria, and was injured.

question: Why was Ahaziah going to certainly die?
answer: Because Ahaziah consulted with Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron, he would certainly die.

question: What did Elijah wear?
answer: Elijah wore a garment made of hair, and he had a leather belt wrapped around his waist.

question: What consumed the captain and his fifty men?
answer: A fire came down from heaven, called by Elijah, and it consumed the captain and his fifty men.

question: How did the third captain approach Elijah?
answer: The third captain went up, fell on his knees before Elijah, and begged him to value his life and the lives of his men.

question: Why did Joram begin to reign in the place of Ahaziah?
answer: Joram began to reign in his place because Ahaziah had no son.

question: When did Elijah leave with Elisha from Gilgal?
answer: When Yahweh was going to take up Elijah by a whirlwind into heaven, Elijah left with Elisha from Gilgal.

question: How did Elisha answer when the sons of the prophets told him that Yahweh would take his master from him?
answer: Elisha answered, “Yes, I know it, but do not talk about it.”

question: Why did the river divide on both sides?
answer: Because Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the water with it, the river divided on both sides.

question: For what did Elisha ask?
answer: Elisha asked for a double portion of Elijah’s spirit to come on him.

question: How did Elijah go up into heaven?
answer: Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

question: What happened when Elisha struck the waters with Elijah’s cloak?
answer: When Elisha had struck the waters, they divided on both sides and Elisha crossed over.

question: What did the sons of the prophets want fifty strong men to do?
answer: They wanted fifty strong men to go and look for Elisha’s master, in case the Spirit of Yahweh had taken him up and thrown him onto some mountain or into some valley.

question: For how long did the fifty men search for Elijah?
answer: The fifty men searched for three days.

question: What was the problem at Jericho?
answer: The water was bad and the land was not fruitful.

question: How was the water healed?
answer: Elisha went out to the spring of water and threw salt in it.

question: When some boys mocked Elisha, what curse happened to them?
answer: When some boys mocked Elisha, two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the boys.

question: How was Joram’s evil different from the evil of his father and his mother?
answer: Joram’s evil was not like his father and his mother, for he removed the sacred stone pillar of Baal that his father had made.

question: Why did King Joram leave Samaria?
answer: King Joram left Samaria to mobilize all Israel for war.

question: What three armies marched around the Sea of the Arabah for seven days?
answer: The armies of Israel, Judah, and Edom marched for seven days.

question: What had Elisha done for Elijah?
answer: Elisha had poured water on the hands of Elijah, acting as his servant.

question: Why did Elisha pay attention to the king of Israel?
answer: Elisha paid attention to the king of Israel because Elisha honored the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.

question: When did the hand of Yahweh come upon Elisha?
answer: When the harpist played, the hand of Yahweh came upon Elisha.

question: When was the country filled with water?
answer: In the morning about the time of offering the grain sacrifice, there came water from the direction of Edom, and the country was filled with water.

question: Who from the Moabites gathered themselves together to fight?
answer: All who were able to put on armor gathered themselves together.

question: What did the Moabites think when they saw the water?
answer: When the Moabites saw the water, they thought the three kings had killed each other.

question: What did the king of Moab do to his oldest son?
answer: He took his oldest son and offered him as a burnt offering upon the wall.

question: What was going to happen to the children of the wife of one of the sons of the prophets?
answer: The creditor was going to take her two children to be his slaves.

question: From where should the woman borrow jars?
answer: The woman should borrow jars from her neighbors.

question: When did the oil stop flowing?
answer: After her son said there were no more jars, the oil stopped flowing.

question: What did the important woman from Shunem and her husband make for Elisha?
answer: They made a little room on the roof for Elisha, with a bed, a table, a seat, and a lamp.

question: What was the woman to be holding in one year’s time?
answer: In one year’s time, she would be holding a son.

question: When did the child develop pain in his head?
answer: When the child went out one day to his father, who was with harvesters, he cried out about pain in his head.

question: Where did the child sit until he died?
answer: The child sat on his mother’s knees until he died.

question: Where was the man of God?
answer: The man of God was at Mount Carmel.

question: When Gehazi asked the woman if everything was alright, what did she answer?
answer: When Gehazi asked the woman if everything was alright, she answered, “It is alright.”

question: What did the woman do when she came to the man of God at the mountain?
answer: When she came to the man of God at the mountain, she caught hold of his feet.

question: What should Gehazi do if he met any man or if anyone greeted him?
answer: If Gehazi met any man or if anyone greeted him, he should not answer him.

question: What did Gehazi lay on the child’s face?
answer: He laid the staff on the child’s face.

question: How did the boy’s body grow warm?
answer: Elisha stretched himself out on the boy, and the boy’s body grew warm.

question: What did the child do before he opened his eyes?
answer: The child sneezed seven times and then opened his eyes.

question: Who gathered wild gourds?
answer: One of the prophets gathered wild gourds.

question: How did Elisha remove the death from the pot?
answer: Elisha threw some flour into the pot.

question: How many people ate the twenty loaves of barley bread?
answer: One hundred people ate the twenty loaves of barley bread.

question: What had Yahweh given to Aram by Naaman?
answer: Yahweh had given deliverance to Aram.

question: Whom did the little girl say would heal her master?
answer: The girl said the prophet who was in Samaria would heal her master.

question: To whom did Naaman take the letter which was from the king of Aram?
answer: Naaman took the letter to the king of Israel.

question: What did the king of Israel think was the reason Naaman came to him for a cure?
answer: The king of Israel thought Naaman was seeking to start an argument with him.

question: What was Naaman told to do to be clean?
answer: Naaman was told to go and wash himself into the Jordan seven times to be clean.

question: How did Naaman think Elisha would heal him?
answer: Naaman thought Elisha would come out to him and stand and call on the name of Yahweh his God, and wave his hand over the place and heal the leprosy.

question: Like what was Naaman’s flesh restored?
answer: Naaman’s flesh was restored again like the flesh of a little boy.

question: After Naaman was healed, what did he know?
answer: After Naaman was healed, he knew that there was no God in all the earth except in Israel.

question: For what did Naaman ask Yahweh to pardon him?
answer: Naaman asked Yahweh to pardon him when he bowed himself in the house of Rimmon to serve his master.

question: According to Gehazi, who came from the hill country of Ephraim?
answer: According to Gehazi, two young men of the sons of the prophets came from the hill country of Ephraim.

question: What did Gehazi hide in the house?
answer: He hid the bags of silver in the house.

question: What happened because Gehazi lied?
answer: Because Gehazi lied, he became a leper.

question: Why did the sons of the prophets want to build a place to live?
answer: The place where they lived with Elisha was too small, so they wanted to build a new place to live.

question: Why was the man who lost the axe head worried?
answer: He was worried because the axe was borrowed.

question: How did Elisha make iron float?
answer: He cut off a stick, threw it in the water, and made the iron float.

question: Who told the king of Israel the words of the king of Aram?
answer: Elisha told the king of Israel the words of the king of Aram.

question: Why was Elisha’s servant worried?
answer: He was worried because he saw a large army with horses and chariots surrounding the city.

question: How did Elisha lead the Arameans to Samaria?
answer: Elisha asked Yahweh to blind them, and then Elisha told them to follow him.

question: Where were the Arameans when Yahweh opened their eyes?
answer: The Arameans were in the middle of the city of Samaria when Yahweh opened their eyes.

question: What did the king of Israel do to the Arameans?
answer: He put bread and water before them, and he sent them away.

question: Why was a donkey’s head sold for eighty pieces of silver?
answer: There was a great famine in Samaria, so a donkey’s head was sold for eighty pieces of silver.

question: What did the woman tell the king was troubling her?
answer: She answered, “This woman said to me, ‘Give your son so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.’ So we boiled my son and ate him, and I said to her on the next day, “Give your son that we may eat him, but she has hidden her son.”

question: When the messenger came to Elisha, what did he tell the elders to do?
answer: When the messenger came to Elisha, he told the elders to shut the door, and hold the door shut against him.

question: What did Elisa say would happen to the captain who did not believe him?
answer: Elisha said the captain would not eat any of the flour or barley.

question: Why did the four men with leprosy go to the army of the Arameans?
answer: They went to the army of the Arameans because they said they might die stayed where they were.

question: Why did the Aramean army think the king of Israel hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians to come against the Arameans?
answer: The Aramean army thought the king of Israel hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians to come against the Arameans because they heard a noise of chariots, and a noise of horses—the noise of another large army approaching.

question: What did the gatekeepers do after they were told that the Arameans had deserted their camp?
answer: The gatekeepers shouted out the news that the Arameans had deserted their camp.

question: What did the king think was the reason the Arameans left their camp?
answer: The king thought they had gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the fields. Then when the Israelites came out of the city, the Arameans would take them alive, and conquer the city.

question: Of what was the road full?
answer: The road was full of clothes and equipment the Arameans had cast away in their hurry.

question: What did the captain say when Elisha told him, “About this time in the gate of Samaria, two measures of barley will be available for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel.”?
answer: The captain said to Elisha, “That could not happen even if Yahweh opened the windows of the sky and sent grain down to us!”

question: Why did the woman whose son Elisha restored to life live in the land of the Philistines seven years?
answer: The woman whose son Elisha restored to life lived in the land of the Philistines seven years because Elisha said Yahweh had called for a famine.

question: Why did the woman go to the king?
answer: The woman went to the king to beg him for her house and for her land.

question: What was Gehazi telling the king when the woman whose son Elisha restored to life arrived?
answer: Gehazi was telling the king how Elisha had restored to life the child who was dead.

question: What did Hazael take with him to give to Elisha?
answer: Hazael took a gift with him of every kind of good thing of Damascus, carried by forty camels.

question: Why did the man of God weep?
answer: The man of God wept because he knew the evil that Hazael would do to the people of Israel.

question: After Hazael told the king of Aram that he would recover, what did he do to King Ben Hadad?
answer: After Hazael told King Ben Hadad that he would recover, he took the blanket and dipped it in water, and spread it on Ben Hadad’s face so that he died.

question: Who was Jehoram’s wife?
answer: Jehoram’s wife was Ahab’s daughter.

question: Why was Yahweh not willing to destroy Judah?
answer: Yahweh was unwilling to destroy Judah because he had told his servant David that his descendants would always be kings.

question: When did Edom revolt from under the hand of Judah?
answer: In Jehoram’s days, Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah.

question: Why did Ahaziah do what was evil in Yahweh’s sight?
answer: Ahaziah did what was evil in Yahweh’s sight, for Ahaziah was a son-in-law to the house of Ahab.

question: Where did King Joram return to be healed of the wounds that the Arameans had given him at Ramah?
answer: King Joram returned to be healed in Jezreel.

question: Why did one of the sons of the prophets take a little bottle of oil in his hand and go to Ramoth Gilead?
answer: He took the bottle of oil and went to Ramoth Gilead to anoint Jehu.

question: Who poured the oil on Jehu’s head?
answer: The prophet poured the oil on Jehu’s head.

question: How would Yahweh avenge the blood of his servants?
answer: If Jehu killed the family of Ahab, Yahweh would avenge the blood of his servants shed by the hand of Jezebel.

question: What was going to happen to Jezebel?
answer: The dogs would eat Jezebel in Jezreel, and there would be no one to bury her.

question: What did the servants of Jehu’s master do after Jehu said he was anointed as king?
answer: After Jehu said he was anointed as king, each of the servants quickly took off his outer garment and put it under Jehu at the top of the steps. They blew the trumpet and said, “Jehu is king.”

question: Why had King Joram gone back to Jezreel?
answer: King Joram had gone back to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds that the Arameans had given him.

question: What did the watchman see the messenger do?
answer: The watchman saw the messenger speak to the men but did not come back ahead of them.

question: How did the watchman know Jehu was driving the chariot?
answer: The watchman knew Jehu was driving the chariot, for he was driving wildly.

question: How did Joram king of Israel ride out to meet Jehu?
answer: Joram king of Israel rode out with Ahaziah king of Judah, each in his chariot, to meet Jehu.

question: What happened after Jehu shot Joram between his shoulders?
answer: After Jehu shot Joram between his shoulders, the arrow went through Joram’s heart, and he sank down in his chariot.

question: What would bring to pass the things that were told would happen by the word of Yahweh?
answer: Taking Joram’s body and throwing him into that field would bring to pass the things that were told would happen by the word of Yahweh.

question: Who was buried in his sepulchre with his fathers in the City of David?
answer: Ahaziah was buried in his sepulchre with his fathers in the City of David.

question: What happened when Jehu came to Jezreel?
answer: When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it, and she painted her eyes, arranged her hair, and looked out the window.

question: Who threw Jezebel down?
answer: Some eunuchs threw Jezebel down.

question: Why could no one bury Jezebel?
answer: When they went to bury her, they found no more of her than the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.

question: What did Jehu’s letter tell the elders and guardians of Ahab’s descendants to do?
answer: It told the elders and guardians of Ahab’s descendants to select the best and most deserving of their master’s descendants and set him on his father’s throne and then defend him.

question: Why did the elders and guardians of Ahab’s descendants not make any man king?
answer: They did not make any man king because they realized that not even the two kings could stand before Jehu.

question: What did the elders and guardians of Ahab’s descendants do to the king’s sons?
answer: They took the king’s sons and killed them, seventy persons, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jehu in Jezreel.

question: Why did Jehu say that no part of Yahweh’s word, the word that he spoke concerning the family of Ahab, would fall to the ground?
answer: Jehu said that no part of Yahweh’s word, the word that he spoke concerning the family of Ahab, would fall to the ground, for Yahweh had done what he spoke about through his servant Elijah.

question: How many brothers of Ahaziah did Jehu meet and kill?
answer: He met and killed forty-two men.

question: Why did Jehu take Jonadab into the chariot?
answer: Jehu took Jonadab into the chariot because Jonadab said his heart was with Jehu, and he gave Jehu his hand.

question: Why did Jehu gather all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers, and all his priests?
answer: He gathered them deceitfully, with the intent to kill the worshipers of Baal.

question: To where did the worshipers of Baal come?
answer: They came into the temple of Baal.

question: What would happen if any of the worshipers of Baal escaped?
answer: If any of the worshipers of Baal escaped, whoever let that man escape, his life would be taken for the life of he who escaped.

question: Into what did the guards and captains make the house of Baal?
answer: They made the house of Baal into a latrine.

question: How did Jehu not leave the sins of Jeroboam?
answer: Jehu did not leave the sins of Jeroboam because he worshiped the golden calves in Bethel and Dan.

question: Why would Jehu’s descendants sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation?
answer: Because Jehu did well in executing what was right in Yahweh’s eyes, and did to the house of Ahab and did all that was in Yahweh’s heart, his descendants would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.

question: Where were the other matters concerning Jehu written?
answer: The other matters concerning Jehu, and all that he did, and all his power, were written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.

question: Who was Athaliah not able to kill?
answer: Athaliah could not kill Joash because the soldiers could not find him.

question: What did the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the guard have to do before they saw the king’s son?
answer: The commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the guard had to make a covenant with Jehoiada and swear an oath in the house of Yahweh. Then he showed them the king’s son.

question: What did the two groups who were not serving on the Sabbath have to do?
answer: The two groups who were not serving on the Sabbath had to guard the house of Yahweh to protect young King Joash.

question: What did Jehoiada hand over to the commanders?
answer: Jehoiada handed over to the commanders the spears and shields that had been King David’s, which were in the house of Yahweh.

question: Why did Athaliah tear her clothes and shout?
answer: Athaliah tore her clothes and shouted because she saw King Joash standing by the pillar.

question: Why was Athaliah killed at the king’s house?
answer: Athaliah was killed at the king’s house, for the priest had said, “Do not let her be killed in the house of Yahweh.”

question: After Jehoiada made a covenant, what did the people do?
answer: After Jehoiada made a covenant, the people tore down the house of Baal, smashed Baal’s altars and his idol figures to pieces, and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal.

question: When Joash sat on the throne of the kings, how did the people respond?
answer: When Joash sat on the throne of the kings, all the people of the land rejoiced.

question: Why did Joash do what was right in the eyes of Yahweh all the time?
answer: Joash did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh all the time, because Jehoiada the priest was instructing him.

question: By what were the people motivated to give money for the temple?
answer: The people were motivated by Yahweh in their hearts to give.

question: Why did Joash tell the priests to take no more money from the taxpayers?
answer: Joash told the priests this because they had not repaired anything in the temple.

question: Who put money into the chest?
answer: The priests who were guarding the temple entrance put into the chest all the money that was brought to the house of Yahweh.

question: For what did the workers use the money?
answer: The workers used the money for buying timber and cutting stone to repair the temple of Yahweh, and for all that was needed to be paid to repair it.

question: Why was the money for the guilt offerings and the money for the sin offerings not brought into the temple of Yahweh?
answer: The money for the guilt offerings and the money for the sin offerings was not brought into the temple of Yahweh, because it belonged to the priests.

question: How did King Joash prevent King Hazael from attacking Jerusalem?
answer: Joash took all the holy objects that Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah had consecrated to Yahweh, his own holy things, and all the gold that was found in the storerooms of the houses of Yahweh and of the king, and he sent them to Hazael, king of Aram. Then Hazael went away from Jerusalem.

question: Who attacked Joash?
answer: Jozacar, the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad, the son of Shomer, his servants, attacked Joash.

question: Why did Yahweh give Israel a rescuer?
answer: Jehoahaz implored Yahweh, so Yahweh gave Israel a rescuer.

question: The king of Aram destroyed the army of Israel and made them like what?
answer: The king of Aram had destroyed the army of Israel and made them like the dust at threshing time.

question: When Elisha was sick, what did he tell Joash to bring?
answer: He told Joash to bring a bow and some arrows.

question: What happened because Joash hit the ground only three times?
answer: Because he hit the ground only three times, he would strike Aram only three times.

question: What happened to the man who was buried in Elisha’s grave?
answer: The man who was buried in Elisha’s grave revived and stood up on his feet as soon as the man touched Elisha’s bones.

question: Why did Yahweh not drive Israel away from his presence?
answer: Yahweh was gracious to Israel and had compassion on them and concern for them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. So Yahweh did not destroy them, and he did not drive them away from his presence.

question: What did Amaziah do as soon as his rule was well established?
answer: As soon as his rule was well established, Amaziah killed the servants who had murdered his father, the king.

question: Why did Amaziah not put the sons of the assassins to death?
answer: Amaziah did not put the sons of the assassins to death because Yahweh had commanded him, saying, “The fathers must not be put to death for their children, neither must the children be put to death for their parents. Instead, every person must be put to death for his own sin.”

question: What trampled down the thistle?
answer: A wild beast in Lebanon trampled down the thistle.

question: What did Jehoash take to Samaria from Jerusalem?
answer: He took all the gold and silver, all the objects that were found in the house of Yahweh, and the valuable things in the king’s palace, and hostages also.

question: How did Amaziah die?
answer: A conspiracy was made against Amaziah in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But men were sent after him to Lachish and they killed him there.

question: What did Uzziah do to Elath?
answer: Uzziah rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah.

question: Through whom did Jeroboam hear that he should restore the border of Israel from Lebo Hamath to the sea of the Arabah?
answer: Jeroboam heard through Jonah the son of Amittai, the prophet, that he should restore the border of Israel from Lebo Hamath to the sea of the Arabah.

question: Because Yahweh saw there was no rescuer for Israel, how did he save them?
answer: Because Yahweh saw there was no rescuer for Israel, Yahweh saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Jehoash.

question: How did Yahweh afflict King Azariah?
answer: Yahweh afflicted the king so that he was a leper to the day of his death and lived in a separate house.

question: Who became king in Azariah’s place?
answer: Jotham, his son, became king in his place.

question: Where did Shallum kill Zechariah?
answer: Shallum killed Zechariah in front of the people.

question: For how long would Jehu’s descendants sit on the throne of Israel?
answer: Jehu’s descendants would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.

question: Why did Shallum reign only one month in Samaria?
answer: Shallum reigned only one month in Samaria because Menahem the son of Gadi killed him.

question: Why did Menahem attack Tiphsah and all who were there?
answer: Menahem attacked Tiphsah and all who were there because they did not open the city up to him.

question: How did Menahem collect the one thousand talents of silver to give Pul?
answer: Menahem collected one thousand talents of silver by requiring each of the wealthy men to pay fifty shekels of silver to him.

question: Who killed Pekahiah?
answer: Pekah killed Pekahiah.

question: Why did Hoshea form a conspiracy against Pekah?
answer: Hoshea formed a conspiracy against Pekah because Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria came and took many cities.

question: Whose example did Jotham follow?
answer: Jotham followed the example of his father, Uzziah.

question: What did Ahaz do to his son?
answer: Ahaz put his son in the fire as a burned offering, following the detestable practices of the nations.

question: What could Rezin not do when he attacked Jerusalem?
answer: When Rezin attacked Jerusalem, he could not conquer Ahaz.

question: What gift did Ahaz give the king of Assyria?
answer: Ahaz took the silver and gold that was found in the house of Yahweh and among the treasures of the king’s palace, and he sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria.

question: What altar did Ahaz want Uriah to replicate?
answer: Ahaz wanted to replicate the altar at Damascus.

question: Who made his burned offering and his grain offering?
answer: The king made his burned offering and his grain offering.

question: What was the purpose of the bronze altar?
answer: The bronze altar was for Ahaz to ask for God’s help.

question: Why did Ahaz remove the covered walkway for the Sabbath that they had built at the temple, along with the king’s entry outside the temple of Yahweh?
answer: Ahaz removed the covered walkway for the Sabbath they had built at the temple, along with the king’s entry outside the temple of Yahweh, to please the king of Assyria.

question: What did Hoshea do when he became Shalmaneser’s servant?
answer: Hoshea became his servant and brought him tribute.

question: How had Hoshea been plotting against Shalmaneser?
answer: Hoshea had been plotting against Shalmaneser, for Hoshea had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt.

question: Why did the captivity happen?
answer: The captivity happened because the people of Israel had sinned against Yahweh their God.

question: What had Yahweh said the Israelites must not do?
answer: Yahweh had said they must not worship idols.

question: By whom had Yahweh testified to Israel and to Judah?
answer: Yahweh had testified to Israel and to Judah by every prophet and every seer.

question: The Israelites were very stubborn like whom?
answer: The Israelites were very stubborn like their fathers who did not trust in Yahweh their God.

question: How did the Israelites sell themselves?
answer: The Israelites sold themselves to do that which was evil in the sight of Yahweh.

question: Why did Yahweh remove Israel from his sight?
answer: The people of Israel followed all the sins of Jeroboam and they did not depart from them, so Yahweh removed Israel from his sight.

question: Why did Yahweh send lions among the new nations in Samaria?
answer: The nations in Samaria did not worship Yahweh, so he sent lions among them.

question: What did the priest teach the new people in Bethel?
answer: The priest taught them how they should fear Yahweh.

question: Where did every ethnic group put the gods they made?
answer: Every ethnic group made gods of their own, and put them in the shrines that the Samaritans had made.

question: Besides their own gods, who did the new nations in Israel honor?
answer: The new nations also honored Yahweh.

question: How did the new people in Israel not honor Yahweh?
answer: The new people did not honor Yahweh, because he commanded that they must not fear other gods.

question: How did the nations in Israel not listen?
answer: They did not listen because they continued to do what they had done in the past.

question: What were the people of Israel doing to the bronze serpent Moses had made?
answer: The people of Israel were burning incense to the bronze serpent Moses had made.

question: For how long did Shalmaneser king of Assyria attack Samaria?
answer: Shalmaneser king of Assyria attacked Samaria for three years.

question: Why did the king of Assyria carry Israel captive away to Assyria?
answer: The king of Assyria carried Israel captive away to Assyria because they disobeyed the solemn agreement that Yahweh had made with their ancestors.

question: From where did Hezekiah get silver to give the king of Assyria?
answer: Hezekiah got silver that was found in the house of Yahweh and in the treasuries of the king’s palace.

question: From where did Tartan and Rabsaris and the chief commander call to King Hezekiah?
answer: They called to King Hezekiah from the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway of the Field of the Fuller.

question: What would happen if a man leaned on Egypt?
answer: If a man leaned on Egypt, it would stick into his hand and pierce it.

question: What wager did the king of Assyria make?
answer: The king of Assyria wagered two thousand horses if Hezekiah was able to find riders for them.

question: What did Yahweh tell the king of Assyria to do?
answer: Yahweh told the king of Assyria to attack Judah and destroy it.

question: In what language did Eliakim, Shebnah, and Joah ask the chief commander to speak?
answer: Eliakim, Shebnah, and Joah asked the chief commander to speak in Aramaic.

question: In what language did the chief commander shout?
answer: The chief commander shouted in the Jews’ language.

question: What would the king of Assyria let those who made peace with him do?
answer: He would let them eat from their own vine and from their own fig tree, and drink from the water in their own cistern.

question: What did King Hezekiah command?
answer: The king commanded the people to not answer the chief commander.

question: What did King Hezekiah do when he heard the report?
answer: When King Hezekiah heard the report, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of Yahweh.

question: What did Hezekiah say Yahweh might do?
answer: Hezekiah said that perhaps Yahweh will punish him for saying those things.

question: What would Yahweh do to stop the king of Assyria?
answer: Yahweh would put a spirit in him, and the king would hear a certain report and go back to his own land.

question: According to Sennacherib, in what way did God deceive Hezekiah?
answer: According to Sennacherib, God deceived Hezekiah by saying Jerusalem would not be given over into the hand of the king of Assyria.

question: Where did Hezekiah spread the letter from the messengers?
answer: Hezekiah spread the letter from the messengers in the house of Yahweh.

question: Why should Yahweh save the people of Judah?
answer: Yahweh should save the people of Judah so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that Yahweh is God alone.

question: Against whom did the king of Assyria raise his voice?
answer: The king of Assyria raised his voice against the Holy One of Israel!

question: Who said he would dry up all the streams of Matsor under the soles of his feet?
answer: Sennacherib said he would dry up all the streams of Matsor under the soles of his feet.

question: Who determined long ago that impregnable cities would be reduced into heaps of ruins?
answer: Yahweh determined long ago that impregnable cities would be reduced into heaps of ruins.

question: What would Yahweh put in Sennacherib’s nose?
answer: Yahweh would put his hook in Sennacherib’s nose.

question: What would be the sign for Hezekiah?
answer: The sign would be that the people of Judah would eat what grows wild, and in the second year what grows from that.

question: Why would Yahweh defend Jerusalem?
answer: Yahweh would defend Jerusalem for his own sake and for his servant David’s sake.

question: How did Yahweh defend Jerusalem?
answer: The angel of Yahweh went out and struck the camp of the Assyrians, putting to death 185,000 soldiers.

question: What did Yahweh tell Hezekiah to do because he would die?
answer: Yahweh told Hezekiah to set his house in order, for he would die.

question: Why was Yahweh about to heal Hezekiah?
answer: Because Yahweh heard Hezekiah’s prayer and saw his tears, he was about to heal him.

question: How did Hezekiah recover?
answer: A lump of figs was put on his boil, and he recovered.

question: How did Yahweh change the shadow?
answer: Yahweh brought the shadow ten steps backward from where it had moved to on the stairway of Ahaz.

question: What did Hezekiah show the messengers from the king of Babylon?
answer: Hezekiah showed them everything in his house and kingdom.

question: What would happen to the sons born from Hezekiah?
answer: The people of Babylon would take away the sons born from him, and they would become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.

question: Why did Hezekiah think that the word of Yahweh was good?
answer: Hezekiah thought that the word of Yahweh was good because there would be peace and stability in his days.

question: What did Manasseh rebuild?
answer: Manasseh rebuilt the shrines that Hezekiah, his father, had destroyed.

question: With whom did Manasseh consult?
answer: Manasseh practiced divination, and he observed signs, and he made a ritual pit and familiar spirits.

question: What did Manasseh place in the house of Yahweh?
answer: Manasseh placed the carved figure of Asherah that he had made in the house of Yahweh.

question: Whom did Manasseh act more wickedly than?
answer: Manasseh acted more wickedly than the Amorites who were before him.

question: Why would the remnant become victims and plunder for all their enemies?
answer: The remnant would become victims and plunder for all their enemies because his people have done things that he has told them are very evil.

question: How much innocent blood did Manasseh shed?
answer: Manasseh shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem from one end to another with death.

question: How did Amon die?
answer: The servants of Amon conspired against him and put the king to death in his own house.

question: Where was Amon buried?
answer: The people buried Amon in his tomb in the garden of Uzza.

question: How did Josiah walk?
answer: Josiah walked in all the ways of David his ancestor, and he did not turn away either to the right or to the left.

question: What did Josiah want Hilkiah to give to the workmen who were in the house of Yahweh?
answer: Josiah wanted Hilkiah to give the money that was brought into the house of Yahweh to the workmen who were in the house of Yahweh.

question: Why was no accounting required for the money that was given to the workmen?
answer: No accounting was required for the money that was given to the workmen, because they handled it faithfully.

question: What did Hilkiah find in the house of Yahweh?
answer: Hilkiah found the Book of the Law in the house of Yahweh.

question: When the king heard the words of the law, what did he do?
answer: When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.

question: Where did Huldah live?
answer: Huldah lived in Jerusalem in the second quarter.

question: Why did Yahweh listen to the king of Judah?
answer: Yahweh listened to the king of Judah because his heart was tender and because he humbled himself before Yahweh and because he tore his clothes and wept before Yahweh.

question: What would the eyes of the king of Judah not see?
answer: His eyes would not see any of the disaster that Yahweh would bring on the place and its inhabitants.

question: In whose hearing did the king read all the words of the book of the covenant?
answer: The king read all the words of the book of the covenant in the hearing of all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the priests, prophets, and all the people, from small to great.

question: What did all the people agree to do?
answer: All the people agreed to obey the covenant.

question: What did the king burn outside Jerusalem in the fields in the Kidron Valley?
answer: The king burned all the vessels that were made for Baal and Asherah, and for all the stars of heaven outside Jerusalem in the fields in the Kidron Valley.

question: What rooms did the king clear out?
answer: The king cleared out the rooms of the male prostitutes who were by the temple of Yahweh.

question: Where were the priests of those shrines where incense was burned allowed to eat unleavened bread?
answer: The priests of those shrines where incense was burned were allowed to eat unleavened bread in Jerusalem.

question: Where were the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun?
answer: The horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun were in an area at the entrance to the temple of Yahweh, near the room of Nathan Melech.

question: Who built the Mount of Destruction?
answer: Solomon king of Israel built the Mount of Destruction.

question: Why did Josiah burn bones on the altar at Bethel?
answer: He burned bones on the altar to defile it.

question: Whose bones did Josiah not move?

question: What did David do after defeating the Amalekites?

question: On the third day, who came to David from Saul’s camp?

question: Where is the funeral song that David sang for Saul and Jonathan written?

question: What was slain on Israel’s high places?

question: Where does the shield of the Saul, the mighty king, remain?

question: What did Saul do for the daughters of Israel?

question: Who went up with David to Hebron?

question: What did the men of Judah do when they came to David?

question: What did Abner do with Ishbosheth, the son of Saul?

question: Who was Abner?

question: Which son of Zeruiah pursued Abner?

question: What happened to Asahel when he refused to stop pursuing Abner?

question: To what location did Joab and Abishai pursue Abner?

question: What did Abner say to stop Joab from pursuing him?

question: Where did Abner and his men travel?

question: Who were David’s first three sons born to him in Hebron?

question: How did David and Abner part ways?

question: Why did David curse Joab for murdering Abner?

question: After Joab killed Abner, what curse did David pronounce on Joab’s family?

question: What did David tell Joab and all the people with him to do?

question: What did David hope for the sons of Zeruiah?

question: What caused Ishbosheth’s hands to become weak?

question: What were the names of two of Ishbosheth’s commanders?

question: How did Rechab and Baanah get into Ishbosheth’s house?

question: What did David have done with the head of Ishbosheth?

question: What did the tribes of Israel say Yahweh had promised David?

question: Who came to Hebron, made a covenant with David, and anointed him king over Israel?

question: How many years did David reign in Jerusalem over all Israel and Judah?

question: By what other names was Jerusalem called?

question: From whom did David capture the stronghold of Zion?

question: Why did David become greater and greater?

question: How many sons were born to David in Jerusalem?

question: What did David do with the Box of God after Uzzah died?

question: Why did David bring the Box of God from Obed Edom’s house to the City of David?

question: What did David do as the Box of God was being brought up?

question: What did David distribute to all the people?

question: What did Michal say to David when he returned home?

question: What was David’s response to Michal’s rebuke?

question: What question did Yahweh ask about the leaders of Israel?

question: Who did Yahweh say would build a house for his name?

question: What did Yahweh say about David’s house and kingdom?

question: After Nathan told David all the words Yahweh had said, what did David do?

question: After hearing the prophecy, what did David say about Yahweh?

question: Why did David say Yahweh had done this great thing and revealed it to him?

question: Why did God go to redeem Israel?

question: Why did David say he had been bold enough to pray like this to Yahweh?

question: What did David say about Yahweh’s words?

question: What did David ask Yahweh to do?

question: What did David gain by attacking and subduing the Philistines?

question: How did David decide which Moabite soldiers would live or die?

question: What happened to the Moabites who were left alive?

question: What did David capture from Hadadezer?

question: What did David do to the Arameans of Damascus when they came to help Hadadezer?

question: What did Toi, king of Hamath, do when he heard that David had defeated Hadadezer’s army?

question: What did David do with the silver and gold from the nations he had subdued?

question: Where did David strike the Arameans?

question: How did David’s sons serve his kingdom?

question: What did David tell Ziba to do for Mephibosheth?

question: Where did Mephibosheth live after David showed him kindness?

question: What physical problem did Mephibosheth have?
answer: Mephibosheth was lame in both of his feet.

question: Who became king of the Ammonites after the former king died?

question: How did David show kindness to Hanun?

question: What did the Ammonite commanders say about David’s show of kindness to Hanun?

question: What did Hanun do to David’s servants?

question: Where did the Ammonites and their hired soldiers position themselves for battle?

question: Why did the Ammonites hire soldiers from other nations?

question: What did David do when he heard that the Ammonites had hired soldiers?
