question: How did Joab prepare for the battle?
answer: Joab chose some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them to meet the Arameans, and he put the rest of the people in the hand of his brother Abishai to meet the Ammonites.

question: What did the Ammonites do when they saw that the Arameans had fled from Joab?
answer: When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they also fled from Abishai and went into the city.

question: What did the Arameans do when they saw they had been defeated by Israel?
answer: The Arameans gathered themselves together again at Helam, and Hadadezer sent for many troops from Aramean kingdoms beyond the Euphrates River.

question: What did David do when he heard that the Arameans had gathered again?
answer: David gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came toward Helam to fight the Arameans.

question: What did all the kings who were servants of Hadadezer do when they saw they were defeated by Israel?
answer: They made peace with Israel and served them. The Arameans would not help the Ammonites anymore after that, because they were afraid of Israel.

question: When did kings normally go out to war?
answer: Kings normally went out to war at the return of the year, in the spring.

question: Where was King David at this time?
answer: David sent out his commander Joab with his officers and the rest of the Israelite army, but David himself stayed in Jerusalem.

question: Who did David see one evening when he was walking on the roof of his palace?
answer: David saw a very beautiful woman bathing, and her name was Bathsheba.

question: Who was Bathsheba’s husband?
answer: Bathsheba’s husband was Uriah the Hittite.

question: What did David do with Bathsheba?
answer: David sent for her, he had sexual relations with her, and she became pregnant.

question: After David found out Bathsheba was pregnant, what did he do?
answer: He told Joab to send Uriah the Hittite to him.

question: When Uriah came to David, what did David try to get him to do?
answer: David tried to get Uriah to go down to his house and relax for a while.

question: What did Uriah do after David told him to go to his house?
answer: Uriah did not go to his house, but instead slept at the entrance of the king’s house with all the servants of his master.

question: Why did Uriah say he would not go to his own house?
answer: Uriah said he would never go to his house to eat, drink, and lie with his wife while the Box, Israel, and Judah were dwelling in tents, and Joab and his men were camping in the open field.

question: What did David’s letter to Joab say?
answer: The letter said to put Uriah in the front of the strongest battle and then to retreat from him so he would be struck and die.

question: What did Joab think might happen when his messenger brought news of the war to David?
answer: Joab thought David might become angry because he had allowed the Ammonites to kill some of his soldiers.

question: What news did Joab think David might be angry about?
answer: Joab thought David might be angry that soldiers got so close to the city to fight because the Ammonite soldiers would shoot arrows at them from the top of the city wall.

question: What did Joab tell the messenger to say if David got angry?
answer: Joab told the messenger to say that his servant Uriah the Hittite was also dead.

question: What did David tell the messenger to say to Joab?
answer: David told the messenger to encourage Joab by telling him to not feel badly since no one ever knows who might die in a battle. David advised him to strengthen his battle against the city and destroy it.

question: What did Uriah’s wife do when she heard that her husband was dead?
answer: When she heard her husband was dead, she mourned for him.

question: What happened to Bathsheba?
answer: After her mourning passed, David sent for her, and she became his wife, and she bore him a son.

question: Who was displeased with what David had done?
answer: Yahweh was very displeased with what David had done.

question: What was Nathan’s story about?
answer: The story was about a rich man with many flocks and herds and a poor man who had only one little ewe lamb that was like a daughter to him.

question: Why did Nathan go to David?
answer: Nathan went to David because Yahweh sent him.

question: What did the rich man do with the poor man’s lamb?
answer: When a traveler came to the rich man, he took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it as a meal for his guest.

question: What was David’s reaction to Nathan’s story?
answer: David was very angry and said that he wanted to execute the man who did that.

question: What did Nathan tell David after David reacted in anger?
answer: Nathan told David, “You are the man.”

question: What did Yahweh say David had done?
answer: Yahweh said David had struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword, had taken his wife to be his own wife, and had murdered him with the sword of the Ammonites. Yahweh said that David did not take seriously what he commanded when he said that his people must not commit adultery or murder. David did things that Yahweh considers to be very evil!

question: What did Yahweh say would happen because David despised him and took Uriah’s wife?
answer: Yahweh said that he would make someone from David’s own family cause disaster for him. Yahweh would take David’s wives away from him and give them to that person instead. He will have sexual relations with them in public.

question: After he confessed his sin, what did Nathan say would happen to David?
answer: Nathan told David that Yahweh had taken away his sin and that he would not die.

question: What did Nathan say would happen to the son born to David?
answer: Nathan said that because David had shown great contempt for Yahweh by doing this, the son born to him would surely die.

question: What did David do when the child was very sick?
answer: David prayed to God that the child would not die, fasted, and went in and slept on the floor of his room.

question: When did the child die?
answer: The child died on the seventh day.

question: What did David do once he knew the child was dead?
answer: David arose from the ground, washed and anointed himself, changed his clothes, and went to the house of Yahweh and prostrated himself. Then he asked his servants for food and he ate it.

question: Why did David stop fasting after the child died?
answer: David reasoned that there was no reason to fast since he could not bring the child back again.

question: Why did Yahweh send word through Nathan to name the new son Jedidiah?
answer: Yahweh said to name him Jedidiah because of Yahweh.

question: Against whom was Joab fighting at this time?
answer: Joab was fighting against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon.

question: Why did Joab tell David to gather the rest of the army and capture the city?
answer: Joab did not want to capture the city himself, because if he did, it would renamed to honor him and not King David.

question: What did David make the people of Rabbah do after he captured the city?
answer: David brought out the people and set them to work with saws, iron picks, and iron axes. David’s troops also forced them to make bricks.

question: To whom was Amnon, the son of David, attracted?
answer: Amnon loved his beautiful half-sister Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom.

question: How did Amnon respond when Jonadab asked him why he was so weak?
answer: Amnon told Jonadab that he loved Tamar, his brother Absalom’s sister.

question: What did Amnon do to get to see Tamar?
answer: Amnon pretended to be sick, and when David came to see him, he asked David to let Tamar come and make food for him so he could eat from her hand.

question: What did Amnon do when Tamar came to feed him?
answer: When Tamar came to feed him, he seized her and told her to come and lie with him.

question: What did Amnon do when Tamar begged him not to force her?
answer: He refused to do what she said he should do. He was stronger than she was, so he forcibly had sexual relations with her.

question: How did Amnon feel toward Tamar after he raped her?
answer: Amnon hated her with a very great hatred that was greater than the love with which he had loved her.

question: What did Amnon command Tamar to do?
answer: Amnon commanded Tamar to leave.

question: What did Amnon order his servant to do?
answer: He ordered his servant to send Tamar outside and to lock the door behind her.

question: What did Tamar do after she was put out of Amnon’s room?
answer: Tamar tore the long robe that she was wearing. She put ashes on her head, and she put her hand on her head. As she went away, she kept screaming.

question: What was King David’s response when he heard about these things?
answer: When King David heard all these things, it made him very angry, but he did nothing about it.

question: How did Absalom feel toward Amnon after he raped Tamar?
answer: Absalom hated Amnon because he had humbled his sister Tamar.

question: Whom did Absalom invite to visit him at Baal Hazor?
answer: Absalom invited the king and all the king’s sons to visit him.

question: What did the king say in response to Absalom’s invitation?
answer: The king said they should not all go because they would be a heavy burden to Absalom.

question: What did David say when Absalom asked him to let Amnon go with them?
answer: But the king replied, “You do not need to invite him to the celebration either.”

question: Who went with Absalom?
answer: Absalom urged David, so he sent Amnon and all the king’s sons with him.

question: What did Absalom command his servants to do to Amnon?
answer: Absalom commanded his servants to kill Amnon when Amnon began to be drunk with wine.

question: What did the king’s sons do after Absalom’s servants killed Amnon?
answer: All the king’s sons arose, and they got onto their mules and escaped by riding away fast.

question: What was the first news David heard about the incident?
answer: The first report to David said that Absalom had killed all the king’s sons and not one was still alive.

question: What did Jonadab say had happened and why?
answer: Jonadab said that only Amnon is dead. Absalom has been determined to kill him ever since the day that Amnon raped his sister Tamar.

question: Where did Absalom go after having Amnon killed?
answer: Absalom fled to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur.

question: How long was Absalom in Geshur?
answer: Absalom was in Geshur for three years.

question: What did King David intend to do?
answer: King David had intended to attack Absalom and punish him for killing Amnon.

question: What did Joab do when he knew the king’s heart was against Absalom?
answer: Joab sent to Tekoa and brought a wise woman from there to act as if she had been in mourning for a long time.

question: What did Joab want the wise woman to do?
answer: Joab wanted the wise woman to pretend to be a mourner and to go speak to the king the words Joab told her to say.

question: When the wise woman went to the king, whom did she say she was?
answer: The wise woman told the king she was a widow.

question: What did the wise woman tell the king her two sons had done?
answer: She told the king that her two sons fought in a field, and one struck the other and killed him.

question: What did the wise woman tell the king she was afraid would happen to her remaining son?
answer: She said she was afraid the whole clan would kill her remaining son, destroying her heir and leaving no descendants to preserve her family’s name.

question: Why did the wise woman ask the king to remember Yahweh his God?
answer: She asked the king to remember Yahweh so that the avenger of blood would not destroy her son.

question: Who did the king swear by when he told the woman that not one hair of her son would fall to the ground?
answer: The king swore by the life of Yahweh.

question: Why did the woman say the king had been doing the wrong thing?
answer: The woman said the king was acting badly because he had not brought back his own banished son.

question: What did the woman say God does instead of taking away life?
answer: She said that God forgives people who have sinned against him so that they can once more be in a good relationship with him.

question: Why did the woman say she came to speak to the king?
answer: She said she came because the people had frightened her, and she hoped the king would listen and deliver her.

question: What did the woman say about the king?
answer: She said that what the king says will comfort her, because he is like an angel of God, and he knows how to determine what is right and what is wrong.

question: What did the king ask the woman?
answer: The king asked the woman if Joab arranged for her to do all this.

question: Why did Joab have the woman go to the king?
answer: Joab did that to try to get David to feel differently about this matter.

question: What did Joab do when the king told him to bring Absalom back?
answer: Joab lay facedown on the ground in honor and gratitude to the king.

question: What instructions did the king give about Absalom?
answer: The king said that Absalom could return to his own house but could go and speak with the king.

question: What was notable about Absalom’s appearance?
answer: He was so handsome that people throughout Israel praised Absalom for being a very handsome man. He did not seem to have any flaws in any part of his body. His hair was long, thick, and heavy.

question: How long did Absalom live in Jerusalem without seeing the king’s face?
answer: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years, during which David still did not allow Absalom to come and speak with him.

question: What did Absalom tell his servants to do after Joab refused to come to him?
answer: Absalom told his servants to go and burn Joab’s barley field with fire.

question: What did Absalom want Joab to do?
answer: Absalom wanted Joab to go to the king and ask why he had come from Geshur, and to say that he wanted to come and speak with him.

question: What did the king do when Absalom bowed before him?
answer: The king kissed Absalom on the cheek to show that he was no longer hostile to him.

question: What did Absalom prepare for himself?
answer: Absalom prepared a chariot and horses for himself.

question: Who ran before Absalom’s chariot?
answer: He hired fifty men to run in front of his chariot.

question: Whom would Absalom call to as he stood by the gate?
answer: Absalom would call to any man who had a dispute and was coming to the king for judgment.

question: What would Absalom say about the cases of the men who came for judgment?
answer: Absalom would say to them that their matter was good and right, but the king is not able to decide everyone’s case, and he has not appointed anyone else to judge cases for people like you.

question: Why did Absalom say he wished he were a judge in the land?
answer: Absalom said he wished he were a judge so that every person with a dispute could come to him and he would give them justice.

question: What did Absalom do when a man approached to prostrate himself?
answer: Absalom would stretch out his hand, hold the man up, and kiss him on the cheek.

question: What did Absalom steal from the men of Israel?
answer: Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel. The Israelites began to wish that Absalom were their king instead of David.

question: What reason did Absalom give the king for needing to go to Hebron?
answer: Absalom said he had to go to Hebron to fulfill a vow he had made to Yahweh.

question: What did the spies that Absalom sent throughout Israel say?
answer: The spies said that when people heard the sound of the shofar, they should say that Absalom has become the king at Hebron.

question: Did the two hundred men who went with Absalom to Hebron know of his plans?
answer: No, the two hundred men came because he had invited them to the feast he was going to host there. They were not part of his conspiracy. They knew nothing about what he was planning to do.

question: What did David tell his servants to do after a messenger told him that the hearts of the men of Israel were behind Absalom?
answer: David told his servants in Jerusalem to arise and flee, because there would be no escape from Absalom.

question: Whom did the king leave behind in Jerusalem to keep the house?
answer: The king left ten women, who were concubines, to keep the house.

question: Who marched with the king as he left Jerusalem?
answer: All his servants, all the Cherethites, all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites—600 men from Gath—marched with him.

question: What did Ittai the Gittite tell the king after the king told him to return?
answer: Ittai swore that he would go wherever the king would go, and he would fight to defend David even if he had to die doing that.

question: Which way did David and all those with him go as they left Jerusalem?
answer: Since Absalom would be coming from the southwest, the king and the others crossed the Kidron Valley and then went up the hill on the road that goes through the desolate area east of Jerusalem.

question: What did the king tell Zadok the priest to do with the Box of God?
answer: The king told Zadok to take the Box of God back to the city.

question: Why was David going to wait at the fords of the wilderness?
answer: He was going to wait there until a word came from the priests to tell him what to do.

question: What did David pray when he was told that Ahithophel was with Absalom?
answer: David prayed that Yahweh would make Ahithophel give Absalom bad advice.

question: Who did David meet at the top of the Mount of Olives?
answer: David unexpectedly met Hushai the Archite, who had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show that he was very sad.

question: What did David want Hushai the Archite to do for him?
answer: David wanted Hushai to return to the city and offer to be Absalom’s servant so he would be able to counter any good advice that Ahithophel would give to Absalom.

question: To whom did David want Hushai to report everything he heard in the king’s palace?
answer: David wanted Hushai to report everything to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

question: What did Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, bring to David?
answer: Ziba brought a pair of saddled donkeys, 200 loaves of bread, 100 clusters of raisins, 100 summer fruits, and a skin of wine.

question: According to Ziba, why did Mephibosheth stay in Jerusalem?
answer: Ziba said Mephibosheth stayed because he said that the house of Israel would return the kingdom of his father to him that day.

question: What did the king say now belonged to Ziba?
answer: The king told Ziba that all that belonged to Mephibosheth was now his.

question: What did Shimei do to David and all the king’s officials?
answer: Shimei came out cursing, and he threw stones at David and all the servants of King David.

question: What did Shimei call David?
answer: Shimei called David a man of blood and a man of wickedness.

question: What did David hope Yahweh would do in response to Shimei’s cursing?
answer: David hoped that Yahweh would look at his affliction and return good to him in place of the cursing.

question: When Absalom came to Jerusalem, what did Hushai say to him?
answer: Hushai said to Absalom, “May the king live! May the king live!”

question: To whom did Hushai tell Absalom he would belong?
answer: Hushai told Absalom that he would belong to the one whom Yahweh, the people, and every man of Israel had chosen.

question: What did Ahithophel advise Absalom to do?
answer: Ahithophel advised Absalom to go in to his father’s concubines whom David had left to keep the house.

question: How was Ahithophel’s counsel viewed?
answer: The counsel of Ahithophel was viewed as if God himself had recommended it.

question: What did Ahithophel advise Absalom and all the elders of Israel about how he should attack David?
answer: Ahithophel’s advice was to let him lead a large army carry out a surprise attack on David that night, when he was weary and weak, kill only David, and bring back all the rest of the people for Absalom to rule.

question: What was Hushai’s opinion of Ahithophel’s plan?
answer: Hushai said that the counsel Ahithophel had given on this occasion was not good.

question: Why did Hushai say the plan was not good?
answer: Hushai said that David and his very brave warriors were probably in a safe place, and David’s soldiers will certainly kill some of Ahithophel’s soldiers at the start of the battle. When people hear about that, they will say that David’s soldiers are slaughtering Absalom’s soldiers! Then your other soldiers, even if they are as fearless as lions, will become very afraid.

question: What did Hushai advise Absalom to do?
answer: Hushai advised Absalom to gather all of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and for Absalom himself to go into the battle. He said that this great army would overwhelm David’s smaller army and none of them would survive.

question: How did Absalom and the men of Israel respond to Hushai’s advice?
answer: They said the counsel of Hushai was better than the counsel of Ahithophel and they decided to do what Hushai suggested.

question: What message did Hushai send to David?
answer: The message was that David should not stay at the place where people can walk across the Jordan River but should cross over immediately, because otherwise, Absalom and his army may come and kill them.

question: How was information relayed to King David?
answer: A maidservant of the two priests would go and declare news to Jonathan and Ahimaaz, and they would go and declare it to King David.

question: What did Jonathan and Ahimaaz do when a young man saw them and told Absalom?
answer: The two of them went quickly to the house of a man in Bahurim and went down into a well in his courtyard.

question: How were the two men helped?
answer: The man’s wife spread a covering over the well and spread grain on it, and when Absalom’s servants asked where the men were, she told them they had crossed the brook.

question: After Absalom’s men left, what did the two men do?
answer: They came up from the well, went and reported the news to King David, and told him to get all these people across the Jordan River quickly.

question: What did Ahithophel do when he saw that his counsel was not followed?
answer: Ahithophel saddled his donkey, went to his house, gave to his family instructions about what to do with his possessions, and then he hanged himself because he knew that otherwise David would kill him as a traitor.

question: How were David and his people cared for in the wilderness?
answer: Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai brought beds, basins, pottery, and all kinds of food for David and the people with him to eat.

question: What did King David tell the army?
answer: King David told the army that he would also go out with them himself.

question: What was the response from the men in the army to King David?
answer: The men told King David not to go out, because he was worth ten thousand of them, and it was better for him to be ready to help them from the city.

question: What instructions did the king give his commanders about Absalom?
answer: The king told the commanders not to harm the young man Absalom for his sake.

question: What was the outcome of the battle in the Forest of Ephraim?
answer: The people of Israel were struck down before the servants of David, and more of Absalom’s soldiers died because of accidents in the forest than the number of them whom David’s soldiers killed in the battle.

question: What happened to Absalom when the mule he was riding ran under the thick branches of a large oak tree?
answer: Absalom’s head was caught in the oak tree. The mule kept going, and that left Absalom dangling in the air.

question: Why was Joab upset with the man who saw Absalom?
answer: Joab was upset because the man did not kill Absalom immediately.

question: Why did the man refuse to kill Absalom?
answer: He refused because he had heard the king command his commanders to keep from hurting the young man Absalom.

question: What did Joab do to Absalom?
answer: Joab took three spears and thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.

question: What was done with Absalom’s body?
answer: They threw Absalom’s body into a great pit in the forest and set up a very great heap of stones over him.

question: Why had Absalom set up a pillar for himself in the Valley of the King while he was alive?
answer: Absalom set up a pillar to make his name remembered, because he said he had no son to make people remember his name.

question: Why did Joab tell Ahimaaz not to run to the king with the news?
answer: Joab told him not to bring the news that day because the king’s son was dead.

question: Why did Ahimaaz still run and tell David the news?
answer: Ahimaaz insisted on running after the Cushite, even though Joab told him there was no reward for the news, so Joab told him to go.

question: What did the king think when the watcher reported a lone runner?
answer: The king said that if the man was by himself, that indicates that he is bringing news.

question: What did the king think when the watcher reported another lone runner?
answer: The king said that this one was also bringing news.

question: What did the king think when the watcher identified the first runner as Ahimaaz?
answer: The king said that he was a good man and came with good news.

question: What news did Ahimaaz bring to the king?
answer: Ahimaaz told the king that Yahweh had defeated the men who had lifted their hand against the king.

question: How did Ahimaaz answer when the king asked about Absalom?
answer: Ahimaaz said he saw a great tumult but did not know what it was about.

question: What was the Cushite’s answer when the king asked about Absalom?
answer: The Cushite said that he wished that what happened to Absalom would happen to all of David’s enemies and to anyone who rebels against him.

question: How did the king respond to the news of his son’s death?
answer: The king trembled, went up to the upper room of the gate, and wept, wishing he had died in place of his son.

question: Why did the victory that day turn into mourning for all the people?
answer: The victory turned into mourning because the people heard that the king was grieved because of his son.

question: What was the king’s cry?
answer: The king cried, “My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”

question: What did Joab say would have pleased the king?
answer: Joab said that he could see that if Absalom were still alive and all of David’s men were dead today, David would like that better.

question: What did Joab tell the king would happen if he did not go out and speak to his servants?
answer: Joab swore by Yahweh that if the king did not go out, all his soldiers will have abandoned him by tomorrow morning.

question: When did all the people come before the king?
answer: All the people came before the king after they were told that the king was sitting in the gate.

question: What were the people in the tribes of Israel arguing about?
answer: The people were arguing about what they should do now that Absalom was dead and David had left Israel to escape from Absalom.

question: Whom did King David send to speak to the elders of Judah?
answer: David sent Zadok and Abiathar the priests to speak to the elders of Judah.

question: Whom did David say would be the commander of his army in place of Joab?
answer: David said Amasa would be the commander of the army in place of Joab.

question: Why did the men of Judah come to Gilgal?
answer: The men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and to bring him across the Jordan.

question: Who rushed to the Jordan to meet the king?
answer: Shimei, with 1,000 men from Benjamin, and Ziba, with his 15 sons and 20 servants, rushed to the Jordan.

question: Why did Shimei say he was the first from the house of Joseph to meet the king?
answer: Shimei came first because he knew that he had sinned against the king.

question: What did the king say to Shimei after Abishai said Shimei should be put to death?
answer: The king told Shimei that he would not die, and he swore an oath to him.

question: How did Mephibosheth look when he came to meet the king?
answer: Mephibosheth had not cared for his feet, trimmed his mustache, or washed his clothes from the day the king went away.

question: What reason did Mephibosheth give for not going with the king?
answer: Mephibosheth told the king that his servant, Ziba, had deceived him and left without him, and Mephibosheth could not follow him because he was crippled.

question: What else did Mephibosheth say Ziba had done to him?
answer: Mephibosheth said Ziba had lied about him to the king.

question: How did Mephibosheth reply when the king said he and Ziba should divide the field?
answer: Mephibosheth told the king to let Ziba take the whole field, because all that mattered to him was that the king had returned safely.

question: What had Barzillai done for the king?
answer: Barzillai had provided all of the food that the king and his soldiers needed while they were at Mahanaim.

question: Why did Barzillai say he should not go to Jerusalem with the king?
answer: Barzillai said he was too old, could no longer taste what he ate or drank, could not hear singers, and would be a burden to the king.

question: What did Barzillai request of the king?
answer: Barzillai asked to return to his own city to die, but he asked the king to take his servant Chimham and do for him what was good in the king’s eyes.

question: Who crossed over to Gilgal with the king?
answer: Chimham, all the people of Judah, and also half the people of Israel crossed over to Gilgal with the king.

question: Why did the men of Israel say they had more right to David than the men of Judah?
answer: The men of Israel said they had more right to David because they represented ten tribes that were related to the king. The men of Judah represented only one tribe. Also, the people of Judah had started the rebellion against David.

question: Whose words were harsher, the men of Judah or the men of Israel?
answer: The word of the men of Judah was harsher than the word of the men of Israel.

question: Why was Sheba called a man of wickedness?
answer: He was called a man of wickedness because he blew a shofar and told the men of Israel to return home; he said David did not belong to them at all.

question: How was the response of the men of Judah to Sheba different from the men of Israel?
answer: The men of Judah clung to their king, but the men of Israel did what Sheba had said and returned to their homes.

question: How did David’s relationship with his ten concubines change?
answer: He put them in another residence where someone guarded them. They had to stay in that house until they died. David provided what they needed, but he never had sexual relations with them again.

question: What did the king tell Amasa to do?

question: What was created through Jesus Christ and for him?
answer: All things were created through Jesus Christ and for him.

question: How did God reconcile all things to himself?
answer: God reconciled all things to himself when he made peace through his Son’s blood.

question: What relationship did the Colossians have with God before they believed the gospel?
answer: Before believing the gospel, the Colossians were separated from God and were his enemies.

question: What must the Colossians continue to do?
answer: The Colossians must continue to be settled in the faith and confident of the gospel.

question: For whose sake is Paul suffering, and what is his attitude?
answer: Paul is suffering for the sake of the church, and he rejoices in it.

question: What is the mystery that was hidden for ages but now has been revealed?
answer: The mystery that was hidden for ages but now has been revealed is Christ in you, the confidence of glory.

question: What is the goal for which Paul is admonishing and teaching every man?
answer: Paul’s goal is to present every person complete in Christ.

question: What is the mystery of God?
answer: The mystery of God is Christ.

question: What is hidden in Christ?
answer: All the hidden treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Christ.

question: What is Paul concerned that might happen to the Colossians?
answer: Paul is concerned that the Colossians might be deceived with persuasive speech.

question: What does Paul call the Colossians to do now that they have received Christ Jesus?
answer: Paul calls the Colossians to walk in Christ Jesus in the same way that they received him.

question: Upon what are the empty deceits that Paul is concerned about based?
answer: The empty deceits are based upon human tradition and the sinful belief systems of the world.

question: What lives in Christ?
answer: All the fullness of God’s nature lives in Christ.

question: Who is the head of all rule and authority?
answer: Christ is the head of all rule and authority.

question: What is removed through the circumcision of Christ?
answer: The sinful body of flesh is removed through the circumcision of Christ.

question: What happens in baptism?
answer: A person is buried with Christ in baptism.

question: What is a person’s condition before Christ makes him alive?
answer: A person is dead in his sins before Christ makes him alive.

question: What did Christ do with the record of debts charged against us?
answer: Christ removed the record of debts and nailed it to the cross.

question: What did Christ do with the rulers and authorities?
answer: Christ removed the rulers and authorities, openly exposed them, and led them as his captives in a victory procession.

question: What does Paul say are a shadow of the things to come?
answer: Paul says that food, drink, feast days, and Sabbaths are a shadow of the things to come.

question: To what reality do the shadows point?
answer: The shadows point to the reality of Christ.

question: From what does the whole body grow with the growth from God?
answer: The whole body holds fast to Christ, the head, to grow with the growth from God.

question: What kinds of commandments does Paul say are part of the world’s beliefs?
answer: Commandments to not handle, not taste, and not touch are part of the world’s beliefs.

question: Against what do the rules of man-made religion have no value?
answer: The rules of man-made religion have no value against the indulgence of the flesh.

question: What should believers seek, and what should they not seek?
answer: Believers should seek the things above and not the things of the earth.

question: To where has Christ been raised?
answer: Christ has been raised to sit at the right hand of God.

question: Where has God put the believer’s life?
answer: God has hidden the believer’s life in Christ.

question: What will happen to the believer when Christ is revealed?
answer: When Christ is revealed, the believer will also be revealed with him in glory.

question: What must the believer put to death?
answer: The believer must put to death the sinful desires of the earth.

question: What happens to those who are disobedient to God?
answer: The wrath of God comes upon those who are disobedient to God.

question: What are some of the things that Paul says the believers must get rid of, which are part of the old self?
answer: The believers must get rid of wrath, anger, evil intentions, insults, and obscene speech.

question: In whose image is the believer’s new self created?
answer: The believer’s new self is created in the image of Christ.

question: What are some of the things that Paul says the believers must put on, which are part of the new self?
answer: The believers must put on a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, meekness, and patience.

question: In what way should the believer forgive?
answer: The believer should forgive in the same way that the Lord has forgiven him.

question: What is the bond of perfection among believers?
answer: Love is the bond of perfection.

question: What should the believer give to God in his attitude, song, word, and deed?
answer: In his attitude, song, word, and deed, the believer should give thanks to God.

question: What should rule in the believer’s heart?
answer: The peace of Christ should rule in the believer’s heart.

question: What should live in the believer richly?
answer: The word of Christ should live in the believer richly.

question: How should a wife respond to her husband?
answer: A wife should submit to her husband.

question: How should a husband treat his wife?
answer: A husband should love his wife and not be bitter against her.

question: How should a child treat his parents?
answer: A child should obey his parents in all things.

question: What should a father not do to his children?
answer: A father should not provoke his children.

question: For whom are believers working in whatever they do?
answer: Believers are working for the Lord in whatever they do.

question: What will those receive who serve the Lord in whatever they do?
answer: Those who serve the Lord in whatever they do will receive the reward of the inheritance.

question: What will those receive who do unrighteousness?
answer: Those who do unrighteousness will receive the penalty for what they did.

question: What does Paul remind earthly masters that they also have?
answer: Paul reminds earthly masters that they also have a master in heaven.

question: In what does Paul want the Colossians to continue steadfastly?
answer: Paul wants the Colossians to continue steadfastly in prayer.

question: For what does Paul want the Colossians to pray?
answer: Paul wants the Colossians to pray that he has an open door to speak the word, the mystery of Christ.

question: How does Paul instruct the Colossians to treat those who are outsiders?
answer: Paul instructs them to live in wisdom, and speak with grace toward those who are outsiders.

question: What task had Paul given Tychicus and Onesimus?
answer: Paul gave them the task of making everything known concerning him to the Colossians.

question: What instructions did Paul give concerning Mark, the cousin of Barnabas?
answer: Paul told the Colossians to receive Mark if he comes to them.

question: For what does Epaphras pray for the Colossians?
answer: He prays that the Colossians will stand complete and fully assured in all the will of God.

question: What is the name of the physician that is with Paul?
answer: The physician’s name is Luke.

question: In what kind of place was the church in Laodicea meeting?
answer: The church in Laodicea was meeting in a house.

question: To what other church had Paul also written a letter?
answer: Paul also had written a letter to the church in Laodicea.

question: How did Paul show that this letter was actually from him?
answer: Paul wrote his name in his own handwriting at the end of the letter.

question: Where was Moses when he spoke to Israel?
answer: Moses was east of the Jordan in the wilderness, in the plain of the Jordan River valley.

question: When did Moses speak to the people of Israel, telling them all that Yahweh commanded him?
answer: Moses spoke to the people in the fortieth year after they had left Egypt.

question: To whom had Yahweh promised to give the land?
answer: Yahweh had promised to give the land to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to their descendants.

question: Why did Moses feel he could not govern the people alone?
answer: There were too many of them since God had multiplied them and made them as numerous as the stars of the heavens.

question: Who would help Moses solve all the problems and disputes of the people?
answer: The people would choose wise, understanding, and well-known men from each tribe and appoint these men leaders to help Moses.

question: What did Moses command the judges to do?
answer: He commanded them to hear and judge righteously concerning the quarrels and cases the Israelites had with each other or with any foreigner who lived among them.

question: Where did Israel travel through as they journeyed from Horeb to the hill country?
answer: They traveled through all the great and terrible wilderness.

question: What did the people ask Moses to do before they would enter the land?
answer: They asked Moses to send men ahead to explore the land and report back about it.

question: Who did Moses choose to scout out the land?
answer: He chose one man from each of the 12 tribes.

question: What did the men report back about the land?
answer: They reported that the land that Yahweh was giving them was good.

question: What were the people grumbling against Yahweh about?
answer: They said Yahweh hated them and he brought them out of the land of Egypt to destroy them.

question: What did the spies say about the people of the land?
answer: They said that the people of the land were stronger and taller than the Israelites and had fortified cities.

question: What did Moses say was the reason the people did not need to be afraid?
answer: He told them not to be afraid, because Yahweh would go before them and would fight for them like he did in Egypt and in the wilderness.

question: What did Yahweh say when he became angry?
answer: He said that not one of these men would see the good land except Caleb.

question: What did Yahweh tell Moses to do for Joshua, the son of Nun?
answer: Yahweh told Moses to encourage Joshua for he would lead Israel to occupy the land.

question: Who did Yahweh say will go into the land and possess it?
answer: He said their children will go in and will possess the land.

question: What did the people do when Yahweh told them not to attack the hill country?
answer: They were arrogant and went up to the hill country to fight anyway.

question: Where did Moses say they journeyed?
answer: They journeyed into the wilderness on the way to the Sea of Reeds.

question: What did Yehweh command the people to be careful not to do?
answer: They were not to fight the descendants of Esau, who live near Mount Seir, for Yahweh had given that land to them.

question: How were they to get food and water?
answer: They were to buy food and water from the people living there so they could eat and drink.

question: What did Yahweh tell them they were not to do in Moab?
answer: They were not to trouble or fight with the people of Moab because Yahweh had given that land to them.

question: How long did it take Israel to go from Kadesh Barnea to the wadi of Zered?
answer: It took them 38 years from when they left until they crossed wadi of Zered.

question: What happened to all the men who had been old enough to fight?
answer: All the men who had been old enough to fight had died.

question: To whom had Yahweh given the land where the people of Ammon were living?
answer: Yahweh had given that land to the descendants of Lot.

question: What will the people of the land do when they hear news about the Israelites?
answer: They will tremble and be afraid because of what they hear about the Israelites.

question: What words of peace did Moses send to Sihon, king of Heshbon?
answer: Moses asked that they be allowed to pass through his land, staying on the road and not turning to the right or left.

question: How did Moses plan to get food and water for the people?
answer: He asked the king to sell him food and water so the Israelites could eat and drink.

question: What happened when Sihon came out to fight against Moses and his people?
answer: Yahweh allowed Moses and his people to defeated him, killing him, his son, and all his people.

question: What happened to all the king’s cities?
answer: Moses captured all the king’s cities and destroyed them, including women and children, leaving no survivors.

question: What did Og, the king of Bashan, do to Israel as they approached his land?
answer: As Israel approached the land of Bashan, the king and all his soldiers came and attacked them.

question: What did Israel do to the king of Bashan and his people?
answer: They defeated the king of Bashan, killing him and all his people, leaving no survivors.

question: What did Israel do with the cattle and the spoil of the cities?
answer: They took for themselves all the cattle and the spoil of the cities.

question: To whom did Moses give the land that they had captured?
answer: He gave it to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half of the tribe of Manasseh.

question: What did Moses command the men of war of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half of the tribe of Manasseh to do?
answer: He commanded them to cross over the Jordan River to help the rest of the people of Israel conquer that land.

question: When did Yahweh say the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half of the tribe of Manasseh could return to their own land?
answer: Yahweh said they could return to their own land after the rest of the Israelites captured the land that God was giving to them.

question: What did Moses tell Joshua not to do?
answer: He told Joshua not to fear the enemy because Yahweh would be the one who would fight for him.

question: What did Moses ask Yahweh to allow him to do?
answer: He asked Yahweh to let him go see the good land across the Jordan River and in Lebanon.

question: How did Yahweh respond to Moses’ request to go and see the land?
answer: Yahweh was angry with Moses because of what the people had done and did not listen to his request.

question: What did Yahweh allow Moses to do?
answer: Yahweh told him to go up to the top of Mount Pisgah and look all around from there, for he would not cross the Jordan River.

question: What did Yahweh tell Moses to do for Joshua?
answer: He told Moses to instruct, encourage, and strengthen Joshua, because he would lead the people across the river to occupy the land that he could see.

question: What must the people of Israel do so that they may live and go in and possess the land that Yahweh is giving them?
answer: They must listen and obey the laws that Moses will teach them so that they may possess the land.

question: What does Moses instruct the people not to do?
answer: They must not add to or take away from the words of the commands Moses is giving them so they will obey the commandments of Yahweh.

question: What happened to the men who were worshiping Baal?
answer: Yahweh destroyed the men that worshiped the Baal of Peor.

question: What will be the result of Israel keeping the rules that Moses commanded them?
answer: The people around them will notice that because they keep these rules, they are a nation that has wisdom and understanding.

question: What should the people do so that they do not forget what God has done?
answer: They should guard themselves by remembering the things God has done and telling them to their children and their grandchildren.

question: What did the people hear out of the middle of the fire on the mountain?
answer: They heard Yahweh’s voice out of the middle of the fire but did not see him.

question: What was the covenant written on that Yahweh commanded them to obey?
answer: The Ten Commandments that Yahweh gave to Moses for the people to obey were written on two tablets of stone.

question: What were the people told not to do so as to not act corruptly?
answer: They were told not to make any carved figures or idols of any thing.

question: Why did Moses tell the people to be careful about the sun, moon, and stars?
answer: He told them that they should be careful to not be seduced to worship the heavens, sun, moon, or stars.

question: Why did Yahweh bring the people out of Egypt?
answer: He brought them out of Egypt to be a people who belong to him.

question: What did Yahweh declare to Moses because he was angry with him?
answer: He declared that Moses would not cross the Jordan River into the good land.

question: Why did Yahweh forbid Israel to make any carved figure or idol?
answer: Yahweh their God is a jealous God and wants them to worship only him.

question: What does Moses say will happen if the people corrupt themselves and do evil in Yahweh’s sight?
answer: They will perish in the land over the Jordan and be completely destroyed.

question: What does Moses say Yahweh will do to the people if they worship idols?
answer: Yahweh will scatter them among other nations and only a few would survive.

question: When will the people find Yahweh?
answer: They will find him when they search for him with all their heart and all their soul.

question: What will make the people return to Yahweh their God and listen to his voice?
answer: When they are in trouble and when all the bad things have come on them, they will return to Yahweh.

question: What did God do for the people when they were in Egypt?
answer: God chose for himself all these people from the midst of another nation, by using his great power when he performed miracles, sent plagues, and fought the Egyptians for them.

question: What did Yahweh do to show the people that he alone is God?
answer: He allowed them to hear his voice speak from heaven, and on earth he made them see his great fire and hear his voice coming from it.

question: What did Yahweh do for Israel because he loved their ancestors?
answer: He chose their descendants and brought them out of Egypt with his great power. He gave them their land after driving out the more powerful nations.

question: Where could a person flee if he killed another person accidentally?
answer: He could flee to one of the three cities that Moses had selected on the east side of the Jordan River.

question: What was included in the law that Moses gave the people of Israel?
answer: He gave them the law which included all the instructions, rules, and regulations that he told them when they came out of Egypt.

question: From which two kings did Moses and his people take land on the east side of the Jordan River?
answer: The Israelites took the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan.

question: Where did Yahweh make his covenant with the people?
answer: Yahweh made his covenant with the people of Israel at Horeb.

question: Why did Moses stand between Yahweh and the people when Yahweh revealed his word to them?
answer: They were afraid of the fire from which Yahweh was speaking so Moses stood between them in order to tell them what he said.

question: Who does Yahweh tell Israel he is?
answer: He told them that he is Yahweh their God, who brought them from the land of Egypt and freed them from slavery.

question: What does God tell Israel not make, bow down to, or serve?
answer: They should not make carved figures of any likeness of anything that is in the sky, on earth, or in the water. If they do, God will punish them and their descendants.

question: What will Yahweh do for those who love him and keep his commandments?
answer: He will show covenant faithfulness to those who love him and obey his commandments.

question: Who will Yahweh not leave unpunished?
answer: He will not leave unpunished those who use his name for wrong purposes.

question: What does Yahweh say about the seventh day?
answer: The seventh day is a day of rest which is dedicated to Yahweh their God, so they must not do any work.

question: What does Yahweh want them to remember when they observe the Sabbath day?
answer: He wants them to remember that they were slaves in Egypt and that God brought them out by his great power.

question: What did Yahweh say would be the result if they honor their father and mother?
answer: They will live a long time in the land that God gave them and things will go well for them there.

question: What were they commanded not to do?
answer: They should not murder, commit adultery, steal, or give false witness.

question: On what did Yahweh write down his words?
answer: He wrote his words down on two tablets of stone and gave them to Moses.

question: What did the people say would happen to them if they heard the voice of Yahweh any longer?
answer: The people said that they would be burned up by the great fire and would die.

question: What did the people say they would do when Moses tells them everything that Yahweh says?
answer: They said they will listen and obey Yahweh’s word.

question: What did Yahweh say about the response of the people?
answer: Yahweh said he heard what the people said and that what they had spoken was good.

question: What did Moses say would happen to the people if they did all that Yahweh had commanded them?
answer: If they keep the commandments, they will live a long time in the land and things will go well for them there.

question: What will happen if the Israelites and their children keep all Yahweh’s statutes and commandments all the days of your lives?
answer: If they keep his statutes and commandments, they will live for a long time.

question: How did Moses describe the land into which the people were going?
answer: He said that it was a land flowing with milk and honey.

question: How should Israel love Yahweh?
answer: They should love Yahweh with all their heart, all their soul, and all their strength.

question: When should the people diligently teach the commandments to their children?
answer: They should teach the commandments to their children at every opportunity such as when they are in their house or walking on the road, lying down to rest, or getting up.

question: When should Israel remember what Yahweh has done for them?
answer: They should remember that it was Yahweh who brought them into the land he had promised them when they are enjoying every good thing that Yahweh had given them that they did not have to work for.

question: What will happen to Israel if they worship the gods of the people around them?
answer: Yahweh will become angry with them and he will destroy them completely if they worship the gods of the people around them.

question: What did the people do at Massah that they should not repeat?
answer: They tested Yahweh by doing sinful things to see if he would punish them or not.

question: How should the people respond when their children ask about all the things that Yahweh commanded?
answer: They should tell their children about how they were Pharaoh’s slaves and Yahweh brought them out of Egypt and gave them the land that he promised to their ancestors.

question: Why should the people fear Yahweh?
answer: They should fear him so that things will go well for them and so that he will protect them as a nation.

question: What must the people do to the people of the land that Yahweh is bringing them into?
answer: They must defeat them and destroy them completely.

question: What must the Israelites not do with the people of those nations?
answer: They are not to make any covenants with them, show them mercy, or arrange any marriages with them for their sons or daughters.

question: How should Israel deal with anything associated with the idols of the people of these nations?
answer: They should break down their altars, smash their sacred stone pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their idols.

question: Did Yahweh keep his oath to their ancestors?
answer: Yahweh kept his oath and rescued them from slavery to Pharaoh in Egypt.

question: What will Yahweh do with those who love him and keep his commandments?
answer: Yahweh will keep his covenants with those who love him and keep his commandments and faithfully love them forever.

question: In what ways will the people be blessed by Yahweh if they keep his decrees?
answer: God will love them and bless them and multiply them by giving them many children, crops, and animals.

question: What will God do to the nations of whom Israel is afraid?
answer: God will make them experience the same kinds of great trials and other displays of his power that they saw in Egypt.

question: Why should the Israelites not be frightened of the people?
answer: Yahweh, who is a great and fearsome God, will be with them.

question: How will God enable the people to defeat their enemies?
answer: God will greatly confuse them in battle and cause them to panic until they are destroyed.

question: What are they to do to the idols of the gods of the nations?
answer: They are to burn the idols and not even keep the gold or silver they are made of, as they are to be completely destroyed.

question: What should the people of Israel remember?
answer: They should remember all the ways that Yahweh led them over those 40 years in the wilderness. He was testing them to find out if they would obey his commandments or not.

question: How and why did Yahweh humble them?
answer: He allowed them to be hungry and then fed them manna so that they would know that they could not live only by having enough food to eat but also by paying attention to everything that Yahweh says.

question: How else did Yahweh provide for them all those years in the wilderness?
answer: Their clothing did not wear out and their feet did not swell.

question: How did Yahweh instruct the Israelites?
answer: As a man instructs and corrects his son, so Yahweh taught and corrected them.

question: What is in the good land into which God is bringing them?
answer: The land will be filled with many sources of water, grain, fruit and olive trees, and honey.

question: What will cause the people to bless and thank Yahweh?
answer: They will thank him because of the good and fertile land that he has given them.

question: What were the people reminded not to do?
answer: They were reminded not to forget Yahweh by failing to obey his commandments.

question: Why might the people forget Yahweh who brought them out of Egypt?
answer: When all that they possess increases, including herds, flock, and silver and gold, they might become proud and they might forget Yahweh.

question: How did Yahweh provide water and food in the terrible wilderness for the people of Israel?
answer: Yahweh brought water out of solid rock for them to drink and provided manna for them to eat.

question: What would cause the people to perish like the nations around them?
answer: They will perish if they forget their God and worship and serve other gods, because they would not listen to the voice of Yahweh.

question: Where are the people of Israel preparing to go?
answer: Israel is about to cross over the Jordan.

question: What will happen when Israel crosses Jordan?
answer: Yahweh will go ahead of them and will destroy the nations like a devouring fire.

question: What did Moses tell the people not to think after Yahweh enables them to drive their enemies out of the land?
answer: He told them not to think that it was because of Israel’s righteousness that Yahweh gave them the land.

question: What is the reason God is driving the nations out?
answer: He is driving them out because of their wickedness, and to keep his promise to Israel’s ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

question: Why was Yahweh angry with the people of Israel?
answer: He was angry with them because they were rebellious against him.

question: What did Moses eat and drink on the mountain?
answer: He did not eat or drink anything for 40 days and 40 nights on the mountain.

question: Why did Yahweh tell Moses to quickly go down from the mountain?
answer: Yahweh told him the people had corrupted themselves by doing what Yahweh had commanded them not to do and had made for themselves an idol to worship.

question: Why did Yahweh say he would destroy the Israelites?
answer: Yahweh said he had seen that they were a stubborn people.

question: What did Moses find that Israel had made while he was on the mountain?
answer: They had sinned against Yahweh by molding a calf as an idol just as he had commanded them not to do.

question: What did Moses do after he saw that the people had done evil in the sight of Yahweh?
answer: He threw down the tablets and broke them before their eyes, he prostrated himself before Yahweh for 40 days and nights, and did not eat or drink because of their sin.

question: Why did Moses pray for the people and Aaron?
answer: He prayed because Yahweh was angry enough with the people and with Aaron to destroy them.

question: What did Moses do to the calf that the people had made?
answer: Moses burned it, crushed it, and ground it into dust and threw the dust into the stream that came down from the mountain.

question: How did the people provoke Yahweh to anger?
answer: They rebelled against the commandment of Yahweh by not trusting him or obeying what he told them.

question: What was Moses praying as he prostrated himself before Yahweh for 40 days and nights?
answer: He prayed that Yahweh would not destroy his people whom he had rescued and brought out of Egypt.

question: What was Moses thinking the people of Egypt would say if Yahweh destroyed his people?
answer: He is afraid the people of Egypt would say that Yahweh was not able to bring Israel into the land he had promised them but that he took them into the wilderness to kill them because he hated them.

question: Where did Yahweh tell Moses to place the two tablets of stone on which he would write the words that were on the first tablets?
answer: Yahweh told him he to place the two tablets of stone into the chest of wood that Moses would make.

question: What did Yahweh write on the tablets of stone when Moses went up the mountain with them?
answer: Yahweh wrote the same Ten Commandments on the tablets that he had written on the first tablets.

question: Where did Moses put the two tablets when he returned from the mountain?
answer: He put them into the chest that he had made as Yahweh commanded him.

question: What happened in Moserah?
answer: Aaron died and was buried in Moserah and Eleazar, his son, took his place as priest.

question: What tribe had Yahweh chosen to carry the box of the covenant and to serve Yahweh?
answer: Yahweh chose the tribe of Levi to carry the chest, to serve him, and to bless people in his name.

question: How long did Moses stay on the mountain this time?
answer: He stayed on the mountain 40 days and 40 nights, just like he did the first time.

question: What does Moses say that Yahweh requires of Israel?
answer: Yahweh requires Israel to fear him, walk in all his ways, love him, worship him with all their heart and soul, and to obey his commandments.

question: What did Moses tell the people to circumcise?
answer: He told them to humble themselves as if they were circumcising the foreskin of their hearts.

question: Why should Israel love the foreigner?
answer: Israel should love the foreigner because they were once foreigners in the land of Egypt.

question: How has God blessed the people since they first went down into Egypt?
answer: There were only 70 of their ancestors who went down into Egypt but now, God has made them as numerous as the stars of the heavens.

question: What does Moses tell the people to always keep?
answer: He tells them to always keep Yahweh’s rules, statutes, decrees, and commandments.

question: Who had not seen all that Yahweh did in Egypt?
answer: The children of the Israelites who were born while they wandered in the wilderness had not seen Yahweh’s discipline and his mighty deeds that he did in Egypt.

question: How did Yahweh destroy the army of Egypt when they pursued after Israel?
answer: Yahweh caused the water of the Sea of Reeds to drown the army of Egypt as they pursued after Israel.

question: What had the Israelites seen?
answer: The Israelites had seen all the great works that Yahweh did.

question: What will happen to the people if they keep all the commandments?
answer: If they keep all the commandments, they will be strong, go in and possess the land, and they and their descendants will live in the land for a long time.

question: How is the land they are going to enter different from the land of Egypt?
answer: In the land they are going to enter there are many hills and valleys and plenty of water from the rain.

question: What would Yahweh give them if they obey his commandments and to love and serve him with all their heart and soul?
answer: Yahweh will give them rain in its season, that they may gather their grain and be able to make wine and oil.

question: What will Yahweh do if the people turn aside and worship other gods?
answer: He will become angry and will restrain the heavens so there will not be any rain.

question: What should the people do so that they will live for a very long time in the land?
answer: They will write the commandments on the doorposts of their house and on their gates.

question: If the people keep all the commandments of Yahweh and cling to him, what will he do for them?
answer: Yahweh will drive out all the other nations that are larger and mightier than they are.

question: Why would no man be able to stand before Israel?
answer: Yahweh will cause the people of that land to fear and feel terror of Israel.

question: What did Moses give Israel that day?
answer: He gave them a blessing and a curse.

question: Where must the people go in order to possess the land?
answer: They must cross over the Jordan to possess and live in the land.

question: What places did Moses tell Israel to destroy?
answer: They were to destroy all the places where the nations that Israel dispossessed had worshiped their gods.

question: What does Yahweh instruct the people of Israel do to the name of the gods of the nations?
answer: He told Israel to destroy everything to do with those gods in order to remove their name from there.

question: In what place were the people of Israel to bring their burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, and offerings?
answer: They were to go to the place that Yahweh their God would choose.

question: What kinds of things were the people of Israel doing?
answer: They were doing whatever they thought was right.

question: What kind of rest will Yahweh give to Israel when they go over the Jordan?
answer: He will give them rest by protecting them from all their surrounding enemies, so they will live in safety.

question: What animals can Israel kill and eat?
answer: Israel can kill and eat domesticated animals where they are living.

question: What was Israel not allowed to eat?
answer: Israel was not allowed to eat the blood, but must pour it out on the earth.

question: Where was Israel told they could not eat their tithes and sacrifices?
answer: They were not allowed to eat what was intended for tithing or sacrificing where they lived.

question: Where were the people of Israel to eat their tithes and sacrifices?
answer: They were to eat these offerings in the place that Yahweh their God will choose.

question: What was Israel told be sure not to do?
answer: They were told to not forget to take care of the Levites.

question: What can Israel eat when Yahweh their God enlarges their borders as he has promised them?
answer: Israel can eat the meat from the new land.

question: What can Israel eat if the place that Yahweh their God chooses to put his name is too far from them?
answer: If the place that Yahweh Israel’s God chooses to put his name is too far from where they live, then they may kill some of their flock for sacrifices as well as to eat.

question: Where did they consider the life of the animal?
answer: Israel was to consider the blood as the life of the animal and thus should not eat it with the meat.

question: What is Israel instructed to take to the place that Yahweh chooses?
answer: Israel is to take the sacred things that they have and their offerings to the place that Yahweh chooses.

question: What is to be done with the blood and the meat of the animals they offer as a burnt offering?
answer: They are to pour the blood out on the altar of Yahweh their God and eat the meat.

question: What is Israel instructed to do so that it may go well with them and with their descendants after them?
answer: Israel is to listen to and obey all the words that Yahweh commands them and do what is good and right so that things may go well for them and their descendants forever.

question: What does Yahweh instruct Israel to watch out for when God enables Israel to go in and dispossess the nations in the land and live there?
answer: Israel is to pay attention so that they are not trapped into serving the gods of those nations.

question: What have the other nations done to their sons and daughters in order to worship the gods?
answer: The other nations have even burned their sons and daughters on altars to these other gods.

question: Why should the people of Israel not listen to a prophet who predicts something that happens and then says that they should go after other gods and worship them?
answer: The people of Israel should not listen because Yahweh is testing them to know whether they love him with all their heart and with all their soul.

question: What should the people of Israel do to the prophet who tells them to worship other gods?
answer: They should put that prophet to death because he has spoken against what Yahweh has commanded them.

question: What have the people of Israel been instructed to do to anyone who secretly entices them and says that they should go and worship other gods?
answer: They must surely kill anyone who entices them to worship other gods.

question: How should the people of Israel kill the person who tells them to disobey Yahweh their God?
answer: They should stone that person to death.

question: What shall the people of Israel do if they hear that some wicked person is telling others to go and worship other gods?
answer: They should investigate it thoroughly to see if it is true.

question: What should Israel do to a city if they learn that it is true that the inhabitants have been worshiping other gods?
answer: They should kill the inhabitants of that city and destroy everything in it.

question: What are the people told about the things that Yahweh has told them to destroy?
answer: They must not take any of those things for themselves that Yahweh has told them to destroy, so that Yahweh will not be angry and will have compassion on them as he promised their ancestors.

question: What does Moses instruct the people of Yahweh not to do?
answer: They are not to cut themselves nor shave any part of their heads for the dead.

question: What are the two characteristics of the animals that the Israelites are allowed to eat?
answer: Israel may eat any animal that has split hooves and also chews the cud.

question: Why is the pig not to be eaten?
answer: The pig is unclean for the Israelites because he has split hooves but does not chew the cud.

question: What are the characteristics of the things from the water that the Israelites are allowed to eat?
answer: They may eat whatever has fins and scales.

question: Are the Israelites allowed to eat winged swarming things?
answer: All winged, swarming insects are unclean for the Israelites and must not be eaten.

question: May the Israelites eat anything that dies of natural causes?
answer: They may not eat anything that dies naturally, but they may give it to a foreigner to eat or sell.

question: What could the Israelites not do with a young goat?
answer: They must not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.

question: What are the Israelites to do with the crops produced in their fields?
answer: Israelites must set apart a tenth of all their crops once a year.

question: What are the Israelites instructed to eat in the place that he will choose?
answer: Israel must eat the tithe, which was a tenth of their grain, new wine, and of their oil, as well as the firstborn animals in the place that Yahweh will choose.

question: What are the Israelites allowed to do if they are blessed with such a large crop that they are not able to carry the tithe to the place that Yahweh will choose?
answer: If the journey is too for them to carry all of the tithe of what Yahweh has blessed them with, they can sell a tenth of their crops and take the money to the place that Yahweh has chosen.

question: Who has no inheritance with the Israelites and must not be neglected?
answer: The Levites will not own any land so the others must not neglect to help them.

question: What are the Israelites instructed to do at the end of every three years?
answer: At the end of every three years the Israelites are to store the tithe of their produce from that year for the Levites, the foreigners, the fatherless, and the widows to have enough to eat.

question: What must the Israelites do at the end of every seven years?
answer: At the end of every seven years the Israelites must cancel all debts.

question: Why are debts to be canceled every seven years?
answer: Everyone will cancel that which he has loaned to a fellow Israelite because Yahweh has declared the cancelation of debts every seven years.

question: From whom can Israelites continue to collect payment at the end of every seven years?
answer: The Israelites can continue to collect payment of a debt from a foreigner.

question: Why should there be no poor among the Israelites?
answer: If they do all that Yahweh has commanded them, there should no longer be poor among them since Yahweh will bless them.

question: What will happen to demonstrate that Yahweh has blessed Israel as he promised?
answer: Israel will lend to many nations, but will not borrow; Israel will rule over many nations, but the other nations will not rule over them.

question: What are the Israelites told not to do if there is a poor man among them?
answer: The Israelites are told not to be selfish and refuse to help them.

question: What should the Israelites be careful not to do when the seventh year, the year of remission is near?
answer: They should not refuse to give help to a poor man because the year of canceling debts is near.

question: What will Yahweh do for the Israelites in return for giving generously to the poor?
answer: Yahweh will bless the Israelites in everything they do.

question: Why is Israel commanded to give generously to their fellow Israelites, to the needy and the poor in their land?
answer: They should give generously because there will always be poor living among them.

question: What are Israelites instructed to give a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman who is released to go free in the seventh year?
answer: They must provide for that person freely out of their flocks and their crops with which Yahweh their God has blessed them.

question: What are the Israelites to remember as they give to the one they set free?
answer: The Israelites are told to remember that they were slaves in the land of Egypt and Yahweh freed them.

question: What is an Israelite to do to a male or female slave who says that they do not want to leave?
answer: The Israelite is to pierce the slave’s ear, and he or she will be their slave forever.

question: Why should it not seem difficult for the Israelite to let the slave go free?
answer: It should not be difficult because he has served them for six years and given them twice the value of a hired person.

question: What must the people of Israel do with the firstborn males in their herd and their flock?
answer: They must set them aside for Yahweh and not use them for work or shear them.

question: What are the Israelites to do with the firstborn animal if it is lame or blind or has any other defect?
answer: They must not sacrifice it to Yahweh, but instead they can eat it.

question: Why are the Israelites to keep the Passover for Yahweh their God in the month of Aviv?
answer: The Israelites are to celebrate the Passover each year during the month of Aviv because Yahweh brought Israel out of Egypt in that month.

question: What will the Israelites do to celebrate the Passover?
answer: The Israelites will sacrifice some of the flock and the herd in the place that Yahweh will choose.

question: Why are the Israelites to eat no leavened bread or have yeast in all their land for seven days?
answer: They are to eat no leavened bread or have yeast during those days to remind them that they came out of the land of Egypt with too much haste for bread to rise.

question: What are the Israelites told about the meat that they sacrifice in the evening on the first day?
answer: The Israelites are to make sure there is no meat that they sacrifice in the evening remaining the next morning.

question: Where are the Israelites to offer the sacrifice of the Passover?
answer: They are to sacrifice at the place that Yahweh will choose.

question: When will the sacrifice of the Passover be performed?
answer: The sacrifice of the Passover is to be performed in the evening when the sun is setting, at the time when the Israelites started to leave Egypt.

question: What are the Israelites supposed to do on the first six days as they celebrate Passover?
answer: The Israelites are to eat unleavened bread for six days.

question: What are the Israelites supposed to do on the seventh day as they celebrate Passover?
answer: On the seventh day, they are to have a festive assembly and do no work.

question: How do the Israelites determine the start of the Festival of Weeks for Yahweh?
answer: The Israelites will count seven weeks from the time they begin to harvest their grain.

question: What contribution do the Israelites give on the Festival of Weeks?
answer: They must give Yahweh a freewill offering according to how much Yahweh has blessed them.

question: What must they remember during the Festival of Weeks?
answer: They must remember that they were slaves in Egypt.

question: What festival are the Israelites instructed to keep for seven days after they have gathered in the harvest from their threshing floors and from their wine presses?
answer: They are to keep the Festival of Shelters for seven days after they have gathered in their harvest.

question: How much is every male Israelite supposed to give to Yahweh instead of coming without an offering?
answer: Every male Israelite is to give in proportion to how much Yahweh has blessed him with that year.

question: At what the three festivals must all the males of Israel gather to worship Yahweh at the place that Yahweh chooses?
answer: They must gather to worship Yahweh at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Shelters.

question: Where are the Israelites to find their judges and officers?
answer: The judges and officers will be taken from each of their tribes to judge the people with righteous judgment.

question: Why are the judges not to show partiality or take a bribe?
answer: If a judge takes a bribe, he will find it difficult to judge fairly but will instead want to do what the person who bribes him wants him to do.

question: Why must the judges pursue righteousness and judge fairly?
answer: They must pursue righteousness and judge fairly, so that they may live and occupy the land that Yahweh is giving them.

question: What are the Israelites not to set up for themselves?
answer: They are not to set up an Asherah pole or a stone pillar to worship any idol.

question: Why must the Israelites not sacrifice an ox or a sheep with any blemish or defect to Yahweh?
answer: A sacrifice that is not perfect will be detestable to Yahweh.

question: What are the Israelites told to do if they hear that a man or woman within their cities have done what is evil in the sight of Yahweh and is serving other gods?
answer: The Israelites are to investigate thoroughly to know if this is true and that the idol worship is actually happening.

question: What are the Israelites to do with a man or woman who has done such an evil thing as worshiping other gods?
answer: The Israelites are to stone that person to death.

question: How many witnesses are needed to convict a person to death?
answer: Two or three witnesses are needed to convict a person to death.

question: Who must throw the first stones when putting a person to death?
answer: The witnesses must be the first to throw the stones, followed by the rest of the people of Israel.
