question: On what day did Jotham address the leaders of Shechem?
answer: Jotham addressed them on the same day that they had risen up against his father’s house and killed 70 of his sons.

question: What was the curse of Jotham?
answer: The curse of Jotham was for fire to come out from Abimelech to burn up the men of Shechem and Beth Millo, and for fire to come out from the men of Shechem and Beth Millo to burn up Abimelech.

question: Why did God allow the leaders of Shechem to deal treacherously with Abimelech?
answer: God allowed the leaders of Shechem to deal treacherously with Abimelech so that the violence done to the 70 sons of Jerubbaal might be avenged.

question: Who did the leaders of Shechem hope to ambush?
answer: The leaders of Shechem hoped to ambush Abimelech.

question: Who wished the people would serve him instead of Abimelech?
answer: Gaal wished the people would serve him.

question: When was Zebul’s anger kindled?
answer: When Zebul heard what Gaal was saying about removing Abimelech, he became angry.

question: Why did Zebul send messengers to Abimelech?
answer: He sent messengers to Abimelech in order to warn him that Gaal, the son of Ebed, was inciting the city against him.

question: How did Zebul describe the men Gaal saw coming down the hills?
answer: Zebul said they were shadows of the hills.

question: What did Zebul tell Gaal to do?
answer: Zebul told Gaal to go out and fight against Abimelech.

question: What happened when Gaal fought Abimelech?
answer: Abimelech pursued Gaal, and Gaal fled before Abimelech, and many fell with deadly wounds before the entrance to the city gate.

question: What did Abimelech do after he captured the city?
answer: Abimelech killed the people, tore down the city, and spread salt over it.

question: Where did the leaders of the tower of Shechem enter?
answer: The leaders of the tower of Shechem entered the citadel of the house of El-Berith.

question: How did Abimelech kill all the leaders and people in the tower of Shechem?
answer: Abimelech went up to Mount Zalmon, piled branches around the fortress and set it on fire, killing all the people in it.

question: When Abimelech came near the entrance of the tower of Thebez, what happened to him?
answer: When Abimelech came near the entrance of the tower of Thebez, a woman on the roof dropped a millstone on his head and it crushed his skull.

question: Why did Abimelech tell his armor-bearer to draw his sword and kill him?
answer: Abimelech told his armor-bearer to draw his sword and kill him so no one would say a women killed Abimelech.

question: Where was Shamir?
answer: Shamir was in the hill country of Ephraim.

question: Why did Yahweh burn with anger toward the people of Israel?
answer: The people of Israel forsook Yahweh and no longer served him, so he became angry with Israel.

question: Why was Israel greatly distressed?
answer: The Ammonites crossed over the Jordan to fight against the people of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim, so that Israel was greatly distressed.

question: To whom did Yahweh tell the people of Israel to call out for help?
answer: Yahweh told the people to call out to the gods that they had worshiped to show them that those gods could not save them.

question: Why could Yahweh no longer bear the misery of Israel?
answer: Israel removed the foreign gods from their midst and they worshiped Yahweh, so he had compassion on them.

question: Who were Jephthah’s parents?
answer: Jephthah was the son of a prostitute and Gilead.

question: Why did the elders of Gilead go to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob?
answer: The elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob so he would be their commander in their fight against the Ammonites.

question: Why did the elders of Gilead come to Jephthah?
answer: The elders of Gilead came to Jephthah because they wanted him to come with them to fight the Ammonites and be their leader.

question: If the elders of Gideon brought Jephthah home again to fight against the soldiers of Ammon, and if Yahweh gave them victory over them, what would happen to Jephthah?
answer: If the elders of Gideon brought Jephthah home again to fight against the soldiers of Ammon, and if Yahweh gave them victory over them, Jephthah would be their leader.

question: Why did the people of Ammon come to fight to take the land of Israel?
answer: The people of Ammon came to take the land of Israel because they claimed that when Israel came up out of Egypt, Israel seized the land of Ammon.

question: Who was not willing to let Israel pass?
answer: The king of Edom and the king of Moab were not willing to let Israel pass.

question: Who gave Israel victory over Sihon?
answer: Yahweh, the God of Israel, gave Israel victory over Sihon.

question: For how long did Israel live in Heshbon and its villages and in Aroer and its villages and in all the cities that are along the banks of the Arnon?
answer: Israel lived for 300 years in Heshbon and Aroer and their villages as well as in all the cities that are along the banks of the Arnon.

question: If Yahweh gave Jephthah victory over the people of Ammon, what did Jephthah vow to do?
answer: If Yahweh gave Jephthah victory over the people of Ammon, Jephthah would offer up as a burnt offering whoever came out of the doors of his house to greet him.

question: When Jephthah passed through to the people of Ammon to fight against them, who gave him the victory?
answer: When Jephthah passed through to the people of Ammon to fight against them, Yahweh gave him victory.

question: How many children did Jephthah have?
answer: Jephthah had only one child, this daughter.

question: What did Jephthah’s daughter want to do before he did everything he had promised?
answer: She wanted him to leave her alone for two months, that she could go down to the hills and grieve over her virginity.

question: What did Jephthah do with his daughter?
answer: He did what he had promised in the vow he had made.

question: What did the men of Ephraim want to do to Jephthah’s house because he did not call them to go with him?
answer: The men of Ephraim wanted to burn Jephthah’s house down because he did not call them to go with him to fight against the people of Ammon.

question: Why did the men of Gilead attack the men of Ephraim?
answer: The men of Gilead attacked the men of Ephraim because Ephraimites said the Gileadites were fugitives from Ephraim.

question: How did the men of Gilead test if a man was from Ephraim?
answer: They would tell him to say “Shibboleth.” And if he said, “Sibboleth,” (for the Ephraimites could not pronounce the word correctly), the Gileadites would seize him and kill him at the fords of the Jordan.

question: What clan was Manoah from?
answer: Manoah was from the clan of Dan.

question: Why was no razor to come onto the child’s head?
answer: No razor was to come onto his head, for the child was to be a Nazirite to God.

question: What did the man of God look like?
answer: The man of God looked like an angel of God.

question: When the angel of God came a second time, who was there?
answer: When the angel of God came a second time, only Manoah’s wife was there.

question: What did Manoah ask the angel about?
answer: Manoah asked the angel about the rules for the boy and what his work would be.

question: If Manoah prepared a burnt offering, to whom was he to offer it?
answer: If Manoah prepared a burnt offering, he was to offer it to Yahweh.

question: What wonderful thing did Yahweh do while Manoah and his wife were watching?
answer: While Manoah and his wife were watching, the angel of Yahweh went up in the flame of the altar.

question: Where did Yahweh’s Spirit begin to stir Samson?
answer: Yahweh’s Spirit began to stir Samson in Mahaneh Dan.

question: Who did Samson want his parents to get for him to be his wife?
answer: Samson wanted his parents to get for him a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines, to be his wife.

question: Why did Samson want his parents to get him the woman in Timnah as his wife?
answer: He wanted his parents to get him the woman in Timnah as his wife, for when he looked at her, she pleased him.

question: How was Samson able to tear the lion apart?
answer: Yahweh’s Spirit suddenly came on him, and he tore the lion apart.

question: What was in the carcass of the lion?
answer: There was a swarm of bees and honey in the carcass of the lion.

question: What would Samson get if the 30 companions could not answer his riddle?
answer: Samson would get 30 linen robes and 30 changes of clothes if the 30 companions could not answer his riddle.

question: What would happen to Samson’s wife if she did not entice her husband to get the answer to the riddle?
answer: If Samson’s wife did not entice her husband to get the answer to the riddle, the 30 companions would burn up her and her father’s house.

question: For how long did Samson’s wife cry in order to get the answer to the riddle?
answer: She cried for the seven days that the feast lasted.

question: How did Samson get 30 changes of clothing?
answer: Samson went down to Ashkelon and killed 30 men among those people and took their changes of clothing.

question: When Samson went to visit his wife, why did her father not allow him to go in?
answer: The father thought Samson hated his wife, so had already given her to one of Samson’s companions.

question: How did Samson retaliate after finding out his wife had been given to another?
answer: Samson retaliated by catching 300 foxes, tying torches to them, and letting them go in the Philistines’ grain.

question: When the Philistines were told that Samson burned their fields, what did they do?
answer: When the Philistines were told that Samson burned their fields, they burned his wife and her father.

question: Why did Samson kill a great number of Philistines?
answer: Samson killed a great number of Philistines to avenge the killing of his wife and her father.

question: Why did the Philistines come up to attack Judah?
answer: The Philistines came up to attack Judah so they could capture Samson in order to kill him as he had killed so many of them.

question: When the men of Judah came to tie up Samson, what did he make them swear?
answer: When the men of Judah came to tie up Samson, he made them swear that they would not kill him themselves.

question: With what did Samson kill 1,000 men?
answer: Samson killed 1,000 men with a fresh jawbone of a donkey.

question: After Samson killed 1,000 men with a fresh jawbone of a donkey, how did he think he would die?
answer: After Samson killed 1,000 men with a fresh jawbone of a donkey, he thought he would die of thirst.

question: How did Samson get water?
answer: God split open the hollow place at Lehi, and water came out.

question: When did the Gazites plan to kill Samson?
answer: The Gazites planned to kill Samson at daylight.

question: How did Samson escape Gaza?
answer: Samson took hold of the city gate and its two posts, and he pulled them up out of the ground, bar and all.

question: If Delilah enticed Samson to tell her the secret of his strength, what would the leaders of the Philistines give her?
answer: If Delilah enticed Samson to tell her the secret of his strength, each of the Philistine leaders would give her 1,100 pieces of silver.

question: When Delilah told Samson the Philistines were upon him, what did he do?
answer: When Delilah told Samson the Philistines were upon him, he broke the cords with which he was tied.

question: When Samson tore off the new ropes from his arms, where were the men lying in wait?
answer: When Samson tore off the new ropes from his arms, the men were waiting in one of the rooms of the house.

question: How much did Delilah beg Samson to tell her his secret?
answer: She begged him so much that he wished he would die.

question: Why had Samson never cut the hair on his head?
answer: Samson had never cut the hair on his head, for he had been a Nazirite of God from his mother’s womb.

question: How was Delilah able to subdue Samson?
answer: Delilah was able to subdue him when the locks of his head were shaven off, for his strength left him.

question: What work did the Philistines make Samson do?
answer: The Philistines made Samson turn the millstone to grind grain in the prison.

question: Why did the leaders of the Philistines gather together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god?
answer: The leaders of the Philistines had a celebration to offer sacrifices to Dagon their god because they said he had conquered Samson.

question: Who helped Samson touch the columns on which the building rested?
answer: The young man leading Samson by the hand led him so he could touch the columns which supported the building.

question: Why did Samson want God to strengthen him?
answer: Samson wanted God to strengthen him so that he could have revenge in one blow on the Philistines for taking his two eyes.

question: How many people did Samson kill when the building fell?
answer: Samson killed more at his death than those he had killed during his life.

question: What did Micah steal?
answer: Micah stole 1,100 pieces of silver from his mother.

question: For what did Micah’s mother set apart the silver?
answer: Micah’s mother said she had dedicated the silver to Yahweh, for her son to make an idol.

question: To what did Micah appoint one of his sons?
answer: He appointed one of his sons to become his priest.

question: Why did the Levite leave Bethlehem?
answer: The Levite left Bethlehem to go and find a place to live.

question: What did Micah ask the Levite to be to him?
answer: Micah asked the Levite to live with him and be an adviser and a priest to him.

question: Why did Micah think Yahweh would be good to him?
answer: Micah thought Yahweh would be good to him because he had a Levite as his priest.

question: Why were the descendants of Dan looking for a territory in which to live?
answer: The descendants of Dan were looking for a territory in which to live because they had not been able to occupy all of the territory that had been assigned to them.

question: What did the people of Dan want the Levite to ask God?
answer: The people of Dan wanted the Levite to ask God if they would succeed in what they were trying to do.

question: What did the five men from Dan want to do with the land of Laish?
answer: The five men from Dan wanted to take possession of the land so their people could live there.

question: What did the five men say was in the houses of Laish?
answer: The five men said that in the houses of Laish there were a sacred vest, household idols, and a silver molded figure.

question: Why was Micah angry?
answer: Micah was angry because the Danites stole the idols he had made and his priest and they were leaving.

question: Why did Micah turn and go back to his house?
answer: When Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back to his house.

question: Why was there no one to rescue the people of Laish?
answer: There was no one to rescue the people of Laish because it was a long way from Sidon and they had no other allies.

question: Who were the priests for the tribe of the Danites?
answer: Jonathan, the son of Gershom, (the grandson of Moses) and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan.

question: Where was the Levite living?
answer: The Levite was living in a remote area of the hill country of Ephraim.

question: Where did the Levite’s concubine bring him?
answer: The concubine brought the Levite into the house of her father.

question: Although the Levite intended to go home, what did his father-in-law want him to do?
answer: His father-in-law wanted him to stay and spend the night.

question: What did the Levite’s father-in-law ask him to do again on the fifth day?
answer: His father-in-law asked him to stay another night and have a good time.

question: Why did the Levite not want to spend the night in Jebus?
answer: The Levite did not want to stay in a city where there were no other Israelites.

question: Why did the Levite and his servant sit down in the city square?
answer: They sat down in the city square, for no one had offered them a place to stay for the night.

question: From what tribe were the men living in Gibeah?
answer: The men living in Gibeah were from the tribe of Benjamin.

question: What did the old man warn the Levite not to do?
answer: The old man warned the Levite not to spend the night in the open square.

question: Why did the wicked men of the city want the old man to bring out the man who was staying in his house?
answer: The wicked men of the city wanted the old man to bring out the man who came was staying in his house so they could have sex with him.

question: Who did the old man offer to the wicked men in place of the Levite?
answer: The old man offered them his virgin daughter and the Levite’s concubine.

question: What happened at dawn?
answer: At dawn the wicked men let the concubine go. She came and she fell down at the door of the man’s house where her master was, and she lay there until it was light.

question: What did the Levite do when his concubine did not answer him?
answer: When the Levite’s concubine did not answer him, he put her body on the donkey and set out for home.

question: What did the Levite do to his concubine’s body?
answer: The Levite cut her up into twelve pieces and sent the pieces to each of the tribes throughout Israel.

question: Who gathered together before Yahweh at Mizpah?
answer: All the people from Dan to Beersheba, including the land of Gilead, gathered together before Yahweh at Mizpah.

question: What did the Levite say the men of Gibeah did to him?
answer: The Levite said the men of Gibeah surrounded the house in order to abuse and kill him.

question: Why did the tribes of Israel tell Benjamin to give them those wicked men of Gibeah?
answer: The tribes of Israel told Benjamin to give them those wicked men of Gibeah, so they might put them to death in order to completely remove this evil from Israel.

question: Why did the people of Benjamin come together at Gibeah?
answer: The people of Benjamin came together at Gibeah to defend it against the people of Israel.

question: What was special about the 700 chosen men?
answer: The 700 chosen men were left-handed; each of them could sling a stone with great accuracy.

question: Why did Judah attack Benjamin?
answer: The people asked God and he told them that Judah should attack first.

question: After Benjamin killed many soldiers of Israel, what did the soldiers of Israel do?
answer: After Benjamin killed many soldiers of Israel, the soldiers of Israel wept and fasted before Yahweh until evening. They also offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to Yahweh.

question: Where was the Box of the Covenant of God in those days?
answer: The Box of the Covenant of God was in Bethel at that time.

question: When the soldiers of Israel drew away from the city, what did the people of Benjamin think?
answer: When the soldiers of Israel drew away from the city, the people of Benjamin thought they had defeated them and they were running away.

question: Why had the men of Israel retreated?
answer: The men of Israel had retreated because they wanted the Benjaminites to be drawn out of the city where they had men hidden outside Gibeah waiting to attack them.

question: What was the signal between the soldiers of Israel and the men hiding in secret?
answer: The arranged signal between the soldiers of Israel and the men hiding in secret was that a great cloud of smoke would rise up out of the city.

question: Why could the men of Benjamin not escape?
answer: The men of Benjamin ran away from the soldiers of Israel, trying to escape into the wilderness, but they were caught between the two groups of Israelites.

question: How many soldiers of Benjamin turned and fled to the wilderness?
answer: Six hundred men were able to escape to the wilderness.

question: Why did the men of Israel say that one of their tribes might not exist anymore?
answer: The men of Israel worried that the Benjaminite tribe would no longer exist since they had promised to not allow their daughters to marry a Benjaminite so the remaining men would not have women to marry.

question: Who would certainly be put to death?
answer: Anyone who did not come when they met with Yahweh at Mizpah would certainly be put to death.

question: Which of the cities did not come to meet with Yahweh at Mizpah?
answer: No one from the city of Jabesh Gilead had come to meet with Yahweh at Mizpah.

question: Who did the men take from those living in Jabesh Gilead?
answer: The men took 400 young women who had never slept with a man from those living in Jabesh Gilead.

question: What was the problem when the Benjaminites were given the women of Jabesh Gilead?
answer: When the Benjaminites were given the women of Jabesh Gilead, there were not enough women for all of them to marry.

question: Where was Shiloh?
answer: Shiloh was north of Bethel, east of the road that went up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.

question: When were the Benjaminites to each rush out of the vineyards and grab a wife from the young women of Shiloh?
answer: When the young women from Shiloh came out to dance, each Benjaminite was to rush out of the vineyards and grab a young woman as his wife.

question: Why would the men of Shiloh not be guilty of breaking their oath?
answer: The men of Shiloh were told that they had not broken their oath since they had not given their daughters to the Benjaminites as wives but instead, the young women had been stolen.

question: How did everyone live in those days when Israel had no king?
answer: Everyone did what he thought was right in his own eyes.

question: Who was the Word with?
answer: The Word was with God.

question: What was in the beginning?
answer: In the beginning was the Word.

question: What was the Word?
answer: The Word was God.

question: Was anything made without the Word?
answer: All things were made through him, and without him there was not one thing made that has been made.

question: What was in the Word?
answer: In him was life.

question: What was the name of the man sent from God?
answer: His name was John.

question: What did John come to do?
answer: He came as a witness to testify about the light, that all might believe through him.

question: Did the world know or receive the light John came to testify about?
answer: The world did not know the light John came to testify about, and that light’s own people did not receive him.

question: What did the light do for those who believed on his name?
answer: To those who believed on his name he gave the right to become children of God.

question: How could those who believed on his name become children of God?
answer: They could become children of God by being born by God.

question: Is there or was there any other person like the Word, who came from the Father?
answer: No! The Word is the only unique person who came from the Father.

question: What have we received from the fullness of this one John testified about?
answer: From his fullness we have all received free gift after free gift.

question: What came through Jesus Christ?
answer: Grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.

question: Who has seen God at any time?
answer: No man has seen God at any time.

question: Who has made God known to us?
answer: The one who is in the bosom of the Father has made him known to us.

question: Who did John say he was when asked by the priests and Levites from Jerusalem?
answer: He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: ‘Make the way of the Lord straight,’ just as Isaiah the prophet said.”

question: What did John say when he saw Jesus coming to him?
answer: He said, “Look, there is the lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.”

question: Why did John come baptizing with water?
answer: He came baptizing with water so that Jesus, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, could be revealed to Israel.

question: What was the sign that revealed Jesus as the son of God to John?
answer: The sign was that on whoever John saw the Spirit descending and remaining, that one is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.

question: What did two of John’s disciples do when they heard John call Jesus “the lamb of God”?
answer: They followed Jesus.

question: What is the name of one of the two who heard John speak and then followed Jesus?
answer: The name of one of the two is Andrew.

question: What did Andrew tell his brother Simon about Jesus?
answer: Andrew told Simon, “We have found the Messiah.”

question: What did Jesus say Simon would be called?
answer: Jesus said Simon would be called “Cephas” (which means “Peter”).

question: What was the city of Andrew and Peter?
answer: The city of Andrew and Peter was Bethsaida.

question: What did Nathaniel say about Jesus?
answer: Nathaniel said, “Rabbi, you are the son of God! You are the King of Israel.”

question: What did Jesus say Nathaniel would see?
answer: Jesus told Nathaniel he would see the heavens opened, and all the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.

question: Who was at the wedding in Cana of Galilee?
answer: Jesus, his mother, and his disciples were at the wedding in Cana of Galilee.

question: Why did the mother of Jesus tell Jesus, “They have no wine”?
answer: She told this to Jesus because she expected the he would do something about the situation.

question: What two things did Jesus tell the servants to do?
answer: He first told them to fill the water pots with water. Then he told the servants to take some of the “water” to the head waiter.

question: What did the head waiter say after he tasted the water that had become wine?
answer: The head waiter said, “Every man places first the good wine and then the cheaper wine when men are drunk. But you have kept the fine wine until now.”

question: What was the response of Jesus’ disciples on seeing this miraculous sign?
answer: Jesus’ disciples believed in Jesus.

question: What did Jesus find when he went to the temple in Jerusalem?
answer: He found money changers and those that sold oxen, sheep and pigeons.

question: What did Jesus do to the sellers and money changers?
answer: He made a whip of cords and drove all of them out from the temple, including both the sheep and the oxen. He also poured out the money changers’ money and overthrew their tables.

question: What did Jesus say to the pigeon sellers?
answer: He said, “Take these things away from here. Stop making my father’s house a marketplace.”

question: How did the Jewish authorities respond to Jesus’ actions in the temple?
answer: They asked Jesus, “What sign will you show us, since you are doing these things?”

question: How did Jesus answer the Jewish authorities?
answer: He answered them by saying, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”

question: What temple was Jesus referring to?
answer: Jesus was speaking of the temple of his body.

question: Why did many believe in Jesus’ name?
answer: They believed because they saw all the miraculous signs he did.

question: Why would Jesus not trust himself to the people?
answer: He would not trust himself to the people because he knew all people, what was in mankind, and because he did not need anyone to testify concerning mankind.

question: Who was Nicodemus?
answer: Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a member of the Jewish Council.

question: What did Nicodemus testify to Jesus?
answer: Nicodemus told Jesus, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher come from God, for no one can do these signs that you do unless God is with him.”

question: What did Jesus tell Nicodemus that confused and perplexed Nicodemus?
answer: Jesus told Nicodemus that one had to be born again in order to enter the kingdom of God.

question: What questions did Nicodemus ask that let us know that Jesus’ statements confused and perplexed Nicodemus?
answer: Nicodemus said, “How can a man be born when he is old? He cannot enter a second time into his mother’s womb and be born, can he?”

question: How did Jesus rebuke Nicodemus?
answer: He rebuked Nicodemus by saying, “Are you a teacher of Israel, and yet you do not understand these things?”

question: Who has ascended into heaven?
answer: No one has ascended into heaven except he who descended from heaven, the Son of Man.

question: Why must the Son of Man be lifted up?
answer: He must be lifted up so that all who believe in him may have everlasting life.

question: How did God show he loved the world?
answer: He showed his love by giving his Only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have everlasting life.

question: Did God send his son to condemn the world?
answer: No. God sent his son so that the world should be saved through his son.

question: Why do men fall under judgment?
answer: Men fall under judgment because light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light because their works were evil.

question: Why wo not those who do evil come into the light?
answer: Those who do evil hate the light and will not come into it, because they do not want their deeds exposed.

question: Why do those who practice the truth come into the light?
answer: They come into the light so that their deeds may be clearly seen and to make known that their deeds have been brought about in obedience to God.

question: What did John say would happen to Jesus’ ministry compared to John’s ministry?
answer: John said, “He must increase, but I must decrease.”

question: What did those who accepted the testimony of the one from above, from heaven, confirm?
answer: They confirmed that God is true.

question: What has the Father given into the hand of the Son?
answer: He has given all things into the Son’s hand.

question: What do those who believe in the Son have?
answer: They have eternal light.

question: What happens to those who disobey the Son?
answer: They will not see life, but the wrath of God abides on them.

question: When did Jesus leave Judea and depart for Galilee?
answer: Jesus left Judea and departed for Galilee after he knew the Pharisees had heard that he was making and baptizing more disciples than John.

question: Where did Jesus come to on his way to Galilee?
answer: He came to a Samaritan town called Sychar.

question: Who came to Jacob’s well while Jesus was there?
answer: A Samaritan woman came there to draw water.

question: What did Jesus first say to the Samaritan Woman?
answer: He said to her, “Give me some water to drink.”

question: Where were Jesus’ disciples?
answer: They had gone away into town to buy food.

question: Why was the Samaritan woman surprised that Jesus would talk to her?
answer: She was surprised because Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans.

question: What does Jesus say to turn the conversation to the things of God?
answer: Jesus tells her that if she had known the gift of God and who was talking to her, she would have asked, and he would have given her living water.

question: What statement does the woman make to indicate she does not understand the spiritual nature of Jesus’ comments?
answer: The woman replied, “Sir, you do not have a bucket, and the well is deep. Where would you get that living water?”

question: What does Jesus tell the woman about the water that he will give?
answer: Jesus tells the woman that those who drink the water he gives will never thirst again, and the water will become a fountain of water springing up into eternal life.

question: Why does the woman now want this water that Jesus offers?
answer: She wants the water so she will not get thirsty and will not have to come to the well to draw water.

question: Jesus then changes the subject of conversation. What does he tell the woman?
answer: Jesus tells her, “Go, call your husband, and come back here.”

question: How does the woman answer Jesus when he tells her to call her husband?
answer: The woman tells Jesus she has no husband.

question: What does Jesus say about the woman which he could not know by natural means?
answer: He tells her she has had five husbands and the man she now has is not her husband.

question: What controversy does the woman bring up to Jesus concerning worship?
answer: She bring up a controversy about where is the proper place to worship.

question: What does Jesus tell the woman about the kind of worshipers the Father seeks?
answer: Jesus tells her God is a Spirit, and true worshipers must worship God in spirit and in truth.

question: What does Jesus say to the woman when she tells Jesus that when Messiah (Christ) comes, he will declare everything to them?
answer: Jesus tells her that he is the Messiah (Christ).

question: What did the woman do after her conversation with Jesus?
answer: The woman left her water pot, went back to town, and said to the people, “Come see a man who told me all things that I ever did. This could not be the Christ, could it?”

question: What did the town’s people do after they heard the woman’s report?
answer: They left the town and came to Jesus.

question: What does Jesus say his food is?
answer: Jesus said his food was to do the will of the one who sent him and to complete his work.

question: What is the benefit of harvesting?
answer: The harvester receives wages and gathers fruit for everlasting life, so that he who sows and he who harvests may rejoice together.

question: Why did many Samaritans in that city to believe in Jesus?
answer: The woman’s report caused many Samaritans in that city to believe in Jesus.

question: What did many of those Samaritans believe about Jesus?
answer: They said that they now knew that Jesus was indeed the Savior of the world.

question: When Jesus came into Galilee, why did the Galileans welcome him?
answer: They welcomed him because they had seen all the things that he had done in Jerusalem at the festival.

question: After Jesus left Judea and returned to Galilee, who came to Jesus, and what did he want?
answer: A certain royal official whose son was sick came to Jesus, imploring him to come down and heal his son.

question: What did Jesus tell the royal official about signs and wonders?
answer: Jesus told him people would not believe unless they saw signs and wonders.

question: What did the royal official do when Jesus did not go with him but told him, “Go; your son lives”?
answer: The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him, and he went his way.

question: What was the result after the father of the sick child was told that his son was living and that the fever had left him the day before at the seventh hour, at the same hour Jesus had told him, “Your son lives.”?
answer: The result was the royal official and his whole household believed.

question: What was the name of the pool in Jerusalem by the sheep gate that had five roofed porticos?
answer: That pool was called Bethesda.

question: Who was at Bethesda?
answer: A great number of people who were sick, blind, lame, or paralyzed were lying in the porticos of Bethesda.

question: At Bethesda, who did Jesus ask, “Do you want to be well?”?
answer: Jesus asked a certain man who had been an invalid for 38 years and who had been lying there a long time.

question: What was the sick man’s response to Jesus’ question, “Do you want to be well?”?
answer: The sick man replied, “Sir, I do not have anyone, when the water is stirred up, to put me into the pool. When I am trying, another steps down before me.”

question: What happened when Jesus said to the sick man, “Get up, take up your mat, and walk”?
answer: Immediately the man was healed, took up his bed, and walked.

question: Why did it upset the Jewish leaders when they saw the sick man walking with his bed (mat)?
answer: It upset them because it was a Sabbath, and they said the man was not permitted to carry his mat on the Sabbath.

question: What did Jesus say to the sick man he had healed after Jesus found him in the temple?
answer: Jesus told him, “See, you have become well! Do not sin any more, lest something worse happens to you.”

question: What did the healed man do after Jesus told him to stop sinning?
answer: The man went and told the Jewish leaders that it was Jesus who had made him well.

question: How did Jesus respond to the Jewish leaders who persecuted him because he was doing these things (healing) on the Sabbath?
answer: Jesus told them, “My Father is working even now, and I, too, work.”

question: Why did Jesus’ statement to the Jewish leaders make them want to kill Jesus?
answer: This happened because Jesus not only broke the Sabbath (in their minds), but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.

question: What did Jesus do?
answer: He did what he saw the Father doing.

question: What would the Father do so that the Jewish leaders would be amazed?
answer: The Father would show the Son greater things than these so that the Jewish leaders would be amazed.

question: Why did the Father give all judgment to the Son?
answer: The Father gave all judgment to the Son so that all may honor the Son even as they honor the Father.

question: What happens if you do not honor the Son?
answer: If you do not honor the Son, you do not honor the Father who sent him.

question: What happens if you believe Jesus’ word and believe in the Father who sent him?
answer: If so, you have eternal life and will not be condemned, but have passed out of death into life.

question: What has the Father given the Son concerning life?
answer: The Father has given to the Son to have life in himself.

question: What will happen when all who are in the tombs hear the Father’s voice?
answer: They will come forth. Those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.

question: Why is Jesus’ judgment righteous?
answer: His judgment is righteous because he is not seeking his own will but the will of the Father who sent him.

question: What testimony, greater than John’s, did Jesus have by which to prove he was sent from the Father?
answer: The works that Jesus did testified that he was sent from the Father.

question: Who had not heard the Father’s voice nor seen his form at any time?
answer: The Jewish leaders had neither heard his voice nor seen his form at any time.

question: Why did the Jewish leaders search the scriptures?
answer: They searched them because they thought that in them they had eternal life.

question: Who do the scriptures testify about?
answer: The scriptures testify concerning Jesus.

question: Who were the Jewish leaders not seeking praise from?
answer: They were not seeking the praise that comes from the only God.

question: Who was going to accuse the Jewish leaders before the Father?
answer: Moses was going to accuse the Jewish leaders before the Father.

question: What does Jesus say the Jewish leaders would do if they believed Moses?
answer: He says the Jewish leaders would believe in Jesus if they believed Moses, because Moses wrote concerning Jesus.

question: What was another name for the Sea of Galilee?
answer: The Sea of Galilee was also called the Sea of Tiberias.

question: Why was a great crowd following Jesus?
answer: They followed him because they were seeing the signs that Jesus was doing on those who were sick.

question: What did Jesus see after he sat down on the mountainside with his disciples and looked up?
answer: He saw a great crowd coming to him.

question: Why did Jesus ask Philip, “Where are we going to buy bread so that these may eat?”?
answer: Jesus said this to test Philip.

question: What was Philip’s response to Jesus’ question, “Where are we going to buy bread so that these may eat?”?
answer: Philip said, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be sufficient for each one to have even a little.”

question: What was Andrew’s response to Jesus’ question, “Where are we going to buy bread so that these may eat?”?
answer: Andrew said, “There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?”

question: About how many men were there in that place?
answer: There were about 5,000 men there.

question: What did Jesus do with the loaves and the fish?
answer: Jesus took the loaves and after giving thanks, he distributed to those who were sitting. He distributed the fish in the same way.

question: How much did the people get to eat?
answer: They got as much as they wanted to eat.

question: How much bread was picked up after the meal?
answer: The disciples filled 12 baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves—the pieces left over from those who had eaten.

question: Why did Jesus withdraw again up the mountain by himself?
answer: Jesus withdrew because he realized the people, after seeing the sign he did (feeding of the 5,000), were about to come and seize him by force and make him king.

question: What happened to the weather after the disciples got into a boat and started out for Capernaum?
answer: A strong wind began to blow and the sea started getting rough.

question: Why did the disciples begin to be afraid?
answer: They were afraid because they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat.

question: What did Jesus say to the disciples that made them willing to receive him into the boat?
answer: Jesus said to them, “It is I! Do not be afraid.”

question: What did Jesus say was the reason the crowd was seeking him?
answer: Jesus said they were seeking him not because they saw signs, but because they ate some of the loaves and were filled.

question: What did Jesus tell the crowd they should and should not work for?
answer: Jesus told them to stop working for the food that perishes, but work for the food that endures to everlasting life.

question: How did Jesus define the work of God for the crowd?
answer: Jesus told the crowd, “This is the work of God: that you believe in the one whom he has sent.”

question: What does Jesus say is the bread of life?
answer: Jesus says that he is the bread of life.

question: Who will come to Jesus?
answer: All whom the Father gives to Jesus will come to him.

question: What is the will of the Father who sent Jesus?
answer: The Father’s will is that Jesus should lose none that the Father has given him and that everyone who sees the son and believes in him should have eternal life; and Jesus will raise him up on the last day.

question: How can a man come to Jesus?
answer: A man can only come to Jesus if his Father draws him.

question: Who has seen the Father?
answer: Only he who is from God has seen the Father.

question: What is the bread that Jesus will give for the life of the world?
answer: The bread that Jesus will give for the life of the world is his own flesh.

question: What do you have to do to have life within yourself?
answer: In order to have life within yourself, you must eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood.

question: How can we remain in Jesus and Jesus remain in us?
answer: If we eat his flesh and drink his blood, we will remain in Jesus and he in us.

question: Why does Jesus live?
answer: Jesus lives because of the Father.

question: How did many of Jesus’ disciples respond after hearing Jesus teaching about eating his flesh and drinking his blood?
answer: When the disciples heard this teaching, many of them said, “This is a difficult teaching; who can accept it?”

question: What did Jesus know about people from the beginning?
answer: Jesus knew from the beginning who the ones were who would not believe and who it was who would betray him.

question: When Jesus asked the Twelve, “You do not want to go away also, do you?”, who answered and what did he say?
answer: Simon Peter answered him and said, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of everlasting life, and we have believed and come to know that you are the Holy One of God.”

question: Who did Jesus mean when he said one of the Twelve was a devil?
answer: Jesus spoke of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, for it was he, being one of the Twelve, who would betray Jesus.

question: Why was Jesus not willing to go into Judea?
answer: He was not willing to go there, because the Jews wanted to kill him.

question: Why did the brothers of Jesus urge him to go to Judea to the Festival of Shelters?
answer: They urged him to go so that Jesus’ disciples could see the deeds he was doing and so that the world would know.

question: What reason did Jesus give for not going to the festival?
answer: Jesus told his brothers his time had not yet come, and his time had not yet been fulfilled.

question: Why does the world hate Jesus?
answer: Jesus said the world hated him because he testifies about the world that its deeds are evil.

question: When and how did Jesus go up to the festival?
answer: Jesus went up after his brothers had gone up to the festival, but he went in private, not publicly.

question: What did the people in the crowd say about Jesus?
answer: Some said, “He is a good man.” Others said, “No, he leads the crowds astray.”

question: Why did no one speak openly about Jesus?
answer: It was for fear of the Jews that no one spoke openly about Jesus.

question: When did Jesus go up into the temple and begin teaching?
answer: When the festival was half over, Jesus went up into the temple and began teaching.

question: How did Jesus say one could know whether his teaching came from God or whether Jesus was speaking from himself?
answer: Jesus said if anyone wished to do the will of the person who sent Jesus, he would know about this teaching, whether it came from God or not.

question: What did Jesus say about the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him?
answer: Jesus said that person is true, and there is no unrighteousness in him.

question: According to Jesus, who does the law?
answer: Jesus said none of you does the law.

question: What is Jesus’ argument for healing on the Sabbath?
answer: Jesus’ argument was: You will circumcise a man on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses is not broken. Then why are you angry with me because I made a man completely well on the Sabbath.

question: How did Jesus tell the people to judge?
answer: Jesus told them not to judge according to appearance, but to judge righteously.

question: What was one of the arguments the people made for not believing Jesus was the Christ?
answer: The people said they knew where Jesus came from, but they said when Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from.

question: Who sent officers to arrest Jesus?
answer: The chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to arrest Jesus.

question: Did the Jews understand what Jesus meant when he said, “Yet a little while am I still with you, and then I go to him who sent me. You will seek me but will not find me; where I go, you will not be able to come.”?
answer: By their conversation among themselves, they indicated that they did not understand Jesus’ statement.

question: What was Jesus referring to when he said, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink. He who believes in me, as the scripture has said, from within him will flow rivers of living water”?
answer: Jesus said this about the Spirit, whom those who believed in him would receive.

question: How did the officers answer the chief priests and Pharisees who said to them, “Why did you not bring him (Jesus)?”?
answer: The officers answered, “No man has ever spoken like this before.”

question: How did Nicodemus answer the Pharisees when the Pharisees asked the officers sent to arrest Jesus, “Have you also been led astray? Have any of the rulers believed in him, or any of the Pharisees?”?
answer: Nicodemus said to the Pharisees, “Does our law judge a man unless it first hears from him and knows what he does?”

question: While Jesus was teaching the people in the temple, what did the scribes and Pharisees do?
answer: They brought in a woman caught in the act of adultery and placed her in their midst and asked Jesus what he had to say about her (to judge her).

question: Why did the scribes and Pharisees really bring this woman to Jesus?
answer: They really brought this woman to Jesus in order to trap Jesus so that they might have something to accuse him about.

question: What did Jesus say to the scribes and Pharisees after they kept asking Jesus about the woman caught in adultery?
answer: Jesus said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him be the first to throw a stone at her.”

question: What did the people do after Jesus spoke to them about who should be the first to throw a stone at the woman caught in adultery?
answer: After Jesus spoke, they went out one by one, beginning from the eldest and ending with the last.

question: What did Jesus tell the woman (caught in adultery) to do?
answer: Jesus told her to go her way and to sin no more from then on.

question: What was the Pharisees complaint after Jesus said, “I am the light of the world; he who follows me will not walk in the darkness but will have the light of life”?
answer: The Pharisees complained that Jesus was bearing witness about himself and that his witness was not true.

question: How did Jesus defend his witness as being true?
answer: Jesus said that in their law it is written that the testimony of two men is true. He then stated that he and the Father who sent him both bear witness about Jesus.

question: On what did Jesus base his statement about the Pharisees that they would die in their sins?
answer: Jesus based that statement on his knowledge of them, that they were from below, and he was from above. They were of this world and he was not of this world.

question: How could the Pharisee escape dying in their sins?
answer: Jesus said they would die in their sins unless they believed “that I am.”

question: What things did Jesus say to the world?
answer: Jesus said to the world the things he heard from the Father.

question: Why did the Father who sent Jesus stay with him and not leave him alone?
answer: The Father was with Jesus and did not leave him alone because Jesus always did the things that were pleasing to the Father.

question: How did Jesus say the Jews who had believed in him could know they were truly his disciples?
answer: They could know they were truly Jesus’ disciples by remaining in his word.

question: What did the Jews that believed Jesus think Jesus was referring to when he said, “… and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”?
answer: Those Jews thought Jesus was speaking of being slave of, or in bondage to, men.

question: What was Jesus referring to when he said, “and you shall know the truth and the truth will set you free”?
answer: Jesus was referring to being set free from being slaves of sin.

question: What is the reason, according to Jesus, the Jews sought to kill Jesus?
answer: They sought to kill Jesus because his word had no place in them.

question: Why did Jesus say these Jews were not Abraham’s children?
answer: Jesus said they were not Abraham’s children because they did not do the works of Abraham. Instead, they sought to kill Jesus.

question: When these Jews say they have one Father, God, how does Jesus refute them?
answer: Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would have loved me, for I came from God and am here; for neither have I come from myself, but that one sent me.”

question: Who does Jesus say is the father of these Jews?
answer: Jesus says their father is the devil.

question: What did Jesus say about the devil?
answer: Jesus said that the devil was a murderer from the beginning and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When the devil speaks a lie, he speaks from his own nature because he is a liar and the father of lies.

question: Who hears the words of God?
answer: He who is from God hears the words of God.

question: What does Jesus say will happen if anyone keeps Jesus’ word?
answer: If anyone keeps Jesus’ word, he will never see death.

question: Why did the Jews think Jesus’ statement about never seeing death was outlandish?
answer: They thought this because they were thinking of the physical death of the body. Even Abraham and the prophets died (their physical bodies).

question: Why did the Jews say Jesus had a demon?
answer: They said this because Jesus said, “Truly, truly, I say to you, if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death.”

question: What statements does Jesus make to say that he was alive before Abraham?
answer: Jesus said, “Truly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham was born, I AM.”

question: What is the assumption made by the disciples as to why the man was born blind?
answer: The disciples are assuming that the reason the man was born blind is because either the man or his parents had sinned.

question: What does Jesus say is the reason the man was born blind?
answer: Jesus says the man was born blind so that the works of God should be revealed in him.

question: What did Jesus do and say to the blind man?
answer: Jesus spit on the ground, made some mud and anointed the man’s eyes with the mud.

question: What happened after the blind man washed in the pool of Siloam?
answer: He came back seeing.

question: What did the man testify when a dispute arose as to whether or not he was the man born blind who used to sit and beg?
answer: The man testified that he was the blind beggar.

question: What did the people do who were with the formerly blind beggar?
answer: They took the man to the Pharisees.

question: When did the healing take place?
answer: The healing of the blind man took place on the Sabbath.

question: What did the Pharisees ask the formerly blind man?
answer: They asked him how he had received his sight.

question: What was the division that arose among the Pharisees?
answer: Some Pharisees said Jesus was not from God because he did not keep the Sabbath (he healed on the Sabbath) and some of the Pharisees said how could a man that is a sinner do such signs.

question: What did the formerly blind man say about Jesus when asked?
answer: The formerly blind man said, “He is a prophet.”

question: Why did the Jews call in the parents of the blind man that had received his sight?
answer: They called in the man’s parents because they still did not believe the man was the one that had been blind.

question: What did the parents of the man testify concerning their son?
answer: The parents testified that the man was indeed their son and that he had been born blind.

question: What did the man’s parents say they did not know?
answer: They said they did not know how he could now see, or who opened his eyes.

question: Why did the man’s parents say, “He is an adult. Ask him”?
answer: They said this because they were afraid of the Jews. For the Jews had already agreed that if anyone should confess Jesus to be the Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.

question: What did the Pharisees say to the formerly blind man when they called him in the second time?
answer: They said, “Give glory to God. We know this man (Jesus) is a sinner.”

question: What was the formerly blind man’s response to the Pharisees when they called Jesus a sinner?
answer: He replied, “Whether he is a sinner, I do not know. One thing I do know: Once I was blind, and now I see.”

question: What questions did the formerly blind man ask the Pharisees?
answer: The formerly blind man said, “Why do you want to hear it again? You do not want to become his disciples too, do you?”

question: When the Pharisees reviled the man, what did the formerly blind man say everyone knew?
answer: The formerly blind man said that everyone knew God does not listen to sinners.

question: How did the Pharisees respond to the blind man’s retort?
answer: They rebuked the man he was born in sin and yet he dared to teach them. Then they cast the man out of the synagogue.

question: What did Jesus say to the formerly blind man after Jesus found him?
answer: Jesus asked the man if he believed in the Son of Man, and then he told the formerly blind man that he (Jesus) was the Son of Man.

question: What did Jesus do when he heard the formerly blind man had been cast out of the synagogue?
answer: Jesus went looking for the man and found him.

question: How did the formerly blind man respond when told that Jesus was the Son of Man?
answer: The formerly blind man told Jesus he believed, and he worshiped Jesus.

question: What did Jesus say about the sins of the Pharisees?
answer: Jesus told them, “If you were blind, you would have no sin. However, now you say, ‘We see.’ So your sin remains.”

question: According to Jesus, who is a thief and a robber?
answer: He who does not enter by the gate into the sheepfold, but climbs up some other way, that man is a thief and a robber.

question: Who enters the sheepfold by the gate?
answer: He who enters the sheepfold by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.

question: Why do the sheep follow the shepherd when he calls them?
answer: They follow the shepherd because they know his voice.

question: Will the sheep follow a stranger?
answer: No. The sheep will not follow a stranger.

question: What were all those who came before Jesus came?
answer: All those who came before Jesus came were thieves and robbers, and the sheep did not listen to them.

question: Jesus said he was the gate. What happens to those who enter through that gate?
answer: Those who enter through Jesus, the gate, will be saved; they will go in and out and will find pasture.

question: What does the good shepherd, Jesus, do for his sheep?
answer: Jesus, the good shepherd, lays down his life for the sheep.

question: Does Jesus have another sheep fold, and if so, what will happen to them?
answer: Jesus said he had other sheep that were not of that fold. He said he must bring them, and they would hear his voice so that there would be one flock and one shepherd.

question: Why does the Father love Jesus?
answer: The Father loves Jesus because Jesus lays down his life that he may take it up again.

question: Does someone take Jesus’ life away?
answer: No. He lays if down of himself.

question: Where did Jesus get the authority to lay down his life and to take it again?
answer: Jesus received this command from his Father.

question: What did the Jews say because of Jesus’ words?
answer: Many said, “He has a demon and is insane. Why do you listen to him?” Others said, “These are not the statements of one possessed with a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”

question: What did the Jews say to Jesus when they surrounded him in the Temple in Solomon’s porch?
answer: They said, “How long will you hold us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”

question: How did Jesus reply to the Jews in Solomon’s porch?
answer: Jesus said he had already told them (that he was the Christ) and they did not believe him because they were not his sheep.

question: What does Jesus say about his care and protection of his sheep?
answer: Jesus said he gives his sheep eternal life, they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of his hand.

question: Who gave the sheep to Jesus?
answer: The Father gave the sheep to Jesus.

question: Is anyone greater than the Father?
answer: No. The Father is greater than all others.

question: Why did the Jews take up stones to stone Jesus?
answer: Because they believed Jesus was blaspheming and making himself God even though he was a man.

question: What is Jesus’ defense against the charge of blasphemy?
answer: Jesus defends himself by saying, “Is it not written in your law, ‘I said, “You are gods’”? If he called them gods, to whom the word of God came (and the scripture cannot be broken), do you say about him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, “You are blaspheming,” because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?”

question: What does Jesus tell the Jews to do in order to determine whether to believe him or not?
answer: Jesus tell the Jews to look at his works. If Jesus is not doing the works of his Father, do not believe him.

question: What does Jesus say the Jews could know and understand if they would believe in the works that Jesus did?
answer: Jesus said they could know and understand that the Father is in Jesus and that Jesus is in the Father.

question: What was the response of the Jews to Jesus statement about the Father being in Jesus and Jesus being in the Father?
answer: The Jews tried again to seize Jesus.

question: Where did Jesus go after this event?
answer: Jesus went away again beyond the Jordan to the place where John had been baptizing at first.

question: What did many people who came to Jesus say and do?
answer: They kept saying, “John indeed did no sign, but all that John said about this one was true.” Many people believed in Jesus there.

question: Who was this Lazarus? And who was Mary?
answer: Lazarus was a man from Bethany. His sisters were Mary and Martha. It was the same Mary who would anoint the Lord with myrrh and wipe his feet with her hair.

question: What did Jesus say about Lazarus and his sickness when Jesus heard he was sick?
answer: Jesus said, “This sickness is not to end in death, but it is instead for the glory of God so that the Son of God may be glorified in it.”

question: What did Jesus do when he heard Lazarus was sick?
answer: Jesus stayed two more days in the place where he was.

question: What did Jesus’ disciples say when he told them, “Let us go to Judea again.”?
answer: The disciples said to Jesus, “Rabbi, the Jews were only now trying to stone you, and are you going back there again?”

question: What did Jesus say about walking in the day?
answer: Jesus said if someone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble because he sees by the daylight.

question: What did Jesus say about walking in the night?
answer: If someone walks at night, he will stumble because the light is not in him.

question: In what way did the disciples think that Lazarus had fallen asleep?
answer: The disciples thought Lazarus had fallen asleep to rest.

question: What did Jesus mean when he said Lazarus had fallen asleep?
answer: When Jesus said Lazarus had fallen asleep, he was speaking of Lazarus’ death.

question: Why was Jesus glad that he was not there when Lazarus died?
answer: Jesus said, “I am glad for your sakes, that I was not there, so that you may believe.”

question: What did Thomas think would happen if they went back to Judea?
answer: Thomas thought they would all die.

question: How long had Lazarus been in the tomb when Jesus came?
answer: Lazarus had been in the tomb four days.

question: What did Martha do when she heard Jesus was coming?
answer: When Martha heard Jesus was coming, she went and met him.

question: What did Martha think God would do for Jesus?
answer: Martha said, “Even now, I know that whatever you ask from God, he will give to you.”

question: When Jesus said to Martha, “Your brother will rise again,” what was her response to Jesus?
answer: She said to Jesus, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”

question: What did Jesus say would happen to those who believe in him?
answer: Jesus said that whoever believes in Jesus, though he die, yet he will live; and whoever lives and believes in Jesus will never die.

question: What was Martha’s testimony about who Jesus is?
answer: Martha said to Jesus, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one who is coming into the world.”

question: Where was Mary going?
answer: Mary was going to meet Jesus.

question: When Mary got up quickly and went out, what did the Jews who were with her think and do?
answer: The Jews who were in the house with Mary supposed she was going to the tomb to weep there, so they followed her.

question: What seems to have prompted Jesus to groan in the spirit and be troubled and weep?
answer: Jesus groaned in the spirit was troubled and wept after he saw Mary weeping and the Jews who came with her weeping.

question: What did the Jews conclude when they saw Jesus weeping?
answer: They concluded that Jesus loved Lazarus.

question: What was Martha’s objection to Jesus’ command to take away the stone from the mouth of the cave where they had laid Lazarus?
answer: Martha said, “Lord, by this time the body will stink, for he has been dead four days.”

question: What is Jesus’ reply to Martha’s objection to taking away the stone?
answer: Jesus said to Martha, “Did I not say to you that, if you believed, you would see the glory of God.”

question: What did Jesus do immediately after the stone was taken away from the cave?
answer: Jesus lifted up his eyes and prayed aloud to his Father.

question: Why did Jesus pray aloud and say what he said to his Father?
answer: He prayed aloud and said what he did because of the crowd that was standing around him, so that they might believe that the Father had sent him.

question: What happened when Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”?
answer: The dead man came out, bound hand and foot with burial cloths, and his face was bound about with a cloth.

question: What was the response of the Jews when they saw Lazarus come out of the cave?
answer: Many of the Jews, when they saw what Jesus did, believed in him, but some went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.

question: In the council meeting of the chief priests and Pharisees, what did Caiaphas prophesy?
answer: Caiaphas said it was expedient for them that one man should die for the people rather than that the whole nation should perish.

question: From that day onward, what did the council plan?
answer: They planned how to put Jesus to death.

question: What did Jesus do after he raised Lazarus?
answer: Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews, but he departed from Bethany into the country near to the wilderness into a town called Ephraim. There he stayed with his disciples.

question: What order did the chief priests and Pharisees issue?
answer: They gave an order that if anyone knew where Jesus was, he should report it so that they might seize him.

question: When did Jesus come back to Bethany?
answer: He came to Bethany six days before the Passover.

question: What did Mary do at the supper which had been made for Jesus?
answer: Mary took a litra of perfume made of very precious pure nard, anointed the feet of Jesus with it, and wiped his feet with her hair.

question: Why did Judas Iscariot, one of Jesus’ disciples, complain that the perfume should have been sold and the money given to the poor?
answer: Judas said this not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief: He had charge of the money bag and would take some of what was in it for himself.

question: How did Jesus defend Mary’s use of the perfume (nard)?
answer: Jesus said, “Allow her to keep what she has for the day of my burial. The poor you will always have with you; but you will not always have me.”

question: Why did a large crowd gather in Bethany?
answer: They came for Jesus’ sake and also to see Lazarus, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.

question: Why did the chief priests want to put Lazarus to death?
answer: They wanted to put Lazarus to death because it was on account of him that many of the Jews went away and believed on Jesus.

question: What did the crowd at the festival do when they heard Jesus was coming?
answer: They took the branches of the palm trees and went out to meet him and cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the king of Israel.”

question: What prophecy about Jesus was fulfilled as Jesus entered the city on a donkey?
answer: The prophecy that Zion’s King would come, sitting on the young of a donkey was fulfilled.

question: Why did the crowd at the festival go out to meet Jesus?
answer: They went out to meet Jesus because they had heard from eye witnesses that Jesus had called Lazarus out of the tomb and had raised him from the dead.

question: What did Jesus say initially after Andrew and Philip told Jesus some Greeks wanted to see him?
answer: Jesus answered them and said, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.”

question: What did Jesus say would happen to a grain of wheat if it fell into the earth and died?
answer: Jesus said that if it died it would bear much fruit.

question: What did Jesus say would happen to the one who loves his life and to the one who hates his life in this world?
answer: Jesus said the one who love his life will lose it, but the one who hates his life in this world will keep it for everlasting life.

question: How will God treat anyone who serves Jesus?
answer: The Father will honor him.

question: What happened when Jesus said, “Father, glorify your name”?
answer: A voice came out of heaven and said, “I have glorified it and will glorify it again.”

question: What did Jesus say was the reason for the voice out of heaven?
answer: Jesus said that the voice was not for his own sake, but for the Jews.

question: What did Jesus say was going to happen now?
answer: Jesus said, “Now is the judgment of this world: Now will the prince of this world be thrown out.”

question: Why did Jesus say, “And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself”?
answer: Jesus said this to signify by what manner of death he would die.

question: When the crowd asked about what he had said, did Jesus directly answer them?
answer: No. he did not answer their questions directly.

question: What did Jesus say about the light?
answer: Jesus said, “Yet a little longer is the light among you. Walk while you have the light …” He also said, “While you have the light, believe in the light so that you may become sons of light.”

question: Why did the people not believe in Jesus?
answer: They did not believe so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he said: “Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

question: Why were the people not able to believe in Jesus?
answer: They were not able to believe because as Isaiah said, “He has blinded their eyes, and he has hardened their hearts; otherwise they would see with their eyes and would perceive with their hearts, and would turn, and I would heal them.”

question: Why did Isaiah say these things?
answer: He said these things because he saw Jesus’ glory and spoke about him.

question: Why did the rulers who did believe in Jesus not admit it?
answer: They would not admit it, because they were afraid of the Pharisees and did not want to be banned from the synagogue. They loved the praise that comes from people more than the praise that comes from God.

question: What statement does Jesus make about himself and his Father?
answer: Jesus said, “The one who believes in me, believes not only in me but also in him who sent me, and the one who sees me sees him who sent me.”

question: What did Jesus say he had come into the world to do?
answer: Jesus said he came to save the world.

question: What will judge those who reject Jesus and do not receive his words?
answer: The word that Jesus has spoken will judge those who reject him on the last day.

question: Did Jesus speak of his own accord?
answer: No. The Father who sent Jesus commanded him what he should say and speak.

question: Why did Jesus say to the people just what the Father had said to him?
answer: Jesus did this because he knew his Father’s command is life everlasting.

question: How long did Jesus love his own?
answer: He loved them to the end.

question: What had the devil done to Judas Iscariot?
answer: The devil had put it into the heart of Judas Iscariot to betray Jesus.

question: What had the Father given to Jesus?
answer: The Father gave all things over into the hands of Jesus.

question: Where had Jesus come from and where was he going?
answer: Jesus had come from God and was going back to God.

question: What did Jesus do when he rose from supper?
answer: He laid aside his outer clothing, took a towel and wrapped it around himself, poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and to wipe them with the towel.

question: What did Jesus say when Peter objected to having his feet washed by Jesus?
answer: Jesus said, “If I do not wash you, you can have no part with me.”

question: Why did Jesus say to his disciples, “Not all of you are clean”?
answer: Jesus said this because he knew who would betray him.

question: Why did Jesus wash the disciples feet?
answer: Jesus washed the disciples feet to give the disciples an example so that they should do for each other as he did for them.

question: Is the servant greater than his master or the one sent greater than the one who sent him?
answer: The servant is not greater than his master and the one sent is not greater than the one who sent him.

question: Who lifted up his heel against Jesus?
answer: The one who ate Jesus’ bread lifted up his heel against him.

question: Why did Jesus tell his disciples, “Not all of you are clean” and “He who eats my bread lifted up his heel against me”?
answer: Jesus told them this before it happened so that when it did happen, they might believe he is the I AM.

question: Who will you receive if you receive whomever Jesus sends?
answer: If you receive whomever Jesus sends, you will receive Jesus, and you also receive the one who sent Jesus.

question: When Jesus told his disciples that one of them would betray him, what did Simon Peter do?
answer: Simon Peter motioned to the disciple whom Jesus loved and said, “Tell us who it is of whom he is speaking.”

question: How did Jesus respond when the disciple whom Jesus loved asked Jesus who was going to betray Jesus?
answer: Jesus answered, “He it is for whom I will dip the piece of bread and give it to him.” Then Jesus dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot.

question: What happened to Judas and what did he do after Jesus gave Judas the bread?
answer: After Judas took the bread, Satan entered into him, and he went out immediately.

question: What happened to Judas and what did he do after Jesus gave Judas the bread?
answer: After Judas took the bread, Satan entered into him and he went out immediately.

question: How was God going to be glorified?
answer: God was going to be glorified in the Son of Man. When the Son of Man was glorified, that glorified God.

question: Did Simon Peter understand where Jesus was going when Jesus told them, “Where I am going, you cannot come”?
answer: No, Simon Peter did not understand, because he asked Jesus, “Lord, where are you going?”

question: What new commandment did Jesus give his disciples?
answer: The new commandment was that they should love one another as Jesus had loved them.

question: What did Jesus say would happen if his disciples obeyed the commandment to love one another?
answer: Jesus said that by them obeying this commandment, all people would know that they were his disciples.

question: How did Jesus answer when Simon Peter said, “I will lay down my life for you”?
answer: Jesus answered, “Will you lay down your life for me? Truly, truly, I say to you, the rooster will not crow before you have denied me three times.”

question: Why should the hearts of the disciples not be troubled?
answer: Their hearts should not be troubled because Jesus is going to prepare a place for them, and Jesus will come again to receive them to himself so that where Jesus is they may be also.

question: What is in the Father’s house?
answer: There are many dwelling places in the Father’s house.

question: What was Jesus going to do for the disciples?
answer: Jesus was going to prepare a place for them and then come back for them.

question: What is the only way to come to the Father?
answer: The only way to come to the Father is through Jesus.

question: What does Philip tell Jesus to do that would be enough for the disciples?
answer: Philip says to Jesus, “Lord show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.”

question: Is Jesus speaking to the disciples of his own accord?
answer: Jesus is not speaking of his own accord. Instead, it is the Father living in him who is doing the Father’s work.

question: If for no other reason, why does Jesus say the disciples should believe that Jesus is in the Father and the Father is in Jesus?
answer: Jesus says they should believe this if for no other reason then because of Jesus’ very works.

question: Why does Jesus say the disciples will be able to do even greater works than he did?
answer: Jesus says the disciples will do even greater works because Jesus is going to the Father.

question: Why will Jesus do whatever the disciples ask in his name?
answer: Jesus will do it so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

question: What does Jesus say you will do if you love him?
answer: Jesus says you will keep his commandments if you love him.

question: What does Jesus call the other comforter that the Father will give to be with the disciples forever?
answer: Jesus calls him the Spirit of Truth.

question: Why can the world not receive the Spirit of Truth?
answer: The world cannot receive the Spirit of Truth, because it does not see him or know him.

question: Where does Jesus say the Spirit of Truth will be?
answer: Jesus said the Spirit of Truth would remain with and be in the disciples.

question: What will happen to whoever has Jesus’ commandments and keeps them?
answer: Those people will be loved by Jesus and his Father and Jesus will show himself to those people.

question: What will the Helper, the Holy Spirit, do when the Father sends him?
answer: The Helper, the Holy Spirit, will teach the disciples all things and bring to their remembrance all the Jesus said to them.

question: Why should the disciples have rejoiced that Jesus was going away?
answer: Jesus said they should rejoice because Jesus was going to the Father, for the Father is greater than Jesus.

question: What reason does Jesus give for saying he will not speak much more with the disciples?
answer: The reason Jesus gives is that the prince of this world is coming.

question: Who is the true vine?
answer: Jesus is the true vine.

question: Who is the vine grower?
answer: The Father is the vine grower.

question: What does the Father do with the branches who are in Christ?
answer: The Father takes away the branches that bear no fruit, and he prunes every branch that bears fruit so that it may bear more fruit.

question: Why are the disciples clean?
answer: They are clean because of the message Jesus spoke to them.

question: Who are the branches?
answer: We are the branches.

question: What must we do to bear fruit?
answer: In order to bear fruit you must remain in Jesus.

question: What happens if you do not remain in Jesus?
answer: If anyone does not remain in Jesus, he is thrown away like a branch, dries up, and is burnt up.

question: What must we do so that whatever we ask will be done for us?
answer: We must remain in Jesus and his word must remain in us. Then we may ask whatever we wish, and it will be done for us.

question: What are two ways the Father is glorified?
answer: The Father is glorified when we bear much fruit and when we are disciples of Jesus.

question: What must we do to remain in the love of Jesus?
answer: We must keep his commandments.

question: What is the greatest love a person can have?
answer: No one has greater love than this, that he should lay down his life for his friends.

question: How do we know if we are Jesus’ friends or not?
answer: We are friends of Jesus if we do the things he commanded us.

question: Why did Jesus call the disciples his friends?
answer: He called them friends, for he made known to them all the things that he heard from his Father.

question: Why does the world hate those who follow Jesus?
answer: The world hates those who follow Jesus because they are not of this world and because Jesus chose them out of the world.
