question: What did Jesus do so that the world has no excuse for their sin?
answer: The world has no excuse for their sin because Jesus came and did among them the works that no one else did.

question: Who will bear witness about Jesus?
answer: The Helper, that is the Spirit of Truth, would bear witness about Jesus.

question: Why would the disciples bear witness about Jesus?
answer: They would bear witness about Jesus because they had been with him from the beginning.

question: Why did Jesus speak these things to the disciples?
answer: Jesus spoke these things to them so that they should not be made to stumble.

question: Why will people put the disciples of Jesus out of the synagogues and kill some of them?
answer: They will do this because they have not known the Father or Jesus.

question: Why did Jesus not tell the disciples about these things in the beginning?
answer: Jesus did not tell them in the beginning because he was with them.

question: Why is it better for Jesus to go away?
answer: It is better for Jesus to go away because the Comforter will not come to them unless Jesus goes away; but if Jesus goes away, Jesus will send the Comforter to them.

question: Regarding what will the Comforter convict the world?
answer: The Comforter will convict the world regarding sin, righteousness, and judgment.

question: What will the Spirit of Truth do for the disciples when he comes?
answer: He will guide the disciples into all truth; for he will not speak from himself; but whatever things he hears, he will say those things and will declare to them the things that are to come.

question: How will the Spirit of Truth glorify Jesus?
answer: He will glorify Jesus by taking things of Jesus and declaring them to the disciples.

question: What will the Spirit of Truth do with the things of Jesus?
answer: The Spirit of Truth will take the things of Jesus and announce them to the disciples.

question: What sayings of Jesus did the disciples not understand?
answer: They did not understand when Jesus said, “In a little while, you will see me no more; after a little while again, you will see me,” and when he said, “Because I go to the Father.”

question: What will happen to the disciples’ sorrow?
answer: It will be turned to joy.

question: What will happen to cause the disciples to rejoice?
answer: They will see Jesus again, and their hearts will rejoice.

question: Why does Jesus tell the disciples to ask and receive?
answer: Jesus says to do this so that their joy may be full.

question: For what reason does the Father himself love the disciples of Jesus?
answer: The Father loves the disciples because the disciples loved Jesus and believed that he came from the Father.

question: Where did Jesus come from and where was he going?
answer: Jesus came into the world from the Father and was going to leave the world and return to the Father.

question: What did Jesus say the disciples would do at that hour?
answer: Jesus said the disciples would be scattered, everyone to his own possessions, and they would leave Jesus all alone.

question: Who was still going to be with Jesus after the disciples left him alone?
answer: The Father was still going to be with Jesus.

question: Why did Jesus tell the disciples to be encouraged even though in the world they would have troubles?
answer: Jesus told them to be encouraged because he had overcome the world.

question: Why did the Father give Jesus authority over all flesh?
answer: The Father did this so that Jesus would give eternal life to all whom the Father have given him.

question: What is eternal life?
answer: Eternal life is knowing the Father, the only true God, and him whom he has sent, Jesus Christ.

question: How did Jesus glorify God on the earth?
answer: He did this by accomplishing the work that the Father gave him to do.

question: What glory does Jesus want?
answer: He wants the glory he had with the Father before the world was created.

question: To whom did Jesus reveal the Father’s name?
answer: Jesus revealed the Father’s name to the people the Father gave to Jesus from the world.

question: How did those people the Father gave to Jesus respond to Jesus’ words?
answer: They received Jesus’ words and truly knew that Jesus came from the Father and they believed that the Father sent Jesus.

question: Who does Jesus say he is not praying for?
answer: Jesus says he is not praying for the world.

question: In brief, what does Jesus ask the Father to do for those the Father has given to Jesus?
answer: Jesus asks the Father to keep them in the Father’s name so they may be one just as the Father and Son are one.

question: While Jesus was in the world, what did Jesus do for those the Father had given to him?
answer: Jesus protected them, so that none perished.

question: In brief, what does Jesus ask the Father to do for those the Father has given to Jesus?
answer: Jesus asks the Father to keep them from the evil one.

question: Why did Jesus sanctify himself?
answer: Jesus sanctified himself so that those the Father gave him might also be sanctified in truth.

question: For whom else does Jesus pray?
answer: Jesus prays for people who will believe in him through the word of those who followed him at that time.

question: What does Jesus ask the Father to do for those the Father has given to Jesus?
answer: Jesus asks the Father to keep them in the Father’s name so they may be one, for them to be one in both Jesus and the Father so that the world would believe God sent Jesus.

question: How does the Father love those he gave to Jesus?
answer: The Father loves them even as he loved Jesus.

question: What does Jesus ask the Father to do for those the Father has given to Jesus?
answer: Jesus asks that his followers may be with him where he is, to see his glory.

question: Why did and will Jesus make the Father’s name known to those the Father has given to him?
answer: Jesus did and will make it known so that the love with which the Father loved Jesus may be in them and that Jesus may be in them.

question: After Jesus spoke these words, where did he go?
answer: He went with his disciples across the Kidron brook to a garden, and he entered it.

question: How did Judas know about the garden?
answer: He knew about it because Jesus often went there with his disciples.

question: Who else came to the garden with lanterns, torches and weapons?
answer: Judas, leading a group of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, also came to the garden.

question: What did Jesus ask this group of people in the garden?
answer: Jesus asked them, “For whom are you looking?”

question: What happened when the group of people said they were looking for Jesus of Nazareth and Jesus responded, “I am”?
answer: The soldiers and others with them went backward and fell to the ground.

question: Why did Jesus say, “I told you that I am he; so if you are looking for me, let these others go”?
answer: Jesus said this so that the word might be fulfilled that he said: “Of those whom you have given me, I lost not one.”

question: What did Jesus tell Peter after Peter cut off the ear of Malchus, the servant of the high priest?
answer: Jesus said to Peter, “Put your sword back into its sheath. The cup that the Father has given me, should I not drink it?”

question: After the group of soldiers, their captain and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus, where did they take him?
answer: They first took Jesus to Annas.

question: Who was Annas?
answer: Annas was the father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.

question: How did Peter get into the courtyard of the high priest?
answer: Another disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman servant who was guarding the door, and he brought in Peter.

question: Who asked Peter if he was a disciple of Jesus?
answer: The woman guarding the door to the courtyard, the people standing around the fire of coals and one of the servants of the high priest, who was a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, all asked Peter if he was with Jesus or a disciple of Jesus.

question: In brief how did Jesus answer when the high priest asked Jesus about his disciples and his teaching?
answer: Jesus said he spoke openly to the world in public. He told the chief priest to ask those who heard him about what he said.

question: After Annas questioned Jesus where did he send Jesus?
answer: Annas sent Jesus to Caiaphas the high priest.

question: What happened immediately after Peter denied being associated with Christ for the third time?
answer: Immediately after the third time Peter denied being associated with Christ, the rooster crowed.

question: Why did those who took Jesus to the Praetorium not enter it?
answer: They did not enter the Praetorium so that they might not be defiled and so that they might eat the Passover.

question: How did Jesus’ accusers answer Pilate when he asked them, “What accusation are you bringing against this man?”?
answer: They answered and said to him, “If this man were not an evil doer, we would not have delivered him up to you.”

question: Why did the Jews take Jesus to Pilate instead of punishing Jesus themselves?
answer: The Jews wanted to kill Jesus, but it was not lawful for them to put any man to death without permission from the Roman authorities (Pilate).

question: What did Pilate ask Jesus?
answer: Pilate asked Jesus, “Are you the King of the Jews?”

question: What did Jesus tell Pilate about Jesus’ kingdom?
answer: Jesus told Pilate that his kingdom is not part of this world and does not come from here.

question: For what purpose was Jesus born?
answer: Jesus was born to be a king and to bear witness to the truth.

question: What is Pilate’s judgment about Jesus after talking with him?
answer: Pilate said to the Jews, “I find no guilt in this man.”

question: When Pilate offered to release Jesus, what did the Jews cry out to Pilate?
answer: The Jews cried out again and said, “Not this man, but Barabbas.”

question: What did the soldiers do to Jesus after Pilate had Jesus whipped?
answer: The soldiers twisted thorns together to make a crown, put it on Jesus’ head, and dressed him in a purple garment. They came to him and said, “Hail, king of the Jews!” and they struck him with their hands.

question: Why did Pilate bring Jesus out to the people again?
answer: Pilate brought Jesus out to the people so that they would know that Pilate found no guilt in Jesus.

question: What was Jesus wearing when Pilate brought him back out to the people?
answer: Jesus was wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment.

question: What did the chief priests and the officers say when they saw Jesus?
answer: They cried out and said, “Crucify him, crucify him!”

question: What did the Jews say that made Pilate even more afraid?
answer: The Jews told Pilate, “We have a law, and by that law he ought to die because he made himself the Son of God.”

question: What did Jesus say when Pilate asked Jesus, “From where do you come?”?
answer: Jesus gave Pilate no answer.

question: Who did Jesus say gave Pilate power over Jesus?
answer: Jesus said, “You would have no power against me, unless it had been given you from above.”

question: Although Pilate wanted to release Jesus, what did the Jews say that prevented him?
answer: The Jews cried out saying, “If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar.”

question: What was the last thing the chief priests said before Pilate handed Jesus over to them to be crucified?
answer: The chief priests said, “We have no king but Caesar.”

question: Where did they crucify Jesus?
answer: They crucified Jesus at Golgotha, which means “The Place of a Skull.”

question: Was Jesus the only one crucified there that day?
answer: No. Two other men, one on each side of Jesus, were crucified with him.

question: What did Pilate write on the sign that was put on the cross of Jesus?
answer: On the sign he wrote, “JESUS THE NAZARENE, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”

question: In what languages was the sign on Jesus’ cross written?
answer: The sign was written in Hebrew, Latin and Greek.

question: Why did the soldiers do what they did with Jesus’ garments?
answer: This happened so that the Scripture might be fulfilled that said, “They divided my garments among themselves.”

question: What did the soldiers do with Jesus’ garments?
answer: The soldiers divided up Jesus’ garments into four parts, a part for each soldier. But they cast lots to see who would get Jesus’ shirt, which was without seams.

question: What did the soldiers do with Jesus’ garments?
answer: The soldiers divided up Jesus’ garments into four parts, a part for each soldier. But they cast lots to see who would get Jesus’ shirt, which was without seams.

question: Who was standing near the cross of Jesus?
answer: Jesus’ mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, Mary Magdalene, and the disciple whom Jesus loved were standing near the cross of Jesus.

question: What did Jesus tell his mother when he saw his mother and the disciple he loved standing nearby?
answer: Jesus told her, “Woman, see, here is your son!”

question: What did the disciple Jesus loved do after Jesus told him, “See, here is your mother!”?
answer: From that hour the disciple Jesus loved took Jesus’ mother to his own home.

question: Why did Jesus say, “I am thirsty”?
answer: Jesus said this in order to make the scriptures come true.

question: What did Jesus do after he had taken the vinegar from the sponge that was held up to his mouth?
answer: After taking the vinegar, Jesus said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

question: Why did the Jews want Pilate to break the legs of the executed men?
answer: It was the Preparation, and in order that the bodies should not remain on the cross during the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was an important day), the Jews asked Pilate that the legs of the executed men be broken so they would die quickly and that their bodies might be taken down.

question: Why did the soldiers not break Jesus’ legs?
answer: They did not break Jesus’ legs, because they saw he was already dead.

question: What did the soldiers do to Jesus after they saw that he was already dead?
answer: One of the soldiers pierced Jesus’ side with a spear, so that blood and water came out.

question: Why did the one who saw all these things concerning the crucifixion of Jesus bear witness to them?
answer: That one bore witness to these events so that you also may believe.

question: Why were the legs of Jesus not broken and why was Jesus pierced with a spear?
answer: These things came about so that the scripture might be fulfilled, “Not a single bone of him will be broken.” and again, “They will look on him whom they pierced.”

question: Who came and asked to take away the body of Jesus?
answer: Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus.

question: Who came with Joseph of Arimathea to take away the body of Jesus?
answer: Nicodemus came with Joseph of Arimathea.

question: What did Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus do with the body of Jesus?
answer: They wrapped Jesus’ body in linen cloths with spices. Then they laid Jesus’ body in a new tomb which was in a garden.

question: When did Mary Magdalene come to the tomb?
answer: She came to the tomb very early on the first day of the week.

question: What did Mary Magdalene see when she got to the tomb?
answer: She saw that the stone had been rolled away from the tomb.

question: What did Mary Magdalene say to the two disciples?
answer: She told them, “They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid him.”

question: What did Simon Peter and the other disciple do after they heard what Mary Magdalene said?
answer: They both went to the tomb.

question: What did Simon Peter see in the tomb?
answer: Peter saw the linen cloths lying there. The cloth that had been on his head was not lying with the linen cloths but was folded up in its place by itself.

question: What was the response of the other disciple to what he saw in the tomb?
answer: He saw and believed.

question: What did Mary see when she stooped and looked into the tomb?
answer: She saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head, and one at the foot, where the body of Jesus had lain.

question: What did the angels say to Mary?
answer: They asked her, “Woman, why are you weeping?”

question: When Mary turned around, what did she see?
answer: She saw Jesus standing there, but she did not know that it was Jesus.

question: Who did Mary think Jesus was?
answer: She thought he was the gardener.

question: When did Mary recognize Jesus?
answer: She recognized Jesus when he said her name, “Mary.”

question: Why did Jesus tell Mary not to hold on to him?
answer: Jesus told her not to hold on to him because he had not yet ascended to the Father.

question: What did Jesus tell Mary to say to his brothers?
answer: Jesus told her to say to his brothers, that he will ascend to his Father and their Father, and his God and their God.

question: What did Mary Magdalene do after she saw the stone rolled away from the tomb?
answer: She ran and told the other disciples Jesus’ message for them.

question: What happened where the disciples were on the evening of the first day of the week?
answer: Jesus came and stood in the midst of them.

question: What did Jesus show the disciples?
answer: He showed them his hands and his side.

question: What did Jesus tell the disciples that he would do?
answer: Jesus said he was sending the disciples just as his Father had sent him.

question: What did Jesus say to his disciples after he breathed on them?
answer: He told them, “Receive the Holy Spirit. Whoever’s sins you forgive, they are forgiven for them; whoever’s sins you keep back, they are kept back.”

question: Which one of the disciples was not present with the other disciples when they saw Jesus?
answer: Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with the other disciples when Jesus came.

question: What did Thomas say it would take for him to believe that Jesus was alive?
answer: Thomas said he would have to see the print of the nails in Jesus’ hands and put his fingers into the nail prints and put his hand into Jesus’ side before he would believe.

question: When did Thomas see Jesus?
answer: Eight days later, while the doors were shut, Thomas was with the other disciples when Jesus came and stood among them.

question: What did Jesus tell Thomas to do?
answer: Jesus told Thomas to reach with his finger and see Jesus’ hands and reach with his hand and put it into Jesus’ side. Jesus then told Thomas not to be faithless, but believe.

question: What did Thomas say to Jesus?
answer: Thomas said, “My Lord and my God.”

question: Who did Jesus say was blessed?
answer: Jesus said, “Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”

question: Did Jesus do other signs that were not written in the book?
answer: Yes, Jesus did many other signs in the presence of the disciples that were not written in the book of John.

question: Why were the signs written in the book?
answer: They were written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that as you believe, you may have life in his name.

question: Where were the disciples when Jesus showed himself to them again?
answer: The disciples were at the Sea of Tiberias when Jesus showed himself to them again.

question: Which disciples were at the Sea of Tiberias?
answer: Simon Peter, Thomas, called Didymus, Nathaniel from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee and two of Jesus’ other disciples were at the Sea of Tiberias.

question: What were these disciples doing?
answer: These disciples had gone fishing but had caught nothing all night.

question: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do?
answer: Jesus told the disciples to cast their net on the right side of the boat and they would catch some fish.

question: What happened when the disciples cast their net?
answer: They could not draw in their net because there were so many fish in it.

question: What did Simon Peter do when the disciple Jesus loved said, “It is the Lord”?
answer: He tucked up his outer garment about himself and threw himself into the sea.

question: What did the other disciples do?
answer: The other disciples came in the boat, pulling the net full of fish.

question: What did Jesus tell the disciples to do with some of the fish that they had caught?
answer: Jesus told the disciples to bring some of the fish they had just caught.

question: How many times had Jesus now shown himself to the disciples since he had risen?
answer: This was the third time Jesus had now shown himself to the disciples since he had risen.

question: After breakfast, what was the first thing Jesus asked Simon Peter?
answer: Jesus asked Simon Peter if Simon loved Jesus more than these.

question: How did Simon Peter answer Jesus the third time Jesus asked Peter if he loved Jesus?
answer: The third time he was asked, Peter responded, “Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you.”

question: The third time Peter responds to Jesus’ question, “Do you love me?” what does Jesus tell Peter to do?
answer: The third time, Jesus told him, “Feed my sheep.”

question: What did Jesus tell Simon Peter was going to happen to him when Simon became old?
answer: Jesus told Simon Peter that when he became old, he would stretch out his hands and another person would clothe him and carry him where he did not wish to go.

question: Why did Jesus tell Peter what was going to happen to Peter when he became old?
answer: Jesus said this in order to signal by what kind of death Peter would glorify God.

question: What did Simon Peter ask Jesus concerning the disciple that Jesus loved?
answer: Peter asked Jesus, “Lord, what will this man do?”

question: How did Jesus respond to Peter’s question, “Lord, what will this man do?”?
answer: Jesus told Peter, “You follow me.”

question: Who wrote this book and to what does he bear witness?
answer: The disciple Jesus loved wrote this book and bears witness that the events described in the book are true.

question: How is Job’s character described?
answer: He was blameless and righteous and honored God and turned from evil.

question: After Job’s sons held feasts with their brothers and sisters in their houses, what would Job do?
answer: Job would consecrate them to God, offer burnt offerings, and pray for them.

question: Why did Yahweh say Satan should consider Job?
answer: There was no one like Job on the earth, a blameless and upright man, one who feared God and turned away from evil.

question: How did Satan say Yahweh had protected Job?
answer: He made a hedge around Job, around his house, and around all that he had on every side.

question: What did Satan think would cause Job to renounce God?
answer: He said to Job would renounce God if God attacked all Job’s possessions.

question: What did Yahweh give Satan permission to do?
answer: He gave Satan permission to take everything from Job, but not to lay a hand on his person.

question: What did the messenger tell Job the Sabeans had done to him?
answer: They killed all Job’s servants in the field and took away all the oxen and donkeys.

question: What did the second messenger tell Job had happened to his sheep?
answer: The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned them up along with the servants.

question: What did the third messenger tell Job had happened to his camels?
answer: Three groups of robbers came and attacked them. They stole all the camels and killed all the men that were caring for them.

question: What news did the fourth messenger bring to Job?
answer: Job’s sons and daughters were feasting in their brother’s home when a great wind came and struck the house, which collapsed on them and killed them.

question: What did Job do after he got all these messages?
answer: Job tore his robe, shaved his head, lay facedown on the ground, and worshiped God.

question: What did Job say about his condition after these events?
answer: He said he came naked from his mother’s womb, and he would return naked.

question: What did Job say that Yahweh had done to him?
answer: Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away.

question: How did Job show that he was not a foolish man?
answer: Job did not sin, nor did he foolishly accuse God.

question: Who came with the sons of God when they presented themselves before Yahweh?
answer: Satan also came and presented himself.

question: What did Satan tell Yahweh that he had been doing?
answer: He said he was going to and fro on the earth, and walking back and forth on it.

question: How did Yahweh say that Job continued to do after Satan’s attacks?
answer: Job held fast to his integrity.

question: What does Satan want to do to Job now so that Job will curse God?
answer: Satan wants to touch Job’s bones and his body to hurt him.

question: How did Satan afflict Job’s body?
answer: He afflicted Job with severe boils from the sole of his foot to the top of his head.

question: What did Job do to deal with the pain of his affliction?
answer: He took a potshard and scraped himself as he sat in ashes.

question: What did Job’s wife want him to do?
answer: Job’s wife wanted him to curse God and die.

question: What accusation did Job make to his wife?
answer: He accused her of thinking they should receive good at the hand of God but not evil.

question: What did Job’s three friends do when they heard what happened to Job?
answer: They came to mourn with him and comfort him.

question: How did the three friends of Job show their grief when they saw him?
answer: They raised their voices and wept, tore their robes, threw dust on their heads, and sat on the ground in silence for seven days and nights.

question: What did Job say about the day he was born?
answer: He cursed the day he was born and asked that it would perish.

question: What does Job want to claim the day he was born?
answer: He wants that day to be claimed by darkness and the shadow of death.

question: What does Job want to seize the night he was conceived?
answer: Job wants that night to be seized by gloom.

question: What did Job wish had happened when he came out of the womb?
answer: He wishes he had died at birth.

question: What does Job say he would be doing now if he had died at birth?
answer: He would be sleeping and at rest with kings and counselors of the earth.

question: From what are prisoners and servants released in death?
answer: The prisoner is released from the voice of the slave driver, and the servant is free from his master.

question: To whom does Job say that death will not come?
answer: It does not come to the one who longs for death and who searches for it more than those who search for hidden treasure.

question: How does Job describe his groaning?
answer: His groaning flows out like water.

question: What are the things that troubles have replaced in Job’s life?
answer: He cannot be at ease or quiet and has no rest.

question: What good things does Eliphaz say Job has done for others?
answer: Job had instructed many and strengthened weak hands.

question: What does Eliphaz say is Job’s confidence and hope in time of trouble?
answer: Job’s fear of God is his confidence, and the integrity of his ways is his hope.

question: Who perishes by the breath of God and his anger?
answer: Those who plow misery and sow trouble perish and cease to exist.

question: What does Eliphaz says is broken?
answer: The teeth of young lions are broken.

question: How did Eliphaz secretly receive a certain message?
answer: He heard a whisper in his ear and saw visions in the night.

question: What came upon Eliphaz when he received the message?
answer: Fear and trembling came on him.

question: What did the voice ask about mortal men?
answer: It asked if a mortal man can be more righteous than God, more pure than his Maker.

question: How does Eliphaz describe mortal men?
answer: They live in houses of clay with their foundation in the dust, and they are crushed sooner than a moth.

question: What does Eliphaz say will happen to a foolish and simple man?
answer: Indignation kills the foolish man, and resentment kills the simple one.

question: What happens to the children of the foolish person in the city gate?
answer: They are unsafe, they are crushed in the gate and are not rescued.

question: From where does trouble really come?
answer: All his life, man makes his own trouble.

question: What does God give to the earth and the fields?
answer: He gives rain on the earth and sends water on the fields.

question: What does God do the schemes of crafty people?
answer: He frustrates their schemes so that their hands cannot carry out their plots.

question: From what does God save the needy and poor person?
answer: He saves the poor person from the threats and accusations of the mighty and saves the needy person from harm by the mighty people.

question: Why is the man happy whom God corrects and chastens?
answer: He is happy because the wounds, God binds up wounds, and his hands heal.

question: At what will the man whom God corrects laugh?
answer: He will laugh at destruction and famine.

question: What will the man whom God corrects find when he visits his sheepfold?
answer: He will find that nothing will be missing.

question: How long will the man whom God corrects live?
answer: He will come to his grave at a full age.

question: How does Job describe his anguish and his calamity?
answer: If his anguish and calamity were weighed, they would be heavier than the sand of the seas.

question: What has the Almighty done to Job with his arrows?
answer: His arrows are in Job, and Job’s spirit drinks up the poison.

question: What food does Job say has no taste?
answer: He says the white of an egg does not have any taste.

question: What one request does Job long for God to grant him?
answer: He wants God to crush him and cut him loose from his life.

question: What is Job’s consolation?
answer: His consolation is that he has not have denied the words of the Holy One.

question: What has been taken away from Job?
answer: Initiative has been taken away from him.

question: To whom should a friend show faithfulness?
answer: A friend should show faithfulness to the despairing person.

question: How does Job compare his brothers to a desert streambed?
answer: They have dealt treacherously like a wadi: they disappear in the dry season.

question: What happened to the caravans when they looked for water in these streams?
answer: They wandered into barren land and then perished. They were disappointed and deceived.

question: Why were Job’s friends nothing to him?
answer: They saw his dreadful situation and were afraid, so they did not help him.

question: What does Job say he will do if his friends would teach him?
answer: He will be silent.

question: What does Job say his friends plan to do with his words?
answer: They plan to correct his words and ignore what he has said.

question: Why does Job say his friends should relent in their attacks on him?
answer: Job’s cause is just.

question: To what does Job compare his months of misery and trouble-filled nights?
answer: He compares them to a slave desiring relief from heat, or a hired man looking for his wages.

question: What covers Job’s flesh?
answer: Worms and clods of dust, open sores and infection cover his flesh.

question: What image does Job use to describe the speed of his days?
answer: His days pass more swiftly than a weaver’s shuttle.

question: To what does Job compare the man who goes down to Sheol?
answer: He is like a cloud that is consumed and vanishes away.

question: In what way will Job speak and complain?
answer: He will speak in the anguish of his spirit and complain in the bitterness of his soul.

question: What does God do to Job when Job goes to bed?
answer: God scares him with dreams and terrifies him through visions.

question: Why did Job want God to leave him alone?
answer: Job said his days are useless.

question: What does Job ask God to let him alone long enough to do?
answer: He asks to be left alone long enough to swallow his own saliva.

question: What does Job think God will not do?
answer: Job thinks God will not pardon his transgression and take away his iniquity.

question: To what did Bildad compare the words of Job’s mouth?
answer: He compared them to a mighty wind.

question: How did Bildad say he knew that Job’s children sinned?
answer: He said he knew this because God had punished them for their sins.

question: How does Bildad say that God would bless Job if Job were pure and upright?
answer: God would reward Job by restoring his former home and wealth.

question: To what does Bildad compare our days on earth?
answer: He says they are a shadow.

question: What do papyrus and reeds require in order to grow?
answer: Papyrus requires a marsh, and reeds need water to grow.

question: To what does Bildad compare the trust of godless men?
answer: Their trust is as fragile as a spider’s web.

question: What do the roots do that represent a person that forgets God?
answer: The roots are wrapped around heaps of stone and look for good places among the rocks.

question: How does God treat the innocent man and the evildoers differently?
answer: He will not cast away an innocent man, but will not take the hand of evildoers.

question: With what will God fill the mouth and lips of the innocent man?
answer: He will fill his mouth with laughter and his lips with shouting.

question: What would happen is a man tried to argue with God?
answer: The man could not answer God once in a thousand times.

question: What does God do to the mountains when he is angry?
answer: He removes the mountains without warning and overturns them.

question: What does God trample down?
answer: He tramples down and subdues the waves of the sea.

question: Does Job see God when he passes by?
answer: God goes by him and Job does not see or perceive him.

question: Even if Job were righteous, how would he need to address God?
answer: Job could not answer him, but could only plead for mercy.

question: Why does Job believe God has multiple his wounds?
answer: Job believed God multiplied his wounds without cause.

question: Is it possible for Job to be righteous and perfect?
answer: No, even then, his mouth would condemn him and prove him guilty.

question: Does Job think God treats righteous and wicked people differently?
answer: He says God destroys both perfect people and wicked people together.

question: To what three things does Job compare the speed of his days?
answer: They are swifter than a running messenger, they are as fast as reed boats, and as fast as the swooping eagle.

question: Why did Job say it would be in vain to forget about his complaints?
answer: God would not consider him innocent, but Job would be condemned.

question: What does Job say that no judge would be able to do?
answer: No judge would lay his hand on both Job and God.

question: What does Job say no other judge could do?
answer: There is no other judge who can take God’s rod from Job, or keep God’s terror from frightening Job.

question: Why does Job want God to show him instead of merely condemning him?
answer: He wants God to show Job why he accuses him.

question: What kind of eyes does Job ask God if he has?
answer: Job asks him if he has eyes of flesh and sees like a man sees.

question: For what does Job say that God seeks and searches?
answer: God inquires after Job’s iniquity and searches after his sin.

question: What had God’s hands done for Job?
answer: They had framed and fashioned Job, yet they are destroying him.

question: With what did God clothe Job?
answer: He clothed him with skin and flesh.

question: What has God granted to Job?
answer: God granted him life and covenant faithfulness.

question: What would God do if Job sinned?
answer: God will notice his sin, and not acquit him of his iniquity.

question: What would God do to Job if Job’s head were lifted up?
answer: God would hunt him down like a lion.

question: Who would God bring against Job?
answer: God would bring new witnesses against him.

question: What does Job wish had happened to him?
answer: He wishes he had died and that no eye had ever seen him.

question: Where is Job going, from which he will not return?
answer: He is going to the land of darkness.

question: What did Zophar think Job had done to their teaching?
answer: He thought Job had mocked his friends’ teaching.

question: What does Zophar say that God has demanded from Job?
answer: He said God has demanded less from Job than his iniquity deserved.

question: Does Zophar think that Job could possibly understand God?
answer: Zophar thinks that it is impossible because God is as high as the heavens, deeper than Sheol, longer than the earth, and wider than the sea.

question: Does Zophar think that it is possible for anyone to stop God?
answer: It is impossible to stop God because he knows false people and punishes iniquity.

question: When does Zophar say foolish people will have understanding?
answer: They will have understanding when the colt of a wild donkey will be born to a man, meaning never!

question: What does Zophar say would happen to Job’s misery if he truly puts away his iniquity?
answer: Job would forget his misery and remember it only like waters that have flowed away.

question: Why would Job be secure if he put away his iniquity?
answer: He would be secure because there would be hope.

question: What does Zophar say will be the hope of wicked people?
answer: He says that their hope will be an expiration of breath, meaning that they can only hope to die.

question: How does Job compare himself to his friends?
answer: He says he also has understanding and is not inferior to them.

question: What do Job’s neighbors think of him now?
answer: They laugh at him.

question: Who does Job think could teach his friends?
answer: The beasts, the birds, the earth, and the fish of the sea could teach his friends.

question: What do all of the animals know?
answer: They know that the hand of Yahweh has given them life.

question: What does Job say about aged men and understanding?
answer: Wisdom and understanding come as people grow old.

question: What does God do with the waters?
answer: He with holds them and they dry up, and he sends them out and they overwhelm the land.

question: What does God take from kings?
answer: He takes off the chain of authority from them.

question: What does Job say about what God does to the trustworthy and the elders?
answer: He can remove the speech of the trustworthy and take away the understanding of elders.

question: What does Job say about God does to nations?
answer: He makes them strong or destroys them, and enlarges them or leads them along as prisoners.

question: What happens to the leaders of the people of the earth when God takes away their understanding?
answer: He causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no path.

question: How does Job say his knowledge compares to that of his friends?
answer: Job says that he knows the same as they know, and he is not inferior to them.

question: Who would Job like to talk to instead of his friends and why?
answer: He would rather speak to the Almighty because Job wants to reason with God.

question: What does Job say about wanting his friends to be silent?
answer: He says that the silence of his friends would be wisdom.

question: What does Job want his friends to hear?
answer: He wants them to listen to his reasoning and the pleading of his lips.

question: Would God approve if Job’s friends were showing favoritism?
answer: No, he would strongly reprove them if they showed favoritism.

question: What does Job think about his friends’ sayings and defenses?
answer: He says their sayings are proverbs made of ashes, and their defenses are made of clay.

question: What does Job ask his friends to do so that he may speak?
answer: Job asks them to hold their peace and let him speak.

question: Why does Job think that he would be acquitted?
answer: He does not come before God like a godless man.

question: What has Job set in order?
answer: He has set his defense in order.

question: What does Job want God to withdraw from him?
answer: Job wants God to withdraw his oppressive hand from Job and stop terrifying him.

question: Who does God treat Job like?
answer: He treats Job like his enemy.

question: What useless things does Job say he is like?
answer: He is like a rotten thing that wastes away, like a garment that moths have eaten.

question: How does Job say man is like a flower?
answer: Man sprouts from the ground like a flower, and then withers.

question: Who decides the lifespan of man?
answer: God has determined his days and the number of his months.

question: What does Job say about a tree that has been cut down?
answer: There can be hope for a tree that has been cut down, for it can sprout again.

question: Does Job say a man can live again?
answer: He says that people do not rise up again, and will not be roused out of their sleep.

question: Where does Job wish would God would hide him?
answer: Job wants God to hide him away in Sheol, away from troubles.

question: How would God treat Job’s transgression and iniquity if God’s wrath were finished?
answer: God would seal up Job’s transgression in a bag, and cover up Job’s iniquity.

question: What amazing thing can water do over time?
answer: Water can wear down stones.

question: What kinds of things does a dead man not know about his sons (his children)?
answer: If they achieve honor or become insignificant, he does not know it.

question: With what should a wise man not fill himself?
answer: He should not fill himself with the east wind.

question: How does Eliphaz think that Job’s statements dishonored God?
answer: He thinks Job destroys fear and diminishes devotion to God.

question: Does Eliphaz think that Job knows something that the other friends do not know?
answer: He does not think that Job knows what they do not know, or that he understands they do not understand.

question: Which people does Eliphaz say agree with Job’s friends?
answer: The gray-headed and very aged men who are older than Job’s father are with Eliphaz and his friends.

question: What does Eliphaz think Job has done?
answer: He thinks Job has turned his spirit against God.

question: How does God view his holy ones and the heavens?
answer: He puts no trust even in his holy ones, and the heavens are not clean in his sight.

question: From whom did Eliphaz get the things he will announce to Job?
answer: The things he has seen are things that wise men passed down from their fathers, and things that ancestors did not hide.

question: When will the destroyer come upon the wicked man?
answer: The destroyer will come upon him while he is in his prosperity.

question: What waits for the wicked man?
answer: The sword waits for the wicked man.

question: With what does the wicked man run against God?
answer: He runs at God with a stiff neck and a thick shield.

question: What will happen to the cities and houses of the wicked man?
answer: They are ready to become heaps.

question: What will cause the wicked to go away?
answer: He will go away at the breath of God’s mouth.

question: What reward will the wicked man have for trusting in worthless things?
answer: Emptiness will be his reward.

question: What will happen to the company of godless people?
answer: It will be barren, and fire will consume their tents of bribery.

question: What did Job say about the comfort offered by his friends?
answer: Job said they were making him more miserable with their endless, useless words.

question: How does Job’s speaking affect his grief?
answer: If he speaks, his grief is not lessened, and if he keeps from speaking, he is not helped.

question: How are other people treating Job as God attacks him?
answer: They gape at Job with open mouth, hit him reproachfully on the cheek, and gathered together against him.

question: To whom has God given Job?
answer: God handed him over to the ungodly and threw him into the hands of wicked people.

question: How has God injured Job?
answer: He has pierced Job’s kidneys and poured out his bile on the ground.

question: What has Job done to his skin to show his grief?
answer: He has sewn sackcloth on his skin.

question: Who is Job’s witness and able to vouch for Job?
answer: Job’s witness is in heaven, and the one who is for him is on high.

question: Who does Job turn to as his friends scoff at him?
answer: Job pours out his tears to God.

question: What must Job always see?
answer: He must always see the provocation of the mockers who are with him.

question: What pledge does Job want God to make to Job?
answer: He wants God to pledge himself to be a guarantee for Job.

question: Whose evil deed will cause the eyes of his children to fail?
answer: The one who denounces his friends for a reward will cause the eyes of his children to fail.

question: What has happened to Job’s eye and his body because of sorrow?
answer: His eye is dim and all his body parts are as thin a shadow.

question: Does Job think that he can find a wise man among his friends?
answer: Job knows that he will not find a wise man among them.

question: Does Job have plans for the future?
answer: Job’s plans are over, as are the wishes of his heart.

question: What has become Job’s father, mother, and sister?
answer: The pit has become his father, and the worm is his mother and sister.

question: How did Bildad think Job viewed his friends?
answer: Bildad thought Job regarded them as beasts and thought they were stupid.

question: What will happen to the light of the wicked person?
answer: His light goes out; the flame of his fire will not shine.

question: What will throw the wicked man into a net?
answer: He will be thrown into a net by his own feet, and he will walk into a pitfall.

question: What will catch the wicked man?
answer: He will be caught by a trap, a snare, and a noose.

question: What will happen to the strength of the wicked man?
answer: His strength will turn into hunger.

question: Where will the wicked man no longer live?
answer: He will no longer live in his tent but will be unable to save himself.

question: What image does Bildad use to describe what will happen to the wicked man?
answer: He describes the wicked man as a tree whose roots will dry up beneath the ground, and whose branch will wither above.

question: Will the wicked man have any descendants?
answer: He will have no son or son’s son among his people, nor any remaining kinfolk where he had stayed.

question: How do the people respond to what happens to the wicked man?
answer: People will be shocked and horrified at what happens to the wicked man.

question: What does Job ask his friends to stop doing to him?
answer: Job asks his friends to stop hurting him and discouraging him.

question: How many times have Job’s friends reproached him?
answer: They have reproached him ten times.

question: Whose concern should it be if Job had erred?
answer: Job says the error should be his own concern.

question: How does Job say God has treated him?
answer: Job says God has done wrong to Job and caught him in God’s net.

question: What happens when Job calls out for help because he has been wronged?
answer: He is not answered and there is no justice.

question: According to Job, how has God regarded Job?
answer: Job says God has regarded him as one of his enemies.

question: What has happened to all of Job’s family and friends?
answer: God has put his brothers far from him, his acquaintances are alienated, his kinsfolk fail him, and his close friends have forgotten him.

question: How does Job’s servant respond to Job when he calls him?
answer: His servant does not respond when Job gives an order.

question: How have Job’s former friends treated him?
answer: His former friends have turned against him.

question: How does Job survive?
answer: He survives only with the skin of his teeth.

question: What does Job want to happen to his words?
answer: He wants them to be written down and inscribed in a book, or engraved with pen and lead in the rock forever.

question: What does Job say he knows?
answer: He knows that his Redeemer lives, and that at last his Redeemer will stand on the earth.

question: What does Job say will happen when his body is destroyed?
answer: Job in his flesh will see God.

question: What does wrath bring?
answer: Wrath brings the punishment of the sword.

question: Why did Zophar answer Job quickly?
answer: He answered Job quickly he was troubled by what Job said. He hears Job’s rebuke and says it puts him to shame.

question: How long does the joy of a godless man last?
answer: The joy of the godless only lasts for a moment.

question: How will the wicked man perish?
answer: He will perish permanently, like garbage disappears.

question: How will the wicked man go away?
answer: He will fly away like a dream, and be chased away like a vision of the night.

question: What will the wicked man’s children do?
answer: His children will apologize to poor people.

question: What happens to wickedness inside the wicked man?
answer: It will cause the food in his intestines to turn bitter, and will becomes like the poison of asps inside him.

question: What will happen to the riches that the wicked man swallows down?
answer: He will vomit them up again.

question: What will the wicked man not live to enjoy?
answer: He will not live to enjoy the blessings that flow from God.

question: Why will the wicked man not rejoice?
answer: He has oppressed and neglected the poor people, and has violently taken away houses that he did not build.

question: Why will the prosperity of the wicked man not be permanent?
answer: It will not be permanent because there is nothing left that he did not devour.

question: What will God do to the wicked man who is about to fill his belly?
answer: God will rain down the fierceness of his wrath on him while he is eating.

question: What will happen when the wicked man flees from the iron weapon?
answer: A bow of bronze will shoot him.

question: What will the heavens and the earth do against the wicked man?
answer: The heavens will reveal his iniquity and the earth will be a witness against him.

question: What will happen to the wicked man on the day of God’s wrath?
answer: The wealth of his house will vanish and his goods will flow away.

question: What does Job think his friends will do after he has spoken?
answer: He thinks they will continue to mock him.

question: How will people respond when they look at Job?
answer: They will be astonished and lay their hands upon their mouths.

question: What happens to Job when he thinks about his sufferings?
answer: He is terrified; his flesh trembles.

question: What does Job ask about wicked people?
answer: Job asks, “Why do they continue to live, become old, and grow mighty in power?”

question: What happens to the bull and the cow of the wicked?
answer: The bull does not fail to breed and the cow does not lose her calf prematurely.

question: What do the wicked say to God?
answer: They tell God to depart from them, for they do not wish any knowledge of his ways.

question: How does Job respond to the advice of wicked people?
answer: He wants nothing to do with their advice.

question: Who does Job want to pay for the guilt of the wicked person?
answer: Job wants the wicked person to pay for his guilt, and not his children, so that he would know his guilt.

question: Can anyone teach God knowledge?
answer: No, for he judges even those who are high.

question: What happens to both the man who dies in full strength and the one who dies in bitterness of soul?
answer: They both lie down alike in the dust and the worms cover them both.

question: What does Job know about his friends’ thoughts and ways?
answer: He knows their thoughts and the ways in which they wrong him.

question: What have traveling people seen happen to the wicked man?
answer: They have seen that the wicked man is kept from the day of calamity, and that he is led away from the day of wrath.

question: What will men do for the tomb of the wicked man?
answer: Men will keep watch over his tomb.

question: With what does Job say Zophar was trying to comfort him?
answer: Job says Zophar was trying to comfort him with things that are not true.

question: What does Eliphaz ask Job if his righteousness can do for the Almighty?
answer: He asks if it brings any pleasure to the Almighty if Job is righteous.

question: How does Eliphaz mock Job’s reverence for God?
answer: He mockingly says that God would not punish Job if Job had truly been righteous.

question: What does Eliphaz accuse Job of doing to the naked?
answer: He says that Job has stripped the naked of their clothing.

question: What does Eliphaz accuse Job of doing to widows?
answer: He claims Job has sent widows away empty.

question: What does Eliphaz say the darkness has done to Job?
answer: He says Job is in darkness so that he does not know what to do.

question: What does Eliphaz claim Job says about God not seeing people?
answer: Job says, “Thick clouds are a covering to God, so that he does not see people.”

question: What happens to the foundations of wicked men?
answer: The wicked men’s foundations have washed away, as if by a flooding river.

question: How do the righteous act when they see the fate of the wicked?
answer: The righteous see their fate and are glad.

question: What will happen if Job is at peace with God?
answer: If Job is at peace with God, good will come to him.

question: What does Eliphaz say will happen if Job returns to the Almighty?
answer: If Job returns to the Almighty, he will be built up.

question: What will happen when Job takes pleasure in the Almighty?
answer: When Job takes pleasure in the Almighty, he will lift up his face to God.

question: What does God do for the humble?
answer: God saves those who are humble.

question: Is Job finished protesting?
answer: No. Job said that there is much more he could protest about.

question: What would Job do before God if he could find him?
answer: He would lay his case in order before God and fill his mouth with arguments.

question: Does Job think God would argue against him in the greatness of God’s power if he could stand before him?
answer: No, he thinks God would listen to him fairly.

question: What does Job say God is doing in the south?
answer: Job says in the south, God hides himself so that no one can see what he does there.

question: What result does Job expect from God’s testing him?
answer: When God has tested Job, he will come out like gold.

question: What has Job done with the words of God’s mouth?
answer: Job has treasured up in his heart the words of God’s mouth.

question: What will God carry out for Job?
answer: God will carry out his decrees for Job.

question: How does Job feel when he thinks about God?
answer: When Job thinks about him, he is afraid of him.

question: What covers Job’s face?
answer: The thick darkness covers Job’s face.

question: What times does Job think are not set by the Almighty?
answer: Job asks why times for judging the wicked are not set by the Almighty.

question: What do the wicked do to the donkey of the fatherless?
answer: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless.

question: What do the poor hope the Arabah will provide?
answer: They hope the Arabah will provide them food for their children.

question: What do the poor lack in the cold?
answer: They have no covering in the cold.

question: What do the poor embrace for lack of shelter?
answer: They embrace a rock for lack of shelter.

question: What do the poor do for others even though they go hungry?
answer: Even though they go hungry, they carry others’ sheaves of grain.

question: What do the poor do for others even though they suffer thirst?
answer: They tread the wicked men’s winepresses, but they suffer thirst.

question: What is the murderer like in the night?
answer: In the night, the murderer is like a thief.

question: Why do the wicked shut themselves up in daytime?
answer: The wicked do not care for the light.

question: With what terrors are the wicked comfortable?
answer: They are comfortable with the terrors of the thick darkness.

question: Who does Sheol consume?
answer: Sheol consumes those who have sinned.

question: Who does the wicked one devour?
answer: The wicked one devours the barren women who have not born children.

question: Who does God drag away?
answer: God drags away the mighty by his power.

question: What will happen to the mighty in a little while?
answer: In only a little while, the mighty will be gone.

question: Where does God make order?
answer: God makes order in his high places of heaven.

question: Of whom does Bildad ask can they be clean and acceptable to God?
answer: He asks if one who is born of a woman can be clean and acceptable to God.

question: To what does Bildad compare a son of man?
answer: He says that a son of man is a grub.

question: Whose words does Job say Bildad is speaking?
answer: Job says Bildad is not speaking God’s words, but his own.

question: What has no covering before God?
answer: Sheol itself has no covering against God.

question: Where does God bind up the waters?
answer: He binds up the waters in his thick clouds.

question: What does God spread on the face of the moon?
answer: He encloses the face of the moon and spreads his cloud on it.

question: What did God calm with his power?
answer: He calmed the sea with his power.

question: By what did God clear the heavens of storms?
answer: By his breath, he cleared the heavens of storms.

question: How much of God’s ways are people able to see?
answer: People can see only the edges of God’s ways.

question: What does Job say God has taken away from him?
answer: God has taken away his justice.

question: What does Job vow his lips will not speak?
answer: Job vows that surely his lips will not speak wickedness or deceit.

question: How long will Job’s thoughts not reproach him?
answer: His thoughts will not reproach him so long as he lives.

question: What does Job say God does when he cuts off a godless man’s life?
answer: When God cuts off his life, God will punish him for the wrong things that he has done.

question: What does Job say he will not conceal of the Almighty?
answer: Job said that he would not conceal the hand of the Almighty.

question: Of what will the wicked man’s offspring not have enough?
answer: His offspring will never have enough food.

question: What will the wicked man’s widow not do for him?
answer: His widow will make no lament for him.

question: What will happen to the silver of the wicked man?
answer: The innocent will divide up his silver among themselves.

question: What does the wicked man see when he opens his eyes after he lies down rich?
answer: He opens his eyes, and everything is gone.

question: What does the east wind do as it carries the wicked man away?

question: How does the army enter the city?
answer: They rush on the city, they run on the wall, they climb in houses, and they go through windows like thieves.

question: Whose army is this?
answer: This is Yahweh’s army.

question: What should the people tear?
answer: They should tear their hearts and not their garments.

question: Why should the people return to Yahweh?
answer: He is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in love, and he would like to turn from inflicting punishment.

question: Why should the people blow a trumpet in Zion?
answer: They should blow a trumpet to consecrate a fast and to call a sacred assembly.

question: What had Yahweh’s people been among the nations?
answer: Yahweh’s people had been a reproach, an object of scorn, among the nations.

question: Why should the land not fear?
answer: The land should not fear, because Yahweh has done great things.

question: Who sent the mighty army?
answer: Yahweh sent the mighty army.

question: Will Yahweh ever bring shame on his people again?
answer: No, he will never bring shame on his people again.

question: What will happen when Yahweh pours out his Spirit?
answer: Their sons and your daughters will prophesy, their old men will dream dreams, and their young men will see visions.

question: What will Yahweh show in the heavens and on the earth?
answer: Yahweh show wonders in the heavens and on the earth.

question: Into what will the sun turn?
answer: The sun will turn into darkness.

question: Who will be saved at that time?
answer: Everyone who calls on the name of Yahweh will be saved.

question: Who will Yahweh bring to the Valley of Jehoshaphat?
answer: Yahweh will bring the nations to the Valley of Jehoshaphat.

question: Who did the nations scatter?
answer: The nations scattered Yahweh’s people.

question: At whom are Tyre, Sidon and all the regions of Philistia angry?
answer: Tyre, Sidon and all the regions of Philistia are angry at Yahweh.

question: What did Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia do with Yahweh’s treasures?
answer: They brought his treasures into their temples.

question: What did Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia do to the people of Judah and Jerusalem?
answer: They sold the people to the Greeks in order to remove them far from their territory.

question: What will Yahweh do to the sons and daughters of Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia?
answer: Yahweh will sell their sons and daughters to the Sabeans by the hand of the people of Judah.

question: Into what should the nations beat their plowshares?
answer: They should beat their plowshares into swords.

question: What will Yahweh do to all surrounding nations?
answer: Yahweh will sit to judge all surrounding nations.

question: What will happen to the sun, moon, and stars?
answer: The sun and moon will become dark, and the stars will withdraw their brightness.

question: What two things will Yahweh be for his people?
answer: Yahweh be a shelter and a stronghold for his people.

question: Who lives in Zion?
answer: Yahweh their God lives in Zion.

question: With what will the hills flow?
answer: The hills will flow with milk.

question: Who will be abandoned because of the violence they did to the people of Judah?
answer: Egypt and Edom will be abandoned.

question: What did Yahweh tell Jonah to do?
answer: Yahweh told Jonah to get up and go to Nineveh and speak out against it.

question: What did Jonah do after Yahweh told him to go to Nineveh?
answer: Jonah got up to run away to Tarshish from before the face of Yahweh.

question: What did Yahweh do to the ship which Jonah had boarded?
answer: Yahweh sent a great wind and a great storm on the sea so that the ship was near to being broken up.

question: To whom did the sailors cry out in the midst of the storm?
answer: The sailors became very afraid and each cried out to his own god.

question: How did the sailors determine who was the cause of the evil?
answer: The sailors cast lots to determine the cause of the evil and the lot indicated Jonah.

question: What was the result of casting lots?
answer: The result was that the lot indicated that Jonah was the cause of the evil they were experiencing.

question: How did the sailors know that Jonah was running away from before the face of Yahweh?
answer: The sailors knew that Jonah was running away from before the face of Yahweh because Jonah told them.

question: What did Jonah tell the men to do in order to stop the storm?
answer: Jonah told the men to lift him up and throw him into the sea.

question: What two requests did the sailors make of Yahweh?
answer: The sailors asked Yahweh to not let them perish on account of the life of Jonah and to not hold them guilty for Jonah’s death.

question: What happened when the sailors threw Jonah into the sea?
answer: When the sailors threw Jonah into the sea, the sea stopped raging.

question: What happened to Jonah when the sailors threw him into the sea?
answer: Yahweh appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the abdomen of the fish three days and three nights.

question: What did Jonah do in the belly of the fish?
answer: Jonah cried out to Yahweh in prayer because he was distressed.

question: What did Jonah hope he might be able to do again?
answer: Jonah hoped that he might be able to look toward Yahweh’s holy temple again.

question: From where did Yahweh bring up Jonah’s life?
answer: Yahweh brought Jonah’s life up from the pit.

question: What did Jonah say happens to those who give attention to empty vanities?
answer: Jonah said those who give attention to empty vanities forsake their covenant faithfulness.

question: When Jonah prayed in the belly of the fish, what did he say that he would do?
answer: Jonah said he would sacrifice to Yahweh with a voice of thanksgiving and fulfill what he had vowed.

question: To whom did Jonah say salvation belongs?
answer: Jonah said that salvation belongs to Yahweh.

question: How did Yahweh respond to Jonah’s prayer?
answer: Yahweh spoke to the fish and it vomited Jonah up onto the dry land.

question: What did Yahweh command Jonah to do for the second time?
answer: Yahweh commanded Jonah to go to Nineveh and speak Yahweh’s message.

question: How did Jonah respond the second time Yahweh told him to go to Nineveh?
answer: Jonah obeyed Yahweh and went to Nineveh.

question: What message did Jonah speak in Nineveh?
answer: Jonah said that in 40 days Nineveh would be overthrown.

question: How did the Ninevites respond to Yahweh’s message that Jonah preached?
answer: The Ninevites believed God, fasted, and put on sackcloth. The king of Nineveh made a decree which said that no person or animal should eat or drink water and that each person and animal must be covered with sackcloth and that each person should cry out to God and stop doing evil deeds including violent acts.

question: What hope did the king of Nineveh have for the people of Nineveh and the city?
answer: The king of Nineveh hoped that God would turn back from his anger and have compassion on them so that the people of Nineveh would not perish.

question: How did God respond to the Ninevites’ repentance?
answer: God saw their deeds, that they turned away from their evil ways. And God relented in regard to the evil that he had said he would do to them; and he did not do it.

question: Why was Jonah angry?
answer: Jonah was angry because it seemed like a great evil to Jonah that Yahweh had mercy on the Ninevites and did not punish them.

question: Why did Jonah say that he had tried to flee to Tarshish?
answer: Jonah said that he had tried to flee to Tarshish because he knew that Yahweh was a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abundant in covenant faithfulness, and one who relents from evil.

question: What did Jonah ask Yahweh to do to him?
answer: Jonah asked Yahweh to take his life.

question: What question did Yahweh ask Jonah?
answer: Yahweh asked Jonah if it was right for Jonah to be angry.

question: Why did Jonah go out of the city and sit down facing the city?
answer: Jonah wanted to see what would happen to the city of Nineveh.

question: What did Yahweh do for Jonah while he sat outside the city?
answer: Yahweh caused a plant to grow up over Jonah to be a shade for his head.

question: What did Yahweh do to the plant that had provided shade for Jonah?
answer: God appointed a worm at the rising of the dawn of the next day; and it attacked the plant, and it withered.

question: What question did Yahweh ask Jonah after Yahweh caused the plant to wither and a hot east wind to blow on Jonah?
answer: Yahweh asked Jonah if it was right for him to be angry about the plant.

question: How did Jonah feel when the plant that had given him shade withered and died?
answer: Jonah felt compassion for the plant that had withered and died.

question: For whom did Yahweh feel compassion?
answer: Yahweh felt compassion for the people and animals in Nineveh.

question: What did Yahweh tell Joshua to do after the death of Moses?
answer: Yahweh told Joshua to arise, cross the Jordan River with all the people, and go into the land he was giving to the sons of Israel.

question: Why did Yahweh say that no one would be able to stand against Joshua?
answer: Yahweh said that no one would be able to stand against Joshua because Yahweh would be with Joshua just as he had been with Moses.

question: What did Yahweh ask Joshua to do regarding the law of Moses?
answer: Yahweh asked Joshua to be strong and very courageous, and to be careful to do according to all the law that Moses commanded, not turning from it to the right or to the left.

question: What did Yahweh tell Joshua he should meditate on day and night?
answer: Yahweh told Joshua that the book of the law should not depart from his mouth, but he should meditate on it day and night.

question: What did Joshua tell the officers of the people to command the people?
answer: Joshua told the officers to command the people to prepare provisions for themselves because within three days they would cross the Jordan to possess the land Yahweh was giving them.

question: What did Joshua remind the people that Moses had said Yahweh would give them?
answer: Joshua reminded the people that Moses had said, “Yahweh your God is giving rest to you, and he will give to you this land.”

question: What did Joshua tell the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh to do?
answer: Joshua told them that their wives, children, and livestock could remain in the land Moses had given them east of the Jordan, but all their warriors, being armed, should cross over to help their brothers.

question: How did the people answer Joshua’s commands?
answer: The people answered Joshua by saying they would do all that he had commanded them and go wherever he sent them.

question: Where did the two spies stay when Joshua sent them to see the land and Jericho?
answer: The two spies stayed at the house of a prostitute named Rahab in Jericho.

question: What did Rahab do with the two spies when the king of Jericho sent men to find them?
answer: When the king’s men came to Rahab looking for the spies, she had hidden the spies, and she denied knowing where they were.

question: What did Rahab tell the men from the king of Jericho about the spies?
answer: Rahab told the king’s men that the spies had come to her, but she did not know where they were from, and they left at dark when the gate was about to shut. She told the men to pursue them quickly to overtake them.

question: What reason did Rahab give the spies for why she had hidden them?
answer: Rahab told the spies that she knew Yahweh had given them the land and that the dread of them had fallen on her people.

question: What reports had made Rahab believe Yahweh had given the Israelites the land?
answer: Rahab said she believed Yahweh had given the Israelites the land because she had heard how Yahweh dried up the water of the Sea of Reeds for them and what they did to the two Amorite kings, Sihon and Og.

question: What did Rahab ask the spies to do for her and her family?
answer: Rahab asked the spies to swear by Yahweh that they would keep her father, mother, brothers, sisters, and all their households alive and deliver them from death.

question: What did the spies promise Rahab?
answer: The spies promised Rahab that their lives would be given in place of hers if she did not tell about their mission, and they would deal kindly and faithfully with her when Yahweh gave them the land.

question: What did the spies tell Rahab she must do for her and her family to be safe when they came into the land?
answer: The spies told Rahab to tie a scarlet cord in the window and gather her father, mother, brothers, and all her father’s household into her house.

question: What did the spies report to Joshua when they returned?
answer: The spies told Joshua that Yahweh had given all the land into their hand and that all the inhabitants of the land were melting because of them.

question: What did the officers tell the people to do when they saw the Levite priests carrying the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh?
answer: The officers told the people that when they saw the Box of the Covenant and the priests carrying it, they should set out from their place and follow it.

question: Why did the officers tell the people to stay about 2,000 cubits behind the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh?
answer: The officers told the people to stay that far behind the Box of the Covenant so they would know the way to go, since they had not passed that way before.

question: What did Joshua say Yahweh was going to do among the people the next day?
answer: Joshua said that Yahweh was going to do wonders for the people the next day.

question: What did Yahweh tell Joshua to command the priests carrying the Box of the Covenant when they reached the edge of the Jordan River?
answer: Yahweh told Joshua to command the priests to stand still in the Jordan River once they reached the edge of its waters.

question: What did Joshua tell the people would happen when the soles of the feet of the priests carrying the Box of Yahweh rested in the waters of the Jordan?
answer: Joshua told the people that as soon as the soles of the priests’ feet rested in the Jordan’s waters, the waters flowing from above would be cut off and stand in one heap.

question: Where did the people cross the Jordan River?
answer: The people crossed the Jordan opposite Jericho, while the waters from above stood in a heap far away at Adam.

question: What did the priests who carried the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh do while all Israel crossed the Jordan?
answer: The priests who carried the Box of the Covenant stood firmly on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan River until all the nation had finished crossing.

question: What did Yahweh tell Joshua to command 12 men (one from each tribe) to do?
answer: Yahweh told Joshua to command the 12 men to take 12 stones from the middle of the Jordan, from where the priests’ feet stood, and carry them to their lodging place.

question: What did Joshua say was the purpose of the 12 stones taken from the Jordan River?
answer: The stones would be a memorial to the people of Israel forever, because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh when it crossed.

question: About how many armed warriors crossed over before Yahweh to the plains of Jericho for battle?
answer: About 40,000 armed warriors crossed over before Yahweh to the plains of Jericho for battle.

question: What happened when the priests who carried the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh came up out of the Jordan and their feet touched dry ground?
answer: When the priests’ feet touched dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before.

question: Where did Joshua set up the 12 stones that the men had taken out of the Jordan?
answer: At Gilgal Joshua set up the 12 stones that came out of the Jordan.

question: Why did Joshua say the people should tell their children what Yahweh had done for them at the Jordan?
answer: Joshua said they should tell their children so that all the peoples of the earth might know Yahweh’s hand is mighty, and so that they might fear Yahweh their God all the days.

question: What was the reaction of the Amorite and Canaanite kings when they heard Yahweh had dried up the Jordan’s waters for Israel?
answer: When the kings heard how Yahweh had dried up the Jordan’s waters, their hearts melted, and there was no longer any spirit in them because of the sons of Israel.

question: What did Yahweh command Joshua to make and do a second time for the sons of Israel?
answer: Yahweh commanded Joshua to make flint knives and circumcise the sons of Israel a second time.

question: Why did Joshua have to circumcise the sons of those who came out of Egypt?
answer: Joshua had to circumcise them because they were uncircumcised, as they had not been circumcised while they were traveling in the wilderness.

question: What festival did the sons of Israel celebrate while camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho?
answer: While camped at Gilgal, the sons of Israel celebrated the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month.

question: What food stopped the day after the people of Israel ate the produce of the land of Canaan?
answer: The manna stopped the day after they ate the produce of the land, and the sons of Israel no longer had manna.

question: Who did Joshua see standing in front of him with a drawn sword when he was by Jericho?
answer: Joshua saw a man standing in front of him with his drawn sword in his hand.

question: Who did the man with the drawn sword say he was?
answer: The man with the drawn sword told Joshua that he had come as the commander of the army of Yahweh.

question: What did Joshua ask the commander of Yahweh’s army?
answer: Joshua fell on his face to the earth, bowed down, and asked what his lord was speaking to his servant.

question: What did the commander of Yahweh’s army tell Joshua to do because the place on which he was standing was holy?
answer: The commander of Yahweh’s army told Joshua to remove his sandals from his feet because the place on which he was standing was holy.

question: What did Yahweh promise Joshua concerning Jericho, its king, and its warriors?
answer: Yahweh promised Joshua that he had given Jericho, its king, and its warriors into Joshua’s hand.

question: How were the men of war to circle the city of Jericho for six days?
answer: All the men of war were to circle the city, going around it one time each day for six days.

question: What did Yahweh tell Joshua should happen on the seventh day involving priests, shofars, and the people?
answer: Yahweh told him that seven priests should carry seven shofars before the Box, and on the seventh day the people should circle the city seven times while the priests blew the shofars; then, at a long blast, all the people should shout.

question: What did Yahweh say would happen to the city wall when the people shouted on the seventh day?
answer: Yahweh said the wall of the city would collapse unto itself, and the people should go up, every man straight into the city.

question: What did Joshua command the people not to do until he told them to shout?
answer: Joshua commanded the people not to shout, nor let their voice be heard, nor let a word go out of their mouth until the day he told them to shout.

question: Who did Joshua say would live when the city of Jericho was devoted to Yahweh, and why?
answer: Joshua said that only Rahab the prostitute and all who were with her in her house would live, because she hid the messengers they sent.

question: What did Joshua declare was holy to Yahweh and must enter Yahweh’s treasury?
answer: Joshua declared that all the silver, gold, and objects of bronze and iron were holy to Yahweh and must enter Yahweh’s treasury.

question: What did the people of Israel do to everything in the city after the walls of Jericho fell?
answer: The people of Israel devoted to destruction by the sword all that was in the city—men and women, young and old, oxen, sheep, and donkeys.

question: What did Joshua command the two men who had spied out the land to do regarding Rahab?
answer: Joshua commanded the two spies to go into the prostitute’s house and bring her out, and all who belonged to her, as they had sworn to her.

question: What curse did Joshua pronounce on the man who would rebuild Jericho?
answer: Joshua said that the man who rebuilt Jericho would be cursed before Yahweh: he would lay its foundation with his firstborn and set up its gates with his youngest son.
