question: Where did the young man say the disciples would meet Jesus?
answer: The young man said the disciples would meet Jesus in Galilee.

question: To whom did Jesus first appear after his resurrection?
answer: Jesus first appeared to Mary Magdalene.

question: How did Jesus’ disciples respond when Mary told them she had seen Jesus alive?
answer: The disciples did not believe.

question: How did Jesus’ disciples respond when two other people told them they had seen Jesus alive?
answer: The disciples did not believe.

question: When he appeared to the disciples, what did Jesus say to them about their unbelief?
answer: Jesus rebuked the disciples for their unbelief.

question: What command did Jesus give the disciples?
answer: Jesus commanded the disciples to go into all the world and preach the gospel.

question: Who did Jesus say would be saved?
answer: Jesus said those who believed and were baptized would be saved.

question: Who did Jesus say would be condemned?
answer: Jesus said those who did not believe would be condemned.

question: What signs did Jesus say would go with those who believed?
answer: Jesus said those who believed would cast out demons, would speak in new languages, would not be hurt by anything deadly, and would heal others.

question: What happened to Jesus after he spoke to the disciples?
answer: After he spoke to the disciples, Jesus was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.

question: What did the disciples then do?
answer: The disciples then left and preached everywhere.

question: What did the Lord then do?
answer: The Lord then worked with the disciples and confirmed the word with miraculous signs.

question: Of what is Yahweh full?
answer: Yahweh is full of wrath.

question: On whom does Yahweh take vengeance?
answer: Yahweh takes vengeance on his adversaries.

question: Where does Yahweh make his way?
answer: Yahweh makes his way in the whirlwind and the storm.

question: What is happening to the flowers of Lebanon?
answer: The flowers of Lebanon wither.

question: What happens to the earth in Yahweh’s presence?
answer: The earth heaves in Yahweh’s presence.

question: To what can we compare Yahweh in the day of trouble?
answer: Yahweh is a stronghold in the day of trouble.

question: Into what will Yahweh pursue his enemies?
answer: Yahweh will pursue his enemies with darkness, meaning “terrible things.”

question: What will Yahweh do to the people’s yoke?
answer: He will break the people’s yoke from upon them.

question: Why will Yahweh dig graves for the people of Nineveh?
answer: He will dig their graves because they are worthless.

question: Where are the feet of him who brings good news?
answer: On the mountains are the feet of the herald who brings good news.

question: Why should Judah celebrate the festivals and keep vows?
answer: Judah should celebrate its festivals and keep vows because the wicked one will invade them no more.

question: What has Yahweh restored?
answer: Yahweh has restored the majesty of Jacob.

question: What color are the shields of his mighty men?
answer: The shields of his mighty men are red.

question: What speeds through the streets?
answer: The chariots speed through the streets.

question: What has been decreed?
answer: It has been decreed: the queen is taken away into exile; her female servants moan like doves, beating their breasts.

question: What will the people of Nineveh do?
answer: They will flee away without turning back.

question: Of what were the lions afraid?
answer: They were afraid of nothing.

question: With what did the lion fill his cave and his dens?
answer: The lion filled his cave with victims and his dens with carcasses.

question: What will Yahweh do to Nineveh?
answer: Yahweh will burn their chariots in the smoke, devour their young lions, and cut off their prey from the land.

question: Of what is the city full?
answer: The city is full of blood, lies and stolen property.

question: How many people will be killed by the attacking horsemen?
answer: There will be heaps of corpses, a great pile of bodies, and no end of the bodies.

question: Why are these things happening?
answer: This is happening because of the harlotries of the beautiful prostitute.

question: What will Yahweh of hosts do against the prostitute because he is against her?
answer: Yahweh will raise up her skirt over her face and show her private parts to the nations and her shame to the kingdoms. He will throw disgusting filth on her and make her vile. He will make her someone that everyone will look at.

question: Whose wall was the sea?
answer: Thebes’ wall was the sea.

question: Who threw lots for Thebes’ honorable men?
answer: Thebes’ enemies threw lots for her honorable men.

question: If Nineveh’s fortresses are shaken, what happens?
answer: If Nineveh’s fortresses are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.

question: How many guards and generals are there?
answer: The guards and generals are as many as a swarm of locusts.

question: What will everyone who hears the news about you do?
answer: Everyone who hears the news about you will clap their hands in joy over you.

question: When did Nehemiah ask Hanani and some people from Judah about the Jews who had escaped, the remnant of the Jews who were there, and about Jerusalem?
answer: He asked them in the month Kislev, in the twentieth year.

question: Who wrote the book of Nehemiah?
answer: Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah wrote the book of Nehemiah.

question: What did Hanani and some people from Judah reply?
answer: They replied that those who remained in the province were in great evil and reproach because Jerusalem’s wall was broken down and its gates were burned with fire.

question: What did Nehemiah do when he heard about the condition of Jerusalem?
answer: He sat down and wept, and he mourned for days. He also fasted and prayed.

question: What did Nehemiah request while praying before the God of heaven?
answer: Nehemiah requested that Yahweh would listen to his prayer. Nehemiah requested that Yahweh would remember the word he commanded Moses, promising to gather the scattered Israelites if they returned to him and kept his commandments. Nehemiah requested that Yahweh would give him success and grant him mercy.

question: What did Nehemiah confess while praying before the God of heaven?
answer: Nehemiah confessed the sins of the people of Israel and his own sins and the sins of his family. Nehemiah said they had acted very corruptly against Yahweh and had not kept the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments that Yahweh had commanded Moses.

question: What did Nehemiah request while praying before the God of heaven?
answer: Nehemiah requested that Yahweh would listen to his prayer. Nehemiah requested that Yahweh would remember the word he commanded Moses, promising to gather the scattered Israelites if they returned to him and kept his commandments. Nehemiah requested that Yahweh would give him success and grant him mercy.

question: To whom did Nehemiah serve as cupbearer?
answer: Nehemiah served as cupbearer to the king.

question: At what date did Nehemiah, when he was sad, give wine to the king?
answer: Nehemiah gave wine to the king in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes.

question: Why was Nehemiah sad?
answer: He was sad because Jerusalem, the city of the graves of his fathers, was desolate and its gates had been consumed by fire.

question: What did Nehemiah want the king to give him permission to do?
answer: Nehemiah wanted permission from the king to go to Judah to rebuild the city.

question: When the king asked what Nehemiah wanted him to do, what did Nehemiah do?
answer: Nehemiah prayed to the God of heaven.

question: When the king sent Nehemiah with officers of the army and horsemen, why were Sanballat and Tobiah displeased?
answer: Sanballat and Tobiah were displeased that someone had come who wanted to seek good for the people of Israel.

question: When Nehemiah arose in the night, who did he tell what God had put into his heart to do for Jerusalem?
answer: At that time, Nehemiah did not tell anyone what his God had put into his heart to do for Jerusalem.

question: When Nehemiah told the rulers, the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the rest who did the work that the good hand of his God was on him and about the words the king had spoken to him, what did they say and do?
answer: They said that they would rise and build, and they strengthened their hands for the good work.

question: How did Nehemiah respond to Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem when they heard about the work, and mocked and ridiculed the workers?
answer: Nehemiah responded by saying that God would give them success, that they were God’s servants, and that Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem had no share, no right, and no memorial in Jerusalem.

question: Who built and consecrated the Sheep Gate?
answer: Eliashib built and consecrated the Sheep Gate along with his brothers, the priests.

question: Who built the Fish Gate?
answer: The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate.

question: Whose nobles refused to do the work ordered by their lords?
answer: The nobles of the Tekoites refused to do the work.

question: Who repaired the Old Gate?
answer: Joiada and Meshullam repaired the Old Gate.

question: Who repaired Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall?
answer: Uzziel and Hananiah repaired that portion of Jerusalem.

question: Who repaired another section along with the Tower of Ovens?
answer: Malkijah (the son of Harim) and Hasshub repaired another section and the Tower of Ovens.

question: Who helped Shallum repair the walls?
answer: His daughters helped him.

question: Who repaired the Valley Gate as far as the Dung Gate?
answer: Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate and the entire portion of wall between the Valley Gate and the Dung Gate.

question: Who repaired the Dung Gate?
answer: Malkijah (the son of Recab) repaired the Dung Gate.

question: Who repaired the Fountain Gate and the wall of the Pool of Siloam?
answer: Shallun repaired the Fountain Gate and the wall of the Pool of Siloam.

question: Who repaired from the place across from the tombs of David to the house of the mighty men?
answer: Nehemiah the son of Azbuk repaired that section.

question: Who repaired from the angle to the door of the house of Elisahib the high priest?
answer: Baruch repaired it.

question: Which section of the wall did Benjamin and Hasshub repair?
answer: They repaired the section in front of their own house.

question: Who did the repairs on the section above the Horse Gate?
answer: The priests repaired that section. Each of the priests repaired in front of his own house.

question: Who repaired the wall between the upper changes of the corner and the Sheep Gate?
answer: The goldsmiths and the merchants repaired that section.

question: Who mocked the Jews when they heard the Jews were building the wall?
answer: Sanballat and Tobiah mocked the Jews.

question: Why did Nehemiah ask God not to cover over the iniquity of Sanballat and Tobiah?
answer: Nehemiah asked God not to cover their iniquity because they had contempt for the Jews and provoked the builders to anger.

question: When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites came to fight against Jerusalem, what did the builders and people do?
answer: They prayed to their God and set a guard as protection.

question: What did Nehemiah do after the Jews warned him of the schemes being made against them?
answer: After learning of the schemes against them, Nehemiah positioned people in the lowest parts of the wall, in the bare areas. He positioned each family with their weapons. Nehemiah told the people to not be afraid of their enemies, but to remember the great and fearsome Lord and to fight for their families and homes.

question: What did the enemies hear?
answer: They heard that the workers knew their plans and that God had frustrated their plans.

question: What were the young men doing?
answer: Half of them were working on rebuilding the wall and half of them were holding their weapons and armor.

question: What reason did Nehemiah give for sounding the ram’s horn as a signal to fight?
answer: Nehemiah explained that the workers were separated on the wall, far from one another.

question: Why did some people not go to their homes to sleep? Why did some people not change their clothes?
answer: Some people did not go to their homes or change their clothes so that they could spend the night in the middle of Jerusalem, being a guard during the night and a worker in the day.

question: Why did the men and women raise a great outcry against their fellow Jews?
answer: They raised an outcry because some of them had to mortgage their property in order to get grain, some of them had to put their children in bondage as slaves, and some of them had to borrow silver in order to pay the kings taxes on their fields and vineyards.

question: What did Nehemiah do when he heard the outcry of the Jewish men and women against their fellow Jews?
answer: He contended with the nobles and with the prefects and said to them, “You are lending interest, a man against his brother!” And he put forth a great assembly against them.

question: Although the men and women were buying back from slavery their Jewish brothers who had been sold to the nations, what were the nobles and the prefects doing?
answer: They were selling their brothers and sisters, who were then being bought back by other Jewish men and women.

question: Why did Nehemiah command the nobles and the prefects to return the property they taken from the people?
answer: He commanded them to do that because what they were doing was not good.

question: How did the nobles and the prefects respond to Nehemiah’s command?
answer: They said they would return what they had taken, that they would not take anything more, and that they would do as Nehemiah commanded.

question: Why did neither Nehemiah nor his brothers take the food provided for the governor during the 12 years he was Judah’s governor?
answer: He did not do so because he feared God, and because the former governors had laid heavy burdens on the people.

question: Who ate at Nehemiah’s table?
answer: Those who ate at Nehemiah’s table were the Jews and the prefects, 150 men, and also those who came to Nehemiah from among the nations who were around them.

question: Why did Nehemiah ask God to call him to mind for good?
answer: Nehemiah asked God to do this because of all that he (Nehemiah) had done for the people.

question: When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem asked Nehemiah to meet with them in the plain of Ono, what was their intention?
answer: Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem intended to do evil to Nehemiah.

question: How did Nehemiah respond to the requests of their enemies?
answer: Nehemiah sent messengers to them saying, “I am doing a great work and I cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?”

question: What did Sanballat say in his fifth message?
answer: He said that all the nations had reported that Nehemiah and the Jews were planning to rebel, and the king would certainly hear these reports.

question: How did Nehemiah respond to Sanballat’s fifth message?
answer: Nehemiah responded by saying that Sanballat had invented the reports in his own heart.

question: What did Nehemiah pray when he realized that Sanballat and Jews’ enemies were trying to make the work stop and the Jews afraid?
answer: Nehemiah prayed that God would strengthen his hands.

question: How did Nehemiah respond to Sanballat’s fifth message?
answer: Nehemiah responded by saying Sanballat had invented the reports in his own heart.

question: Why did Nehemiah refuse to meet Shemaiah, the son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel, in the temple?
answer: Nehemiah refused because he thought a man like himself should neither run away to save his own life nor hide in the temple.

question: What would have happened if Nehemiah had gone into the temple?
answer: He would have sinned and given himself a bad name, and Sanballat and Tobiah might have reproached him.

question: What did Nehemiah pray the second time?
answer: He prayed God would remember Tobiah, and Sanballat according to their deeds, as well as the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets who were trying to frighten Nehemiah.

question: Why did Nehemiah’s enemies become afraid and fall in their own esteem when the wall was finished?
answer: They became afraid because they knew the work was done with the help of the Jews’ God.

question: When did Nehemiah give his brother Hanani charge over Jerusalem?
answer: Nehemiah gave Hanani charge of Jerusalem after he (Nehemiah) had finished the wall, set up the doors, and appointed the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites.

question: When were the gates of Jerusalem supposed to be opened?
answer: The gates were supposed to be opened when the sun became hot.

question: Although the city was wide and large, were there people and houses within it?
answer: There were few people within the city, and no built houses.

question: What did God put into Nehemiah’s heart to do?
answer: God put into Nehemiah’s heart to gather together the nobles, the prefects, and the people to be enrolled by genealogy.

question: What was done concerning the priests who could not find their genealogical records? What did the Tirshatha restrict them from doing?
answer: The priests who could not find their genealogical records were desecrated from the priesthood. The Tirshatha said that they should not be allowed to eat the holy food from the sacrifices until a priest stood with Urim and Thummim.

question: What was done concerning the priests who could not find their genealogical records? What did the Tirshatha restrict them from doing?
answer: The priests who could not find their genealogical records were desecrated from the priesthood. The Tirshatha said they should not be allowed to eat the priest’s share of food from the sacrifices.

question: When might the priests who could not prove their genealogy be included in the priesthood again?
answer: They might be included when there was a priest to stand with Urim and Thummim.

question: How many people were counted in the enrollment of the assembly?
answer: The whole assembly was counted to be 42,360 people.

question: Who gave gifts for the work?
answer: Some of the heads of ancestors’ families gave gifts, as did both the Tirshatha and the rest of the people.

question: When did the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and people live in their cities?
answer: They lived in their cities by the seventh month.

question: Why did the people gather together on the first day of the seventh month, and every day until the end of the feast?
answer: The people gathered together to listen to the book of the law.

question: Who gathered together to listen to the book of the law?
answer: Men, women, and anyone who could understand gathered to listen to it.

question: Why did the people gather together on the first day of the seventh month, and every day until the end of the feast?
answer: The people gathered together to listen to the book of the law of Moses.

question: Who read from the book of the law?
answer: Ezra and the Levites read from the book of the law.

question: Who read from the book of the law?
answer: Ezra and the Levites read from the book of the law.

question: Why did the Levites read carefully and set the interpretation of the book of the law?
answer: They did those things so that the people could understand the reading.

question: Why did Nehemiah, Ezra, and the Levites command all of the people to celebrate with great joy and not to mourn, weep, or grieve?
answer: They commanded the people to celebrate and not to mourn, weep, or grieve because the day was holy to Yahweh their God and because the joy of Yahweh was their strength.

question: What insight did the leaders of the ancestors’ families, the priests, and the Levites gain when they came together to learn from Ezra?
answer: They learned that Yahweh had commanded the people of Israel to live in tents during the festival of the seventh month.

question: Where did the people make their huts to celebrate the festival?
answer: The people made their huts on their own roofs, in their courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, in the open place by the Water Gate, and in the square at the Gate of Ephraim.

question: Where did the people make their huts to celebrate the feast?
answer: The people made their huts on their own roofs, in their courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, in the open place by the Water Gate, and in the square at the Gate of Ephraim.

question: When was the last time the people of Israel had obeyed the command of Yahweh to celebrate the feast?
answer: The last time the feast had been celebrated was in the days of Joshua the son of Nun.

question: Why did the people gather together on the first day of the seventh month, and every day until the end of the feast?
answer: The people gathered together to listen to the book of the law.

question: In general, what were the people of Israel doing as they gathered together on the twenty-fourth day of the same month?
answer: The people of Israel were fasting, wearing sackcloth, and putting dust on their heads. The Israelites separated themselves from all the foreigners, and they stood and confessed their own sins and the sins of their ancestors.

question: What did the people say about Yahweh?
answer: The people said he alone was Yahweh. The people said that Yahweh had made the heavens, the heavens of the heavens, the earth, the seas, and all that was in them. The people said that Yahweh gave life to everything.

question: What else did the people say of Yahweh concerning Abram?
answer: The people said that Yahweh had chosen Abram, changed his name to Abraham, found his heart faithful, and made the covenant with him to give his descendants the land.

question: How did the people say that Yahweh kept his promise to them?
answer: The people told how Yahweh brought their forefathers out of Egypt, showed signs and wonders against Pharaoh and his people, and saved their forefathers at the Red Sea.

question: What did the people say that Yahweh did for the Israelites at the Red Sea?
answer: Yahweh parted the sea so they could pass through on dry ground, and then he brought the sea back onto those that were pursuing them.

question: What other ways did they say Yahweh took care of the Israelites?
answer: Yahweh led them by a pillar of cloud during the day and a pillar of fire during the night. Also, Yahweh gave them his ten commandments at Mount Sinai.

question: What else did the people say Yahweh provided to their forefathers?
answer: Yahweh made his holy Sabbath known to them, gave them bread from heaven, water from a rock, and told them to possess the land he had promised them.

question: How did the Israelites and their ancestors act toward God?
answer: The Israelites were disrespectful and stubborn. They refused to listen, rebelled, and appointed a leader to return them to their slavery.

question: Why did God not abandon the Israelites when they were disrespectful, stubborn, rebellious, and disobedient?
answer: God did not abandon the Israelites because he is a God who is full of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, and abounding in covenant faithfulness.

question: How did the people say God provided for their forefathers for forty years in the wilderness?
answer: Yahweh gave his good Spirit to instruct them. Yahweh gave them food and water; also, their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell.

question: How did the people say God provided for their forefathers for forty years in the wilderness?
answer: Yahweh gave his Spirit to instruct them. He provided food and water; their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.

question: What did the people say happened after their forefathers were in the wilderness?
answer: The people said that Yahweh multiplied their families, told them to go in and possess the land he had promised them, and subdued the Canaanites.

question: How did the Israelites live after taking possession of the land God had promised them?
answer: The Israelites took the land. They ate and were satisfied and grew fat. They reveled in God’s great goodness.

question: What did the people say Yahweh did to their forefathers and ancestors after they became disobedient and rebelled against him?
answer: Yahweh handed them over to their enemies, who made them suffer.

question: When the Israelites cried out to God, what did God do for them because of his great mercies?
answer: God rescued them from their enemies many times.

question: Why did the rich yield from the Israelite’s land go to the kings God had set over them?
answer: The rich yield of the land went to their kings because of the Israelite’s sins.

question: Why were the Israelites in great distress?
answer: The Israelites were in great distress because their kings ruled over their bodies and their livestock as the kings pleased.

question: What did the Israelites do because of their great distress?
answer: The Israelites made a firm covenant in writing with Yahweh.

question: Whose names were written on the sealed covenant?
answer: The names of the Israelites’ leader, Levites, and priests were written on the sealed covenant.

question: Who pledged themselves to the law of God that was given to Moses?
answer: Those that pledged themselves were the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nethinim, and all the others who bound themselves to God’s law.

question: What promises did they make to God?
answer: They promised not to give their daughters to or let their sons take daughters from the people from whom they had separated. They promised not to buy any goods on the Sabbath, or any holy day. They promised they would let their fields rest every seventh year.

question: What commands did they accept?
answer: They would give money, bread, grain, and provide for all the offerings and feasts each year for the service of the house of God.

question: Why did the priests, the Levites, and the people cast lots for the wood offering?
answer: This would select which family would bring the wood into the house of God at selected times each year.

question: What did they promise to bring to the house of Yahweh?
answer: They promised to bring the firstfruits of the harvests as well as the firstborn of their sons and their livestock.

question: What did they promise to bring to the house of Yahweh?
answer: They promised to bring the firstfruits of their harvests and the firstborn of their sons and their livestock.

question: Who had to be with the Levites when the Levites received the tithes?
answer: A priest who was a descendant of Aaron had to be with the Levites.

question: Where did the people of Israel and descendants of Levi bring the contributions of the harvest?
answer: They brought the contributions to the storerooms where the articles of the sanctuary were kept.

question: Who lived in the holy city of Jerusalem?
answer: The leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to see which one person out of ten people would live there.

question: Where were the remainder of Israel, the priests, and the Levites living?
answer: They were living in all the towns of Judah, on their own inherited property.

question: In what book were the descendants of Levi and their leaders of families recorded?
answer: They were recorded in the Book of the Events of Days until the days of Johanan.

question: Why did the people seek out the Levites at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem?
answer: The people brought the Levites to Jerusalem to perform the dedication ceremony.

question: What did the priests and Levites do for the celebration?
answer: The priests and Levites purified themselves, and then purified the people, the gates, and the wall.

question: Where did the leaders of Judah go on the day of celebration?
answer: The leaders went up to the top of the wall.

question: What were the two large choirs that Nehemiah appointed supposed to do?
answer: The two large choirs were supposed to give thanks.

question: Where did the first choir go?
answer: One choir went to the right on the wall toward the Dung Gate.

question: Who directed the singers?
answer: The singers sang with Jezrahiah as overseer.

question: Why did they offer great sacrifices that day, and rejoice?
answer: They offered great sacrifices that day, and rejoiced, because God had made them rejoice with great rejoicing.

question: Who was assigned to work the fields near the towns?
answer: The men who were appointed to be in charge of the storerooms were assigned to work the fields near the towns.

question: When did all Israel give the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers?
answer: In the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah, all Israel gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers.

question: Why should an Ammonite and a Moabite not come into the assembly of God, forever?
answer: An Ammonite and a Moabite should not come into the assembly of God forever because they had not come to the people of Israel with bread and water, but had hired Balaam to curse Israel.

question: What did Eliashib prepare for Tobiah?
answer: Eliashib prepared for Tobiah a large storeroom.

question: Where did Nehemiah go in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes?
answer: In the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, Nehemiah returned from Jerusalem to the king.

question: Why did Nehemiah throw all the household articles of Tobiah out of the storeroom?
answer: Nehemiah threw all the household articles of Tobiah out of the storeroom because Nehemiah thought it was very wrong for Tobiah to be staying there.

question: Why did the Levites and singers hurry to leave the temple?
answer: Because the people were no longer faithfully supporting God’s work by giving portions to the Levites, and therefore the Levites left the temple as did the singers.

question: Who was counted as trustworthy?
answer: Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, Pedaiah, and Hanan were counted as trustworthy.

question: When were people in Judah treading winepresses?
answer: People in Judah were treading winepresses on the Sabbath.

question: What did men from Tyre do on the Sabbath?
answer: Men from Tyre brought in fish and all kinds of goods, and they sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah and in the city.

question: How did Nehemiah prevent people from coming into Jerusalem on the Sabbath?
answer: As soon as it became dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded that the doors be shut and that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. He stationed some of his servants at the gates so no load could be brought in on the Sabbath day.

question: Who came and guarded the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day?
answer: The Levites came and guarded the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day.

question: What did half the children speak?
answer: Half the children spoke the language of Ashdod, and they could not speak the language of Judah, but only the language of one of the other peoples.

question: How did Nehemiah confront the Jews who married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab?
answer: Nehemiah confronted them, and he cursed them, and he hit some of them and pulled out their hair.

question: How did Nehemiah want God to remember him?
answer: Nehemiah wanted God to remember him for good.

question: For what purpose did Yahweh send an ambassador among the nations?
answer: Yahweh sent an ambassador among the nations to cause the nations to rise up for battle against Edom.

question: What was one of the sins of the Edomites?
answer: The Edomites had pride in their hearts and believed that they could not be brought down to the ground.

question: Who will deceive and prevail against Edom?
answer: The men who had an alliance of peace with Edom will deceive and prevail against Edom.

question: Why will Edom be covered with shame and cut off forever?
answer: Edom will be covered with shame and cut off forever because of the violence Edom did to his brother Jacob.

question: What happened on the day that Edom stood aloof from Jacob?

question: What do the precepts of Yahweh do?

question: What does the commandment of Yahweh do?
answer: The commandment of Yahweh shows them how he wants them to behave.

question: How do the judgments of Yahweh compare to gold?

question: What do the judgments of Yahweh do for the servant?
answer: By them the servant is warned, and there is great reward in keeping them.

question: From what does David ask Yahweh to acquit him?
answer: He asks Yahweh to acquit him from his hidden faults.

question: What does David want to be acceptable to Yahweh?
answer: David wants the words of his mouth and the meditation of his heart to be acceptable to Yahweh.

question: What does the psalmist pray that Yahweh will do for the king in his time of trouble?

question: What does David want Yahweh to remember and accept?

question: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to grant the king?

question: In what does David say they will rejoice?

question: Who does David say that Yahweh will rescue?

question: In what do other people trust?

question: What do David and his people do instead of trusting in chariots or horses?

question: What does the psalmist say happens to enemies compared to his own people?

question: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do at the end of the psalm?

question: In what does the king rejoice?

question: What has Yahweh done for the king?

question: What did Yahweh give the king after the king asked for it?

question: Why is the king’s glory great?

question: What has Yahweh bestowed upon the king?

question: Why will the king not be shaken?

question: What will Yahweh’s hand find?

question: What will Yahweh do to the offspring of his enemies?

question: Why will the plot of Yahweh’s enemies not succeed?

question: How will the people exalt Yahweh?
answer: They will sing and praise his power.

question: What is David asking God?

question: What does David do in the daytime and at night?
answer: David cries out in the daytime, and at night David is not silent.

question: How does David refer to God?
answer: David refers to God as holy, sitting as king with the praises of Israel.

question: What did David’s ancestors do and how did God respond?
answer: They trusted in God, he rescued them, and they were not disappointed.

question: How does David describe himself?

question: What do the people that taunt and mock David say to him?
answer: They say that he trusts in Yahweh and that Yahweh should rescue him since Yahweh delights in him.

question: How long has David trusted God?
answer: David trusted Yahweh when he was on his mother’s breasts and since he was in his mother’s womb.

question: What is David asking God to do for him?
answer: He is asking God to not be far away from him because trouble is near and there is no one to help.

question: What is surrounding David like a roaring lion?
answer: His enemies, like many strong bulls of Bashan, surround him, and they are opening their mouths wide against him like a roaring lion.

question: How does David describe himself?

question: What has surrounded David and encircled him?

question: What was done to the garments and the clothes?
answer: The garments were divided and lots were cast for the clothes.

question: What does David request of Yahweh?
answer: He requests that Yahweh not be far away and hurry to help him.

question: From what does David want to be rescued and saved?
answer: He wants his life delivered from the sword, rescued from the hand of the dog, and saved from the mouth of the lion and the horns of wild oxen.

question: What will David declare to his brothers, and where will he praise Yahweh?
answer: He will declare Yahweh’s name to his brothers and praise him in the midst of the assembly.

question: Who should praise, honor, and stand in awe of Yahweh?
answer: All who fear Yahweh, all descendants of Jacob, and all descendants of Israel should praise, honor, and stand in awe of him.

question: When did Yahweh hear the afflicted one?
answer: He heard the afflicted one when he cried to him.

question: Where will David praise and fulfill his vows?
answer: He will praise Yahweh in the great assembly and fulfill his vows before those who fear Yahweh.

question: Who will eat, be satisfied, and praise Yahweh?
answer: The poor will eat and be satisfied, and those who seek Yahweh will praise him.

question: What will all the peoples of the earth and what will the families of the nations do?
answer: The peoples of the earth will remember and turn to Yahweh and all the families of the nations will bow down before him.

question: Over what does Yahweh rule?
answer: Yahweh rules over the nations.

question: Who will bow before Yahweh?
answer: Both the wealthy of the earth and those who are dying and cannot preserve their own lives will bow before him.

question: What will future generations do?
answer: They will come and declare to a people not yet born what Yahweh has done.

question: Who is David’s shepherd?
answer: David’s shepherd is Yahweh.

question: Where does Yahweh make David lie down?
answer: Yahweh makes David lie down in green pastures.

question: Where does Yahweh lead David?
answer: Yahweh leads David beside tranquil water.

question: What does Yahweh restore?
answer: Yahweh restores David’s soul.

question: Where does Yahweh guide David?
answer: Yahweh guides David along right paths.

question: When David walks through the valley of deep darkness, who is with him?
answer: Yahweh is with David.

question: What does Yahweh prepare before David?
answer: Yahweh prepares a table in the presence of David’s enemies.

question: What does Yahweh anoint?
answer: Yahweh anoints David’s head with oil.

question: What will pursue David all the days of his life?
answer: Goodness and covenant faithfulness will pursue David.

question: Where will David live all the days of his life?
answer: David will live in the house of Yahweh for a very long time.

question: What does the psalmist say belongs to Yahweh?
answer: The earth and its fullness belong to Yahweh, along with the world and everyone who lives in it, because he founded it upon the seas and established it upon the rivers.

question: Who will ascend the mountain of Yahweh and stand in his holy place?
answer: Those who have clean hands and a pure heart, who have not lifted up their soul to what is false and have not sworn deceitfully, will ascend Yahweh’s mountain and stand in his holy place.

question: What will those who seek Yahweh receive?
answer: Those who seek Yahweh and seek his face will receive a blessing and righteousness from the God of their salvation.

question: Why are the gates to be lifted up?
answer: So that the King of glory may come in.

question: Who is the King of glory?
answer: Yahweh is the King of glory. He is strong and mighty in battle, and he commands armies.

question: For what does David ask God?
answer: David asks God to not let him be shamed, and to not let his enemies rejoice over him.

question: What does David ask Yahweh to teach him?
answer: David asks Yahweh to make known to him Yahweh’s ways and paths, and to lead him in Yahweh’s truth.

question: What does David ask Yahweh to remember?
answer: David asks Yahweh to remember his compassion and covenant faithfulness, but not to remember the sins of David’s youth or his transgressions.

question: What does Yahweh do because he is good and upright?
answer: He teaches the sinful in the way, leads the humble in justice, and teaches the humble his way.

question: What are all the paths of Yahweh?
answer: They are covenant love and faithfulness for those who keep his covenant and his testimonies.

question: Why does David ask Yahweh to forgive his iniquity?
answer: David asks Yahweh to forgive his iniquity for the sake of Yahweh’s name.

question: What will Yahweh do for the man who fears Yahweh?
answer: Yahweh will teach him in the way he is to choose, his life will remain in prosperity, and his descendants will inherit the land.

question: What does Yahweh share with those who fear him?

question: Why does David continually keep his eyes on Yahweh?
answer: Because Yahweh will rescue David when his enemies attempt to hurt him.

question: When David is alone and afflicted, what does he request of Yahweh?

question: When the troubles of David’s heart are enlarged, what does he ask of Yahweh?
answer: David asks Yahweh to bring him out of his distresses, to see his affliction and his trouble and forgive all of his sins, and to see his enemies who are many and who hate him with violent hatred.

question: Why does David ask Yahweh to not let him be shamed?
answer: Because David takes refuge in Yahweh.

question: From what does David ask God to redeem Israel?
answer: He asks God to redeem Israel from all of his troubles.

question: How does David say that he has walked?
answer: David says he has walked with integrity and has trusted in Yahweh without wavering.

question: What does David ask Yahweh to examine and test?
answer: He asks Yahweh to test the purity of his inner parts and heart.

question: What is before David’s eyes?
answer: Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness is before David’s eyes.

question: With whom does David not associate or mingle?
answer: David does not associate with deceitful people or mingle with dishonest people.

question: What does David hate?
answer: David hates gathering with evil people.

question: With whom does David say he will not sit?
answer: David says he will not sit with the wicked.

question: What does David do as he goes around Yahweh’s altar?
answer: He sings songs of thanksgiving and recounts all of Yahweh’s wonderful acts.

question: How does David feel about the place where Yahweh lives?
answer: He loves the place where Yahweh lives and his glory appears.

question: What does David ask Yahweh not to do?
answer: David asks Yahweh not to gather his soul with the sinful or his life with men of blood.

question: How does David say that he will walk?
answer: David says that he will walk in integrity.

question: Where does David’s foot stand and where will he bless Yahweh?
answer: His foot stands on level ground and he will bless Yahweh among the assemblies.

question: Why should David not fear anyone?
answer: David should not fear anyone since Yahweh is his light, his salvation, and the refuge of his life.

question: What happened when evildoers advanced against David?
answer: His enemies and those who were hostile to him stumbled and fell.

question: In what situations will David not fear but rather remain confident?
answer: His heart will not fear even though an army encamps against him and war rises up against him.

question: What has David asked of Yahweh?
answer: David has asked that he may dwell in the house of Yahweh all the days of his life, to look upon the beauty of Yahweh, and to inquire in his temple.

question: What will Yahweh do for David in the day of trouble?
answer: Yahweh will protect him in his tabernacle and keep him safe as if he were setting him high upon a rock where David’s enemies cannot reach him.

question: How will David offer worship to Yahweh?
answer: David will offer sacrifices of joy, sing, and make music to Yahweh.

question: What does David ask Yahweh to do?
answer: David asks Yahweh to hear his voice, to be gracious to him, and to answer him.

question: What does David’s heart say to Yahweh?
answer: David’s heart says that he will seek Yahweh’s face.

question: What does David ask Yahweh not to do?
answer: David asks Yahweh not to hide his face from him, not to turn his servant away in anger, nor to abandon or leave him.

question: What does David say Yahweh will do even though his father and mother have left him?
answer: David says that Yahweh will care for him even though his father and mother have left him.

question: What does David ask Yahweh to do because of his enemies?
answer: David asks Yahweh to teach him Yahweh’s way and guide him so that he remains safe from his enemies.

question: Why does David ask Yahweh not to give him up to his adversaries?
answer: David asks this because false witnesses and violent accusers have risen against him.

question: What did David believe that helped him?
answer: David believed that he would see the goodness of Yahweh and trust him as long as he lived.

question: What does David encourage the people to do?
answer: David encourages the people to wait on Yahweh, to be strong, and to let their heart be courageous.

question: To whom does David cry out?
answer: David cries out to Yahweh, his rock.

question: What will happen to David if Yahweh does not respond to him?
answer: David will join those who go down to the grave.

question: Who does David want to hear the sound of his pleading?
answer: David wants Yahweh to hear the sound of his pleading.

question: What does David ask Yahweh not to do?
answer: David asks Yahweh not to drag him away with the wicked.

question: What does David ask Yahweh to give the wicked?
answer: David asks Yahweh to give them what their deeds deserve and to repay them for their evil deeds.

question: What do the wicked not give heed to?
answer: The wicked do not give heed to the works of Yahweh or the action of his hands.

question: What has Yahweh heard?
answer: Yahweh has heard the sound of David’s pleading.

question: Who is David’s strength and shield?
answer: Yahweh is David’s strength and shield.

question: In whom does David’s heart trust?
answer: David’s heart trusts in Yahweh and greatly rejoices.

question: Who is the strength of his people?
answer: Yahweh is the strength of his people.

question: Who is the saving refuge of his anointed one?
answer: Yahweh is the saving refuge of his anointed one.

question: Who does David want Yahweh to save and bless?
answer: David wants Yahweh to save his people and bless his inheritance.

question: Who does David say should ascribe glory and strength to Yahweh?
answer: David says the sons of God should ascribe glory and strength to Yahweh.

question: To what does David compare the voice of Yahweh?
answer: David compares the voice of Yahweh to thunder over the waters.

question: What does Yahweh break?
answer: Yahweh breaks the cedars of Lebanon.

question: What does Yahweh shake?
answer: Yahweh shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.

question: What do the people in Yahweh’s temple declare?
answer: Everyone in his temple declares Yahweh’s glory.

question: How long does Yahweh sit as king?
answer: Yahweh sits as king forever.

question: What two things will Yahweh give his people?
answer: Yahweh will give strength to his people and will bless his people with peace.

question: Why does David extol Yahweh?
answer: He extols Yahweh because Yahweh has drawn him up and has not allowed David’s enemies to rejoice over him.

question: What did Yahweh do when David cried for help?
answer: Yahweh healed David.

question: In what way did Yahweh restore David?
answer: Yahweh caused David to get well and restored him when he was about to die.

question: What are the faithful told to do in remembrance of Yahweh’s holiness?

question: How long does Yahweh’s anger and favor last?

question: What happens after weeping comes for a night?
answer: Joy comes in the morning.

question: What did David say when his life was going well?
answer: David said that he would never be shaken.

question: What happened to David when Yahweh hid his face?
answer: When Yahweh hid his face, David was dismayed.

question: What did David seek from the Lord?
answer: David sought favor from the Lord.

question: What things is David asking Yahweh to do for him?
answer: David is asking Yahweh to hear him, to be gracious to him, and to be his helper.

question: What has Yahweh done for David?
answer: Yahweh has turned David’s mourning into dancing, causing him to change from being sad to being joyful.

question: What does David say his glory will do?
answer: David’s glory will sing praise to Yahweh and not be silent. He will give thanks to Yahweh his God forever.

question: What does David ask Yahweh to become for him?
answer: He asks Yahweh to be his rocky summit of refuge and a stronghold to save him.

question: In whom does David take refuge?
answer: David takes refuge in Yahweh.

question: Why does Yahweh lead and guide David?
answer: Yahweh leads and guides David for the sake of his own name.

question: What does David believe that Yahweh will protect him from?
answer: Yahweh will rescue him from the evil plans his enemies have made to hurt him.

question: Into what does David commit his spirit?
answer: David puts himself into the care of Yahweh.

question: Who does David hate?
answer: He hates those who keep idols of worthlessness.

question: Why will David be glad and rejoice in Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness?
answer: David will be glad and rejoice because Yahweh has seen his affliction and known the troubles of his soul.

question: Where has Yahweh set David’s feet?
answer: Yahweh has set David’s feet in an open space.

question: Why does David ask Yahweh to be gracious to him?
answer: David is in distress and his eye has wasted away from grief.

question: Why does David’s strength fail and his bones waste away?
answer: His strength fails and his bones waste away because of his iniquity.

question: How do people respond to David?
answer: His enemies treat him with contempt, his neighbors are especially horrified by him, and those who see him outside flee from him.

question: To what does David compare himself?
answer: David says he is as forgotten as a dead man whom no one thinks about, and that he is like a broken vessel.

question: Why is David so troubled?
answer: He hears the whispering of many and there is terror on every side, as his enemies conspire together to take his life.

question: From whom does David ask God to rescue him?

question: What does David ask God to do for his servant?

question: What does David ask God not to let happen to him?
answer: David asks Yahweh not to let him have shame.

question: Why should lying lips be silenced?
answer: They speak arrogant and contemptuous things against the righteous.

question: For whom is God’s goodness stored up?
answer: Yahweh’s goodness is stored up for those who fear him.

question: From what does Yahweh protect those who revere him?
answer: He protects them from the evil plots of the enemies who accuse them.

question: Why is Yahweh to be blessed?

question: What did Yahweh do for David even though David said that he was cut off from God’s eyes?
